We benchmark multiple decoding models on hierarchical semantic classification at both fine-grained and coarse-grained levels, meta-feature decoding tasks covering motion, color, object number, face, and human presence, and a state-decoding task that discriminates perception from recall. Within-subject validation results show numerically similar performance for several model--task combinations, alongside higher perception accuracy in two coarse-grained comparisons after multiple-comparison correction. In contrast, perception and recall are highly separable at the state level under the present validation protocol. State accuracy remains high after alpha-band ablation, although this does not exclude ocular or other task-related contributions.

title: BenCoDiC: A Large-Scale Contextual Cyberbullying Corpus for Bengali Political News Discourse FULL VERSION
abstract: Cyberbullying is a growing concern in online communities, yet existing Bengali corpora remain limited in contextual information, annotation transparency, scale, accessibility, and support for multidimensional analysis, thereby hindering robust detection and comprehensive study of harasser behaviors and networks. To address these gaps, we introduce the Bengali Contextual and Diverse Cyberbullying (\textit{BenCoDiC}) corpus, a publicly available contextual cyberbullying resource for Bengali political news discourse comprising 50,250 textual instances collected from 100 YouTube videos and their associated discussions. The corpus preserves caption--comment--reply relationships and is organized through a nine-dimensional star schema covering users, videos, textual content, context, time, engagement, political parties, target identities, and language categories. Five AI chatbots were initially evaluated for annotation but did not meet the predefined reliability criterion. Consequently, a two-tier human annotation process with expert verification was adopted, achieving Fleiss' $κ=0.86$ and Krippendorff's $α=0.86$. Statistical analyses characterize the corpus, while transformer-based experiments show that incorporating conversational context yields modest but consistent improvements over isolated-text classification. \textit{BenCoDiC} supports context-aware cyberbullying detection and perpetrator-oriented behavioral and network analysis. The corpus is available at https://github.com/bencodic/BenCoDiC-Corpus.

title: GuidedNav: Shaping Vision-Language Navigation Representations through Pre-action Attention and Spatial Guidance
abstract: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) requires an agent to track progress through an extended instruction, identify landmarks relevant to its current objective, and understand the surrounding spatial structure to act. End-to-end navigation policies typically rely on action supervision to implicitly learn these capabilities. Without explicit guidance on the evidence underlying each decision, however, policies can overfit to correlations predictive of training actions rather than learn the task-relevant grounding and geometry needed for generalization. Our insight is to guide the representations that connect instructions to actions: identifying what remains to be done determines which visual evidence matters, while understanding the geometry around that evidence informs how to move. We introduce GuidedNav, a unified framework that explicitly shapes these representations through training-time guidance. Subtask and landmark guidance steer native pre-action attention toward the active instruction segment and relevant visual regions, grounding action prediction in the current objective. Spatial guidance aligns the policy's internal representations with geometric features that capture long-horizon context and local spatial structure. Together, these objectives strengthen navigation capabilities while avoiding the inference overhead of intermediate textual reasoning and online geometric encoding. We also introduce Guided-R2R and Guided-RxR, two annotation-enriched navigation datasets that support more interpretable VLN research. GuidedNav establishes state-of-the-art performance among the compared monocular RGB policies, improving success rates by 8.1% and 13.1% relative to the strongest prior results on R2R-CE and RxR-CE val-unseen, respectively, while achieving faster inference. Extensive experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness and real-world transferability of our approach.

title: Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality
abstract: A solid understanding of the predictive success of deep neural networks (DNNs) remains elusive. For example, while many data-dependent metrics exist that seek to predict model quality of DNNs, these metrics may be expensive to compute for large datasets and/or may be impossible to compute when training datasets are not released. A practical and effective predictor of model quality involves analyzing DNN weight matrices, as prior work has established that heavy-tailed spectral distributions in trained weight matrices can be strongly predictive of model quality. However, such metrics lack a rigorous statistical justification. In this work, we aim to understand why these metrics perform well, from a statistical perspective. To do so, we employ a probabilistic framework to derive the marginal likelihood for a DNN, evaluated using only the final layer weights. Across large-scale convolutional DNNs and LLMs, we find that this marginal likelihood predicts model quality. To understand the role heavy-tailed spectra play in predictive performance, we derive the limiting log-marginal likelihood for spectra that follow the (heavy-tailed) High-Temperature Marchenko-Pastur (HTMP) distribution. We show that this limiting quantity is convex in a heaviness parameter, and we derive an optimal heaviness that empirically predicts over-fitting for large-scale DNNs.

title: Electron- and hole-doped superconductivity in two-dimensional electride ZrX$_2$ (X = Cl, Br, I)
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) superconducting systems have recently emerged as a frontier in condensed matter physics, driven by their unique physical properties and potential applications. Using first-principles calculations, we show that monolayer ZrX$_2$ (X = Cl, Br, I), which is a family of 2D semiconducting electrides, hosts phonon-mediated superconductivity under both electron and hole dopings. Electron doping in ZrX$_{2}$ can achieve high superconducting transition temperatures at very low concentrations, with ZrBr$_2$ reaching $T_c = 30.0$ K at 0.01 \textit{e}/f.u., followed by ZrCl$_2$ (22.5 K at 0.05 \textit{e}/f.u.) and ZrI$_2$ (18.1 K at 0.01 \textit{e}/f.u.), for which the high $T_c$ originates from the flat conduction band minimum, with Van Hove singularities nearby enhancing the density of states. In contrast, hole doping requires higher concentrations (0.2--0.25 \textit{h}/f.u.) to activate superconductivity, yielding $T_c \sim 2$ K, and approaches a magnetic instability at elevated doping levels. By comparing with InSe and LaBr$_2$, we identify the spatial location and orbital character of excess electrons as key factors determining the strength of hole-doped superconductivity and the nature of competing orders. These findings establish monolayer ZrX$_2$ as a platform for bipolar superconductivity in a 2D electride and provide insights into flat-band engineering for high-$T_c$ superconductors.

title: Characterizing CPU-GPU Memory Sharing over Unified Memory Architecture
abstract: Unified Memory Architecture (UMA) enables the CPU and GPU to share a single physical memory. However, its complexity and opacity often drive applications back to inefficient copying or to incorrect direct access that sacrifices performance or even correctness. This paper presents a comprehensive study of CPU-GPU memory sharing on UMA, covering correctness and performance across data-plane transmission and control-plane coordination on four platforms. It yields four findings that guide libumsh, a portable library that delivers correct and efficient memory sharing across platforms and extends to emerging ones (e.g., NVIDIA DGX Spark). Applied to nine real-world systems, libumsh reduces data-plane time by 16-75% and control-plane overhead by 7-90%.

title: MLP-Initialized Reinforcement Learning for Exit Timing in SPX Short-Straddle Portfolios
abstract: This paper studies exit timing for SPX short-straddle portfolios using a two-stage supervised and reinforcement-learning framework. Historical episodes first generate ex-post optimal hold/exit labels for training a multilayer perceptron (MLP) using only contemporaneously available state variables at deployment. The trained MLP then initializes reinforcement-learning actors that are fine-tuned with a risk-aware trading reward. Out-of-sample evaluation over 2024-2026 shows that the supervised MLP substantially outperforms passive holding and representative fixed-time and profit-and-loss-based exit rules. Across seven independent seeds, MLP-initialized Actor-Critic averages 37.54% cumulative return and a Sharpe ratio of 1.705, compared with 35.01% and 1.651 for the supervised MLP. Actor-Critic trained from scratch averages only 0.18% return. These findings show that oracle-guided supervised learning provides a stable foundation for reward-based policy fine-tuning in a sparse and path-dependent option-exit problem.

title: Star Cluster Ecology VIII. -- Dynamically Forming S-Type and $α$Centauri-like Systems
abstract: Aims: To analyse the impact of dynamically formed binaries emerging naturally from various star cluster environments on already established planetary systems. Methods: Numerical simulations replicating the star-forming region NGC 1333 are conducted. We consider three models, each using identical cluster realisations and simulation parameters. The cluster itself is initially sub-virial and fractally distributed. Model~A assumes planetary systems are initially in mean motion resonance. In Model~B, the same planetary systems are moved out of resonance, but remain intrinsically stable. Finally, Model~C removes all planets from the simulation. Ten independent realisations are integrated per model until 30 Myr. Results: Dynamically formed binaries emerge at similar rates across models, indicating planets play little role in their formation. We also find a higher production rate of wide binaries compared to previous numerical studies which we attribute to the sub-virial and sub-clustered initial conditions. S-type and binary S-type planetary systems naturally emerge in our simulations, while P-type systems are rare. For Model~A, the fraction of S-type or binary S-type systems is f_{\rm S}=0.02 and $f_{\rm Bin,\, S}=0.05, respectively. Rogue planets originating from a binary system are ejected with a substantially larger velocity than those around singletons. Planet-star collisions and planet capture events occur disproportionately within binary systems. Finally, several \alphaCentauri-like systems emerge in our simulations, suggesting that the nearest stellar system to the Sun may have a dynamical origin.

title: Locate, Judge, Read: Role-Specialized Tool Agents over a Knowledge-Point Index for Open-Domain Multimodal Document QA
abstract: Question answering over large heterogeneous document collections requires first finding the right passages and then reading them, yet current retrieval-augmented agents give one model both kinds of tools and let it schedule itself. We present KnowForge, a pipeline separated by job: a hybrid-retrieval knowledge-point index; a Locator agent that can only search; a code-scheduled bridge judge that forces the missing second hop; a typed, size-bounded evidence pool that merges every search's ranking; a Deep Reader agent that can only read text, images and tables; and a synthesizer with a format checker. With a self-hosted Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (3B active), KnowForge reaches F1 47.5 on the full open-domain M3DocVQA (2,441 questions, 3,368 PDFs), +11.0 over the published M3DocRAG system and +7.1 over one-shot retrieve-and-answer on the same index and model, and 53.5 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash. On MultiHop-RAG it reaches 73.5 accuracy, above the strongest published RAG and GraphRAG results (71.2); on the single-document MMLongBench-Doc it lifts the same model from 34.8 to 47.0, level with GPT-4o reading page images (46.3). Per-job ablations on the full benchmarks attribute the gain: the Deep Reader is worth 3.8, 9.8 and 0 points on the three corpora, tracking how visual each is; merging both agents into one with all tools and twice the rounds loses 1.9 F1 because it keeps searching instead of reading; a round-budget sweep shows a step at four Locator rounds and a plateau beyond; query latency scales with model calls rather than corpus size. We serve the three indexed benchmarks as read-only knowledge bases (free registration) and release all prompts and the runner code: https://github.com/metask-ai/knowforge-bench

title: Fast Gradient-Based Approximation of Continuous Dynamic Time Warping
abstract: Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) is a common choice for measuring the discrepancy between time series. It proceeds by finding an optimal warping between timestamps through dynamic programming, which can be slow and is not differentiable. Consequently, several variants have been proposed. Among them, Soft-DTW proposes a smooth formulation of DTW, amenable to gradient computation, while Continuous-DTW (CDTW) introduces a continuous formulation through parametrizable warping functions. Yet, computational costs remain high for both methods and impractical for large datasets in modern machine learning pipelines. This paper revisits CDTW in several ways. After establishing its differentiability under mild conditions, we introduce FastCDTW, which is an efficient approximate solver with two different computational strategies: an exact closed-form scheme for piecewise-linear warping functions, and an unbiased Monte Carlo estimator for smooth ones, such as implicit neural networks. Both strategies provide gradients with respect to the warping function and the input time series, and the resulting algorithm is GPU-friendly. We demonstrate its benefits through its integration into more complex learning problems, including time series averaging, classification and deep domain adaptation.

title: PCM: Programmable Congestion Management for Terabit RDMA NICs
abstract: Datacenter congestion control (CC) and load balancing (LB) evolve rapidly as workload demands change, but deployment depends on RDMA hardware and transport interfaces. Emerging programmable RDMA engines tie policy code to vendor APIs. Operators must therefore port each policy for every platform they deploy. We address this with PCM, a programming model that separates portable congestion management from platform integration on datacenter NICs. Developers write event-driven handlers that they can debug in simulation and reuse on real hardware. PCM exposes flow telemetry as signals and uses triggers to support per-event reactions and coarser responses to accumulated feedback. Vendors provide optimized backends that map signals and output controls to native NIC mechanisms with defined feedback and control semantics. We demonstrate PCM's expressivity by implementing eleven well-known datacenter CC and LB algorithms. We deploy PCM across four distinct datapaths: an Ultra Ethernet simulator, CPU-based UCCL, and on-NIC offloads on NVIDIA ConnectX-8 and Microsoft 1P. On CX-8, PCM-Swift achieves processing capacity equivalent to one reaction per three 4 KiB packets at 800 Gbit/s, using one-fifth of the NIC's hardware threads. In UCCL, it matches native Swift's 1.56 Tbit/s goodput with 64 KiB chunk-level control. PCM's design informed ongoing Ultra Ethernet work toward a portable congestion management interface.

title: Looking Ahead and Back: Anticipatory Generative Modeling for Road-Network Trajectories
abstract: Trajectory generation underpins urban applications such as traffic management and urban planning. Within road networks, vehicle movement along road segments is largely deterministic, whereas transitions at intersections are critical--multiple outgoing paths may appear equally plausible, yet they can lead to substantially different downstream routes. Existing generative methods such as diffusion models simulate location sequences and fail short of next transition selection, even producing trajectories that drift off the road network. To fill this gap, we advocate a fundamental shift: moving beyond location simulation toward behavior modeling on the road network. In this paper, we revisit trajectory generation through the lens of generative route planning, and introduce a new graph-constrained generative paradigm, Anticipatory Generative Modeling, which resolves next transition selection by incorporating the Anticipation of how the future route may unfold toward the destination. Concretely, we propose a novel generative model named Foresight that formulates a probabilistic model for an "anticipate--select--update--re-anticipate" loop that enables longer-term foresight while continuing sequential generation along the historical trajectory. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Foresight wins state-of-the-art baselines.

title: DP-MIND: Differentially private memory-guided Long context Inference
abstract: LLM-as-a-Service has become a dominant paradigm for accessing large language models without requiring local deployment. However, the process raises severe privacy concerns when user queries may include sensitive or confidential contexts. Differential privacy (DP) provides a principled approach to protecting such inputs, but existing DP inference methods are primarily designed for short- or moderate-context settings and struggle with million-token-scale inputs due to limited context capacity and severe utility degradation under DP perturbation. In this paper, we propose DP-MIND, a memory-guided framework that scales differentially private inference to million-token contexts. DP-MIND enables private long-context inference by locally perturbing the input and processing it chunk by chunk with a compact memory that preserves task-relevant information across the sequence. To make this memory robust to DP noise, we optimize the memory construction policy directly on perturbed inputs using reinforcement learning, guided by both final answer correctness and memory consistency. We further recover perturbation-corrupted answer spans through a local denoising module without exposing the original context to the external model. We provide theoretical privacy analysis of DP-MIND and further conduct extensive empirical analysis across multiple long-context benchmarks with context lengths up to the million-token scale, demonstrating that DP-MIND consistently outperforms existing DP and long-context inference baselines in both scalability and utility.

title: The Limits of Manipulation within Personalized Incentive Policies
abstract: Demand management policies aim to shift individual behavior toward sustainable choices (e.g., goods, transport modes). Personalized incentive policies tailor subsidies to agents' needs and constraints, but personalization also exposes the regulator to agents' strategic manipulative behavior. The extent to which agents can profitably manipulate such policies remains poorly understood, which limits their applicability. This paper establishes analytically the conditions under which manipulation benefits the agent. We formalize a Stackelberg game in which an agent may simulate a different profile to extract higher incentives from a regulator. Previous work typically assumes that the regulator would instantaneously classify agents into the simulated user profile. In contrast, we explicitly model the regulator's process of learning the agent profile, based on observed past behavior. This makes manipulation harder, since it forces the agent to consistently behave according to a simulated profile, thus renouncing following their true preferences. Manipulative agents thus incur a Cost of Manipulation, which has typically been neglected. By accounting for it, we get a counterintuitive finding: although classification uncertainty reduces personalization accuracy, it may benefit the regulator by deterring manipulation. We establish an upper bound on the agent's gain from manipulation, which becomes stricter as profiles become harder to distinguish for the regulator. Simulations on the London Passenger Mode Choice dataset illustrate this deterrence effect. The framework can therefore be used to stress-test the robustness of personalized incentive policies before deployment.

title: Neurograf v1: An End-to-End Romanian-First Language Model Family
abstract: We present Neurograf v1, an experimental end-to-end Romanian-first language-model pipeline developed to investigate the feasibility of training language models from scratch for a lower-resource European language. The pipeline comprises RoSfera, a 635 GB Romanian corpus containing 175.7 million documents; an 80k byte-level BPE tokenizer; five decoder-only models ranging from 160M to 6B parameters, trained on 131 billion tokens; three instruction-tuned assistants; and two contrastively trained embedding models. Training and evaluation were conducted using computing infrastructure at ELI-NP/IFIN-HH. The model family exhibits consistent scaling of validation loss and increasing Romanian factual and cultural knowledge with model size. On the 1,000-question WWTBM benchmark, Neurograf-6B achieves 69.89% accuracy on Romanian-context questions, while Neurograf-3.2B reaches 67.38%. Compute-optimal analysis yields a parameter-scaling exponent of approximately 0.423. Neurograf v1 serves as an experimental demonstrator rather than a production system. The study identifies practical challenges involving diacritic preservation, corpus quality, data composition, and tokenization efficiency, while demonstrating the feasibility of developing Romanian-first base models, instruction-following assistants, and semantic embedding models within a unified training pipeline.

title: Pulsed control of an entanglement-breaking index: thermal valleys, a certified valve, and its open-close asymmetry
abstract: The entanglement-breaking index of a channel is the number of self-compositions after which all entanglement with a reference system is destroyed. In a thermal qubit collision loop whose round is affine in the bath polarisation p, some circuits have thermal valleys: on an interior window of p the index falls below its infinite-temperature value. Rounds at different p compose exactly, so every schedule of polarisations defines a composite channel whose entanglement-breaking status can be certified in ball arithmetic. A gated search of 33 million random circuits finds no valley with contrast above about 3e-3, with an interior maximum near index 90, and yields six certified targets. At the reference target, held inside its window for 88 rounds, a centred excursion to p = 0.05 restores entanglement at exactly eight rounds: every shorter centred pulse certifiably fails, and so do the same eight rounds at the start. A 53-round pulse certifiably beats the static protocol, a depth-three valley is walked down its staircase by pulse duration, and a 1.2 per cent coherent tilt of the ancilla opens the switch at fixed population. Closing the switch costs 21 to 35 rounds. The asymmetry is not one of local rates, which agree to within about two per cent at matched circuit positions (certified). It is one of distance and response: closing must remove an entanglement margin 2.2 times larger, and while hot rounds added to a window hold act almost independently, window rounds added to a hot hold act collectively. Near the crossing, the lever of the log-margin is that of a linear approach to the entanglement-breaking boundary, with no free parameter. At the reference target, depolarising noise of about $4ν/n$ per round kills a signature of size $ν$ read after $n$ rounds: 1.3e-4 for the static signal, 6.5e-6 for the eight-round switch.

title: Stieltjes constants for Hurwitz-type L-series attached to periodic arithmetic functions
abstract: We investigate generalized Stieltjes constants attached to Hurwitz-type Dirichlet series of the form $$ L(s, f, x)=\sum_{n \geq 0} \frac{f(n)}{(n+x)^s} $$ where $f$ is a periodic arithmetic function and $x\in\mathbb C\backslash\{0,-1,-2,\dots\}.$ We prove that these series admit meromorphic continuation to the whole complex plane, with at most a simple pole at $s=1$. We further derive functional equations satisfied by $L(s,f,x).$ Our main result gives an explicit formulas of the Stieltjes constants $γ_n(f, x)$ appearing in the Laurent expansion at $s=1$. In particular, we obtain explicit evaluations in the case of rational $x$. As an application, we derive explicit closed-form expressions for the first three generalized Stieltjes constants associated with nonprincipal real primitive odd Dirichlet characters arising from quadratic fields. These expressions are given in terms of the class number of the corresponding quadratic number field. These results extend and unify recent work of Blagouchine and others on generalized Stieltjes constants and Hurwitz-type $L$-functions.

title: Qualitative-to-quantitative regularity for degenerate equations
abstract: We establish a principle that converts qualitative regularity into uniform interior estimates for degenerate equations. For the $p$-Laplace equation, $p>2$, we prove that local $C^{1,γ}$ regularity of every solution, without any uniform bound on the corresponding seminorms, implies uniform $C^{1,β}$ estimates for every $0<β<γ$. Thus, the optimal qualitative and quantitative gradient Hölder exponents coincide as suprema in every dimension. In the plane, this yields estimates controlled by the $L^p$ norm of the solution for every exponent below the sharp Iwaniec--Manfredi threshold. Applied to Xu's recent qualitative $C^{1,1/3}$ regularity for planar infinity-harmonic functions, we obtain uniform interior $C^{1,β}$ estimates for every $0<β<1/3$. For the nonlocal superconductivity equation $|Du|(-Δ)^s u=0$, with $1/2<s<1$, we prove that pointwise differentiability of all solutions with integrable tails implies uniform interior $C^{1,α}$ estimates for bounded solutions, for some $α>0$. The proofs combine compactness for shifted equations with an improvement-of-flatness iteration at variable scales.

title: A Ray-Traced Digital Twin for 5G NR Positioning with OpenAirInterface
abstract: Evaluating 5G positioning on a physical testbed ties every measurement to one propagation environment and one antenna layout, so any question about an alternative deployment requires a new field campaign. We present a ray-traced digital twin of the GEO-5G testbed at EURECOM that drives an unmodified OpenAirInterface (OAI) 5G stack with per-antenna channels computed by Sionna-RT over a 3D model of the site. The distributed gNB antennas are modelled as independent radio devices rather than as elements of a compact array, which preserves the per-antenna absolute delays on which time-difference-of-arrival (TDoA) positioning depends. With them preserved, the twin drives OAI's SRS-based UL-TDoA pipeline to metre-level accuracy consistent with that reported for the physical deployment. We then use the twin to answer a question the physical testbed cannot. Widening the carrier truncates the tail of the horizontal error distribution without improving a typical position, and leaves the vertical error untouched, because the latter is limited by the array geometry rather than by the measurement. That limit is predictable from the antenna coordinates alone, and a height-diverse layout reduces the RMS height error by a factor of four.

title: Strict Dirichlet Pólya Inequality for Simply Connected Planar Domains
abstract: We establish the strict Dirichlet Pólya inequality on every bounded simply connected planar domain. The proof uses a unitary boundary transport formulation of the Helmholtz equation and relates Dirichlet resonances to unitary eigenphase crossings through the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. An exact area identity yields the sharp Weyl coefficient, while a Ky Fan estimate leaves a strictly positive remainder in the counting estimate. The general case follows by conformal exhaustion.

title: Remarks on temperature-dependent Cahn--Hilliard equations
abstract: We recall several derivations of temperature-dependent Cahn-Hilliard equations. The resulting equations are systems of mixed order. For a suitable subclass of equations we discuss its local-in-time well-posedness based on $L^p$-maximal regularity theory. We also discuss stability of equilibria.

title: Representing the Non-dominated Set of Multi-objective Optimization Problems with Polyhedral Ordering Cones
abstract: In the literature, research on representing the non-dominated set has focused almost exclusively on multi-objective optimization problems with Pareto-dominance. However, general ordering cones are used to incorporate preferences of decision makers into the optimization process and to model other specific types of optimization problems, such as ordinal optimization problems. In this work, we consider several representation approaches based on representation relations in the context of multi-objective optimization problems with polyhedral ordering cones. Our main research question is whether existing theory and solution approaches developed for the Pareto case can be used to address the more general setting.

title: Structure-Aware Online Optimization of the Age of Information with Unknown System Statistics
abstract: Timely information dissemination is essential in modern communication systems, where low informational latency is critical for networked control, monitoring, and real-time decision-making. The Age of Information (AoI) has emerged as a fundamental metric for quantifying information freshness at the receiver. A key challenge in AoI optimization is selecting the update generation rate: infrequent updates lead to stale information, whereas overly frequent updates increase queueing delays. We develop a structure-aware, data-driven framework for adaptive AoI optimization modeled as single-server queues with unknown system statistics. Our key idea is to exploit analytical representations of the AoI gradient, which depend on a finite-dimensional collection of system quantities that can be estimated from observations collected during system operation. This reduces the online learning problem to estimating the quantities required by the gradient, rather than learning the AoI objective as a black box. We propose an online stochastic approximation algorithm that jointly estimates these quantities and optimizes the update generation rate. We prove almost sure convergence of the algorithm to the optimal update generation rate under mild regularity and moment conditions, despite the temporal dependence induced by the underlying queueing process. We demonstrate the framework in four representative incomplete-information settings, including FCFS queues with unknown service characteristics or hidden background traffic, a preemptive LCFS system with partial observations, and a generate-at-will system with threshold waiting.

title: Measurable Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting with Joint Region and Depth Supervision for Interactive Building Inspection
abstract: Image-based 3D reconstruction provides a scalable representation for building inspection and maintenance. However, photorealistic reconstruction alone does not fully provide the geometric measurability, semantic structure, and interactive information access required for engineering applications. This study proposes a measurable semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) framework with region and depth supervision for interactive building inspection from multi-view imagery. Mask-based region supervision suppresses irrelevant backgrounds and focuses optimization on target regions. Point-wise depth supervision guides Gaussian centers toward physical surfaces using reference geometry derived from multi-view stereo (MVS) point clouds, providing geometric anchors for measuring physical dimensions and areas. A semantic Gaussian field associates learnable class features with individual Gaussian primitives, enabling semantic rendering and component-level inspection. These capabilities are operationalized through AEC-SplatTwin, an interactive building inspection platform supporting real-time visualization, semantic analysis, quantitative measurement, and multimodal large language model (MLLM)-assisted interaction. On the synthetic UAV-inspection QuakeCity and smartphone-captured HKUPB datasets, the framework reduces Gaussian-center depth MAE by 58.1% and 86.8%, while its semantic field achieves mIoU values of 0.8529 and 0.8642. On HKUPB, the mean relative errors for height, width, and area measurements are 0.33%, 1.07%, and 0.60%. These results show that the proposed framework extends 3DGS beyond visual reconstruction into a measurable, semantically structured, and interactive engineering representation for building inspection.

title: Competence-Aware Orchestration for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have emerged as a promising paradigm for enhancing complex reasoning through role specialization and collaboration, yet a key challenge remains: how can collaboration be adapted to a backbone's competence on the current query? This problem matters because more collaboration is not always better--richer coordination may help on difficult cases, but it also incurs additional token cost and redundant interactions. We propose a two-stage competence-aware framework for automatic MAS orchestration. It first models the LLM backbone's task-conditioned competence for the current query, and then uses this signal to adapt role activation and the communication graph. Across six benchmarks, our method achieves an average score of 93.81%. Experiments with six LLM backbones of varying competence levels further show that our method adjusts collaboration according to the inferred competence: for higher-competence backbones, it improves average accuracy from 87.22 to 89.97 while reducing token cost by 36.26%; for lower-competence backbones, it yields a further average gain of 4.58 points over existing methods. The same trend also holds on unseen backbones.

title: VIGOR: Verifiable Industrial Geometry Optimization and Repair in Scene Programs
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate structured layouts and executable scene programs from natural-language instructions. However, executability does not imply engineering feasibility: an industrial scene program may execute successfully while its final state still violates coupled boundary, collision, clearance, aisle, or structural constraints. We identify this mismatch as the executability-engineering-feasibility gap, where locally plausible placements can remain globally infeasible because corrections to one device may introduce violations elsewhere. To make this gap measurable in a controlled setting, we construct an execution-grounded industrial scene-program dataset with 1,749 constructible scenarios, complete executable programs, and 94 final-state geometric checks per scenario. We further propose VIGOR, which combines supervised scene-program generation with execution-grounded verification and staged geometric refinement. Supervised fine-tuning establishes complete program generation, local projection resolves independently correctable violations, and joint conflict-graph repair coordinates residual multi-object conflicts while preserving structural relations. Experiments show that VIGOR achieves 96.86% Complete Feasibility and an Overall score of 91.20, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 10.42 points in Overall. These results show that, under controlled industrial layout conditions, reliable scene-program generation requires not only executable programs, but also explicit verification and coordinated resolution of coupled engineering constraints.

title: Extended Neighborhood Message Passing for Inference in Loopy Factor Graphs
abstract: Belief propagation (BP) is widely used for inference on probabilistic graphical models but often suffers from non-convergence and poor accuracy on loopy factor graphs, yielding inexact variance estimates in the Gaussian case. Generalized BP (GBP) improves accuracy but relies on manual design or application-specific heuristics for region-graph construction. We propose extended neighborhood message passing (ENMP), which automatically constructs extended neighborhoods of variable nodes from the bipartite factor graph topology, capturing loop-induced correlations without manual region design. The framework applies to general distributions on factor graphs with a tunable accuracy-complexity trade-off. In the exact regime, message updates converge to the unique fixed point of the ENMP equations in finitely many iterations, yielding exact marginals; in the approximate regime, ENMP provides approximate marginals. For Gaussian factor graphs, we derive closed-form update rules enabling exact variance estimation in the exact regime, addressing the long-standing inaccurate variance estimates of loopy Gaussian BP. We evaluate ENMP on densely loopy Gaussian factor graphs from power-grid benchmarks and on a discrete Ising factor graph. Results show accuracy improves with neighborhood size, with exact marginals achieved on several systems in both settings. On larger Gaussian systems, ENMP outperforms regularized Gaussian BP (sGaBP-m) in both mean and variance estimation accuracy.

title: Is the Number of Foreshocks Underestimated? The Role of Declustering Symmetry
abstract: The physical origin of foreshocks remains one of the major unresolved problems in statistical seismology. In bottom-up (BU) triggering models, foreshocks are interpreted as ordinary earthquakes that stochastically trigger a larger event through cascading interactions, as in the Epidemic-Type Aftershock Sequence (ETAS) model. In contrast, top-down (TD) models interpret foreshocks as manifestations of a preparatory process preceding the mainshock. This ambiguity has important implications not only for earthquake forecasting, but also for declustering itself, since the inferred number of foreshocks may depend on the assumed physical mechanism governing seismicity. Here we investigate the detectability of foreshocks using synthetic catalogues representing two limiting physical scenarios: purely bottom-up triggering and mixed preparatory-triggering dynamics. These cases are implemented through the ETAS and ETAFS models, respectively. We compare the classical nearest-neighbor (NN) declustering metric with a reverse nearest-neighbor metric (rNN) introduced here. While the standard NN metric scales the correlation metric to the magnitude of the earlier event, rNN scales it with the magnitude of the later event. We show that rNN is mathematically equivalent to applying the standard nearest-neighbor metric to the time-reversed catalog, establishing a direct symmetry between the two approaches. Our simulations reveal [...]

title: Les Misérables Dialogue: A film-based network representation of social communication
abstract: In this work, we revisit the classic Les Misérables benchmark network from the perspective of social communication. Using the 1998 film adaptation of the novel, we construct the publicly available Les Misérables Dialogue temporal text network, which explicitly distinguishes speakers, addressees, and other recipients of each utterance, along with its content and timing. Using the ten social dimensions model, we also derive multilayer network representations of the network, in which layers correspond to distinct relational dimensions. Beyond the network dataset, this work offers a general methodology for building similarly rich communication datasets from similar narrative sources.

title: Orbital transfer reveals material-selective structure in Rydberg excitons
abstract: Rydberg excitons in atomically thin semiconductors offer a sensitive view of dielectric screening and electronic structure. As their spectra become increasingly well resolved, a central question is how much material information an effective Hamiltonian can predict beyond the states used to determine it. Using the 1s, 2p and 2s levels to determine a scalar Rytova-Keldysh Hamiltonian, we test its transfer to the excluded 3p state. The transfer deviations have opposite signs: the observed 3p lies 7.38 meV below the prediction in MoSe2 and 5.58 meV above it in WS2; the opposite signs persist across the complete reported +/-2-sigma peak-error boxes. In a separate high-field-calibrated benchmark, RK removes 66.8% of the orbital error of a pure two-dimensional Coulomb reference, making the remaining state-selective deviations particularly informative. After separating gap and common-scale contributions, the residuals reveal distinct material-dependent orbital patterns and constrain simple multichannel descriptions. For WS2, the measured 2p/3p curvatures yield a parameter-fixed prediction, Q4p=+4.08 meV, for a future same-platform measurement. Together these results show how a well-performing spectral model can be tested for transferable physical information, with the next unmeasured state providing an independent experimental check.

title: Disformal Closure Selects 3D Scalar-Tensor Gravity without Local Bulk Modes
abstract: Three-dimensional Einstein gravity has no local degrees of freedom, yet retains rich global and black-hole physics. Adding a scalar normally spoils this. We show that closure of three-dimensional Horndeski gravity under disformal field redefinitions selects a square-root curvature interaction. A nonlinear analysis finds no local bulk modes on regular branches, while an independent Hamiltonian analysis confirms the result on the timelike-gradient branch. This extends the no-local-bulk-dynamics paradigm beyond pure Einstein gravity and motivates studying its boundary and global sectors.

title: Stability of composite waves consisting of a non-classical Liu shock and a rarefaction wave for a non-convex viscoelastic system
abstract: We investigate the time-asymptotic stability of composite waves consisting of a non-classical Liu shock and a rarefaction wave for non-convex viscoelastic system. By choosing delicate time-dependent shift functions to the viscous shock and suitable weight functions for the relative entropy, we succeed in proving the time-asymptotic stability of the composite of a viscous Liu shock and a rarefaction wave from two different characteristic families for the one-dimensional viscoelastic system with a cubic non-convex stress-strain relation by $a$-contraction method. Here the non-classical Liu shock can be either degenerate or non-degenerate, which can be seen as the system version of the scalar Oleinik shock. Note that both the shift and the weight functions are chosen quite differently in the two cases of nearly degenerate and fully non-degenerate. The paper represents the first time-asymptotic stability result for the composite waves consisting of both non-classical Liu shock and rarefaction wave from two different families for the non-convex physical system.

title: Quality, Not Just Outcome: A Structural Scoring Framework for Selecting Coding-Agent Trajectories for Supervised Fine-Tuning
abstract: Open coding agents are commonly trained through supervised fine-tuning on interaction trajectories whose final patches pass the benchmark test suite. However, this outcome-level filtering criterion ignores process quality: trajectories that eventually succeed may still contain inefficient interaction patterns such as repetitive file inspection, unstable tool usage, or delayed modification behavior, all of which become part of the imitation target. We propose TQS (Trajectory Quality Score), a structural scoring framework for coding-agent trajectories that operates directly on trajectory structure, requires no LLM judge, and runs in linear time. TQS characterizes trajectory quality through structural signals organized around structured convergence: information focus, intent--action alignment, and policy dynamics. Using 155,144 successful trajectories from a public open-license corpus, we rank trajectories by TQS and fine-tune coding agents on filtered subsets. Models trained on top-ranked trajectories consistently outperform those trained on random or bottom-ranked subsets on SWE-Bench-Verified. Our results suggest that process-level trajectory quality is an important factor in coding-agent supervision and that structural trajectory filtering provides an effective and scalable alternative to LLM-based data selection.

title: Continuous-wave AC magnetometry up to hundreds of megahertz using nitrogen-vacancy centers under a strong transverse magnetic field
abstract: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are promising quantum sensors for AC magnetic fields. However, conventional dynamical-decoupling-based magnetometry becomes technically demanding at high frequencies because of the requirement for increasingly short and high-power microwave pulses. This paper describes an AC magnetometry technique based on continuous-wave optically detected magnetic resonance (CW-ODMR) measurements, which enables the detection of signals in the hundred-MHz range. By applying a strong static magnetic field transverse to the NV axis, the energy separation between the relevant electron-spin states was tuned and resonantly coupled with the target radiofrequency (RF) magnetic field, thereby forming RF-dressed states. Unlike pulsed dynamical-decoupling schemes, this approach does not require high-power microwave pulse sequences. The key feature of our method is that the detectable frequency can be tuned by controlling the bias magnetic field strength. Using this methodology, we have experimentally achieved the frequency-tunable detection of AC magnetic fields from 14.4-632 MHz. The sensitivity was 0.558 uT/Hz^(0.5) at 14.4 MHz and 24.4 uT/Hz^(0.5) at 632 MHz. We characterized the field-dependent ODMR contrast and linewidth, and found that their degradation at large transverse fields is a important factor limiting the high-frequency sensitivity. These results establish a simple CW-ODMR approach for widely tunable RF magnetic-field sensing without high-power pulsed spin control.

title: From Glance to Focus: Mitigating Recognition Laziness in MLLMs for Fine-Grained Recognition
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) generally fall short of expectations in Fine-Grained Visual Recognition (FGVR), although they exhibit promising FGVR foundations, i.e., visual perception and broad category knowledge. Most existing studies seek to remedy this deficiency by adopting domain-specific post-training, at the risk of compromising generalization to unseen domains. Different from these efforts, in this paper, we revisit the FGVR mechanism underlying MLLMs from both the empirical and theoretical perspectives and uncover an inference-time phenomenon termed FGVR Laziness. In brief, FGVR Laziness refers to the insufficient association between visual cues and category concepts under certain candidate category lists and recognition guidance, leaving the FGVR foundations of MLLMs largely under-utilized. To mitigate FGVR Laziness, we propose Laziness-resIstant Visual rEcognition (LIVE), a training-free framework which jointly refines candidate lists and recognition guidance to elicit the latent FGVR capability of MLLMs. Specifically, LIVE first performs query-adaptive candidate inference to derive a compact yet reliable candidate list. Meanwhile, LIVE constructs category-specific FGVR skills by mining the intra-category characteristics and inter-category differences. Finally, LIVE selectively invokes detailed skill guidance according to recognition uncertainty and category confusion, shifting MLLM-based FGVR from a cursory glance to a focus on associating discriminative visual cues with category concepts. Extensive experiments on 13 benchmarks against 24 state-of-the-art methods spanning fine-grained category recognition, action recognition, and general category recognition, verify the effectiveness and generalizability of LIVE across different MLLM backbones. The code will be released upon acceptance.

title: X-ray absorption spectroscopic studies of oxygen-deficient double perovskite oxide NdBaCo$_2$O$_{5+δ}$ ($δ\sim 0.65$)
abstract: The degree of oxygen vacancy in A-site-doped layered double perovskite oxides can lead to anion vacancy ordering, which subsequently results in distinct superstructures. We have studied oxygen deficient double perovskite oxide, NdBaCo$2$O$_{5+δ}$ ($δ\sim$ 0.65), utilising X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy complemented by multiple scattering and first-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT+U). The present results establish a direct correlation between oxygen-vacancy distribution, magnetic inhomogeneity, and charge transport in layered cobaltates. Our investigations on the Co K, Ba, and Nd $L_{\mathrm{III}}$ edges suggest that the near-edge spectra, based on the number and shape of the spectral features, indicate the value of $δ$ for the compound under study lies closer to 0.75. The analysis of the Ba $L_{\mathrm{III}}$ edge spectrum confirms the +2 oxidation state for Ba ions. The Co K-edge near-edge spectra suggest the possibility of oxygen vacancies arising at the basal sites in addition to the apical sites. This is counterintuitive to the common understanding that oxygen vacancies usually occur at the apical sites, i.e., in the lanthanide (Nd) layer in these compounds. Such a distribution of oxygen vacancies naturally explains the Griffith phase and the conduction mechanism of variable range hopping observed in the compound. The vacancy distribution, when at the optimum level, can also bring about easier oxygen ion mobility and a more sensitive and faster oxygen sensor. We believe that our results will help in tailoring oxygen-ion mobility and enhancing oxygen-sensing performance.

title: How Anthropomorphic Attitudes Toward Agents Divide User Behavior, and How Design Should Change
abstract: Studies of conversational agents rely on interviews, surveys, lab tasks, or taxonomies. Whether anthropomorphic naming splits those patterns, and whether replies should change, lack field evidence. We report a field study of a desktop assistant (May-August 2026; n=257). Stance is an anthropomorphic assistant name (118 users; 45.9%). Behavior comes from a 128-unit sparse-autoencoder codebook, identity tags, and opening lexicons. Ranks differ by stance (Spearman rho=+0.249 vs. null mean +0.382; p=.0419). Teacher and tutoring identities covary with renaming, an introverted task-only orientation against it; renamers greet more and command less; confiding shows the codebook's largest gap. We revise the agent: greet and receive affect on relational openings, execute directly on tasking. In 1,744 judgments (n=129), renamers chose the revised reply far more often than default-name users on being treated as a person and having affect received, less robustly on willingness to continue, and neither judged it worse on task interference.

title: SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) for search agents often suffers from evidence fabrication, a failure mode where agents bypass external information ($E_{ext}$) and fabricate an incorrect answer. We argue that this fabrication arises from an over-reliance on unreliable internal knowledge ($E_{int}$) as shortcuts due to the inherent opacity of reasoning trajectories. To address this, we propose SOAR (SOurce-Aware Reinforcement learning), a paradigm that transforms monolithic reasoning into source-explicit trajectories. SOAR (i) disentangles $E_{ext}$ and $E_{int}$ into parallel, observable streams via a Source-Aware Workflow, and (ii) incorporates Source-Consistent Reward to guide the policy evolution. By making information-source attribution explicit, SOAR enables precise credit assignment between different knowledge streams. Evaluations show that SOAR outperforms baselines on 3B and 7B backbones by 7.3% and 5.4%, while reducing evidence fabrication by 74.8%. These confirm that SOAR significantly improves performance on knowledge-intensive benchmarks while effectively mitigating evidence fabrication, fostering more faithful and grounded reasoning with enhanced robustness.

title: Low-Latency Mapless ESDF Queries for MAV Reactive Collision Avoidance
abstract: Reactive collision avoidance in unknown, cluttered environments must perceive obstacles and correct motion within milliseconds. Existing methods rely on maps for high-rate collision queries, but their acceleration structures require pre- processing. That cost is amortized in long-horizon planning, where a map serves millions of queries; reactive planning, however, is a near-field, short-horizon problem with potentially only hundreds of queries per measurement, where building a map may not pay off. We propose a mapless, Graphics Processing Unit (GPU)-accelerated Euclidean Signed Distance Field (ESDF) query with negligible pre-processing that operates directly on posed depth images, with resolution set by pooling the image rather than by a voxel size. On an embedded GPU it is simultaneously more accurate and lower in total latency than every voxel-grid configuration we measured between 2 cm and 20 cm, at one to two orders of magnitude less memory at matched resolution. With our query integrated into a Model Predictive Controller (MPC), simulated runs in laser-scanned forests at up to 9 m/s collide in 0.4 % through dense branches, against 5.9 % with the best voxel grid and 5.5 % with the best mapless baseline at our resolution, whose failures we attribute to voxel resolution and total latency respectively. We deploy the system onboard at two forest sites and fly at commanded speeds of up to 4 m/s.

title: Morphology-based retrieval of local wave parameters and phase shifts in satellite-observed atmospheric disturbances
abstract: Currently available methods for processing atmospheric wave disturbances are often based on integral wavelet transform techniques, which efficiently estimate spectral data but are fundamentally limited by the uncertainty principle. To address this limitation, this work proposes a novel morphological approach based on partitioning spatial disturbance profiles into separate, well-defined wave segments. By focusing exclusively on the local waveform morphology of a central half-wave and its two adjacent out-of-phase counterparts, and taking the modified Morlet wavelet as a primary example of a model wave packet, we successfully reconstruct the complete set of local wave parameters directly from the amplitudes and positions of these three dominant half-waves. Consequently, the theory demonstrates good agreement with observations, confirming the high accuracy of the proposed waveform morphology approach in reconstructing the localized structure of atmospheric disturbances. When applied to evaluating the phase shift between different wave field components, the method reveals that this shift is a weighted combination of the classical monochromatic phase difference and a morphological one determined by the internal symmetry of the underlying wave packets. Although the classical factor yields the dominant contribution, the symmetry-related factor provides a moderate correction to it. The applicability and accuracy of the approach are verified using observational data gathered over several orbits of the low-Earth-orbit satellite Dynamic Explorer 2 as it passed over Earth's polar caps. The obtained results confirm that the observed disturbances correspond to medium-scale acoustic-gravity waves propagating at a small angle to the horizontal plane, demonstrating the broader methodological potential of the proposed technique for analyzing a wide range of wave phenomena.

title: Hausdorff Dimension and Flexibility for Attractors of Non-Uniformly Hyperbolic Flows
abstract: We study the Hausdorff dimension of attracting sets of three-dimensional flows whose one-dimensional quotient dynamics is non-uniformly expanding. Our main assumption is that the quotient map admits a full-branch uniformly expanding Gibbs--Markov induced map. We first prove that every such attractor contains a hyperbolic horseshoe of Hausdorff dimension strictly larger than two. As a consequence, after an arbitrarily small $C^2$ perturbation, the associated dynamical Lagrange and Markov spectra have robustly non-empty interior for an open and dense set of $C^1$-observables. We then establish intermediate dimension properties. Every admissible intermediate Hausdorff dimension is realized by an ergodic invariant measure supported on the attractor. Moreover, every intermediate stable and unstable dimension is realized by a strictly ergodic hyperbolic subsystem. The approach extends the dimension theory previously developed for geometric Lorenz attractors to more general non-uniformly hyperbolic attractors including singular-hyperbolic attractors, Rovella attractors, and broad classes of skew-product suspension flows modeled by intermittent and Benedicks--Carleson maps.

title: Configuration Migration Planning through Decoupled Modeling and Searching
abstract: Executing large network configuration changes, called migrations, is slow and error-prone today; operators must manually devise a safe order for updating devices that does not disrupt traffic and meets operational intents (e.g., low total time). We develop Smoothie, a versatile migration planning framework that, unlike existing tools, can support diverse operational intents. Inspired by automated planning, it achieves versatility by decoupling the encoding of network safety and intents from the search for a viable plan. Smoothie uses symbolic simulation for general and scalable safety encoding, after which it can use a range of planners, including existing off-the-shelf planners and a new one we developed for optimized parallel plans. We demonstrate Smoothie's versatility and benchmark its performance using diverse migration scenarios on many topologies. It finds both sequential plans and parallel plans, and the parallel ones compress up to thousands of configuration updates into no more than 3 steps. Its versatility does not come at the expense of performance: finishing most planning tasks in less than 1 hour.

title: Entropy Regularization under No-Shorting: Structure Preservation and Convexity in Dynamic Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection
abstract: This paper studies entropy regularization for the discrete-time dynamic mean--variance portfolio problem with no-shorting constraints. In the unconstrained setting, entropy regularization can be introduced without changing the basic quadratic structure of the dynamic program. Under no-shorting, this property is lost: a standard fixed-temperature formulation generally preserves convexity but no longer preserves the homogeneous Bellman structure and the associated piecewise-linear feedback form. We introduce a state-dependent temperature that is matched to the homogeneity of the original mean--variance problem. This restores the piecewise-quadratic value function and the finite-dimensional Bellman recursion. The resulting formulation, however, makes convexity depend on the continuation coefficients generated by the soft recursion. We show that negative continuation coefficients lead to loss of convexity and prove that a common sufficiently small temperature preserves the Bellman structure and convexity over the entire finite horizon. The original no-shorting solution is recovered as the temperature vanishes. We also develop a sample-based implementation for unknown return distributions. Numerical and empirical results illustrate both the structural advantage of the state-dependent temperature and the practical relevance of the convexity-preserving temperature restriction.

title: Towards linear growth for biprojective hypersurfaces of small dimension
abstract: After removing suitable thin subsets, we count rational points of bounded height on some hypersurfaces of small bidegree in $\mathbb{P}^3\times\mathbb{P}^3$ and in $\mathbb{P}^3\times\mathbb{P}^2$. One of the ingredients is a new estimate for the number of rational points of bounded height on diagonal quadratic surfaces which improves as the coefficients grow.

title: Grounded-Dreamer: Robot Learning from World Model Synthetic Data with Physical Grounding
abstract: Scaling robot manipulation policies requires large amounts of diverse, action-labeled data, yet collecting such data in the real world remains expensive and difficult to scale. Existing methods either depend on human teleoperation, rely on simulation with limited visual realism, or use human videos that lack embodiment-specific annotations. In this paper, we introduce Grounded-Dreamer, a framework for synthesizing physically grounded robot manipulation data with video world models while avoiding human teleoperation demonstrations. Grounded-Dreamer combines the visual realism of generative video models with simulator physics engines. Starting from a small set of real images depicting robot task initial states, our method automatically reconstructs task-relevant objects and camera geometry, aligns them in simulation, and collects physically valid trajectories. These trajectories are used to post-train both a video world model and an inverse dynamics model, enabling the generation of visually realistic robot manipulation videos and corresponding robot actions from real images. To filter physically implausible rollouts, Grounded-Dreamer replays generated trajectories in the reconstructed simulation and retains only those that successfully complete the tasks. The real-world robot policies are trained solely on the grounded synthetic trajectories without any human demonstrations. Empirical results in real-world tasks demonstrate that Grounded-Dreamer can synthesize physically grounded data and substantially facilitate policy learning without requiring human teleoperation effort.

title: Recent results in $b \rightarrow s\,\ell\ell$ transitions at LHCb
abstract: Rare decays of $B$ hadrons, such as $b\rightarrow s\ell \ell$ processes, provide great avenues to search for the influence of new physics (NP). They are highly suppressed in the Standard Model (SM) and therefore sensitive to NP contributions. In recent years, experimental measurements have shown tension with SM predictions. It is still up for debate whether these stem from genuine NP or an incomplete understanding of the theory. These proceedings focus on the recent efforts of the LHCb collaboration to advance this field. Some of the results covered show that tensions in these processes, like in $B^0 \rightarrow K^{*0}\, μ^+ μ^-$, still persist upon higher precision. Others aim to shed some light on the theoretical picture through amplitude analyses of decays like $B^0 \rightarrow K^{*0}\, μ^+ μ^-$ and $B^+ \rightarrow K^+ \, μ^+ μ^-$. We also present two innovative measurements: the branching fraction of $B^0 \rightarrow K^+ π^- μ^+ μ^-$ at large dihadron mass; and the first hadron collider measurement of the lepton flavour universality ratio of $B^0 \rightarrow K^{*0} \, \ell^+\ell^-$ at high $q^2$ (dilepton mass squared).

title: Scaling Agentic Data for Long-Horizon Terminal Intelligence
abstract: Terminal agents are moving beyond local operations toward completing real-world professional tasks. Short trajectories can demonstrate commands and tool calls, but they do not fully show how agents accumulate evidence through exploration, use it to inform judgments, continually adjust strategies based on feedback, and turn intermediate results into final deliverables. High-quality long-horizon trajectories capture these agentic behavioral patterns and their connections within a single problem-solving process, providing richer experience for sustained autonomous work. However, environment synthesis may complete or simplify the key work underlying these patterns in advance and thus remove the need for exploration, implementation, and verification that the agent was meant to perform. To address this, we introduce TerminalHorizon, a fully automated data synthesis engine for long-horizon terminal agents. Starting from real-world professional work, it uses independent execution to identify key work omitted during construction and uses the resulting evidence to guide environment reconstruction. To extend these patterns across stages, it progressively expands tasks under the same goal, introducing new requirements that build on prior results and call for further exploration and improvement. Using this engine, we construct 1.5K task environments and perform supervised fine-tuning of Qwen3.5-27B on the resulting dataset to obtain TerminalHorizon-27B. We achieve substantial performance gains on all 12 benchmarks spanning coding-agent tasks, agentic tasks in real-world production settings, and general reasoning. Multiple RSI case studies, each with a 12-hour research budget, further demonstrate the model's ability to continue experimenting beyond an initial solution, improve its methods based on feedback, and retain effective improvements in its final deliverables.

title: Modelling the Nordic power system expansion with PyPSA-Eur: a comparison with the Nordic Grid Development Perspective 2025
abstract: We compare the Nordic Grid Development Perspective 2025 (NGDP) with a least-cost transition pathway for the Nordic power system obtained with PyPSA-Eur for the period 2025-2050 under a net-zero CO$_2$ constraint. The model co-optimises generation, storage, and transmission expansion with hourly system operation while constraining the Nordic generation mix to remain consistent with NGDP milestone ranges. Overall, the optimised capacity pathways reproduce the broad NGDP expansion of wind and solar power, with Denmark emerging as the main locus of offshore wind and solar deployment, Finland as a major site for onshore wind expansion, and Norway and Sweden relying more strongly on existing hydropower and nuclear capacity. The main discrepancy between the two pathways does not lie in the broad build-out of variable renewables, but in the timing and role of hydrogen. Whereas the NGDP treats hydrogen as an early and steadily increasing component of industrial demand and system development already from 2030, PyPSA-Eur delays substantial hydrogen deployment until 2045-2050, when it becomes cost-effective primarily as a flexibility and seasonal storage option in a strongly variable-renewable-energy-dominated system. This contrast suggests that early hydrogen build-out in the Nordics is not a robust outcome of cost optimisation alone, but depends strongly on assumptions regarding industrial demand growth, sector coupling, and anticipatory infrastructure planning. We therefore argue that hydrogen remains the principal strategic uncertainty in the Nordic transition, with the NGDP representing a more anticipatory planning perspective and PyPSA-Eur a more conservative least-cost timing of deployment.

title: Real Fiducial Vectors Only Exist in Dimensions $d\equiv 3 \pmod{4}$
abstract: We investigate restrictions on the dimensions and coordinate fields of real Weyl-Heisenberg fiducial vectors. Our main result is that such vectors can exist only in dimensions $d\equiv 3\pmod{4}$. This result is motivated by evidence showing that real Weyl-Heisenberg fiducial vectors can exist only in dimensions $d = 4m^2 + 3, m \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. We further restrict the possible dimensions when the coordinate field is a totally real number field, an even or odd degree extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, a real quadratic field, or a maximal real subfield of a cyclotomic field. Lastly, we establish non-existence over odd-degree number fields under either positivity of all non-trivial cyclic-shift overlaps or a conjectural containment of a distinguished quadratic field in the SIC field.

title: Imbibition dynamics under dissolution-driven fluid thickening
abstract: The imbibition of milk into a biscuit provides an example of a broader class of processes in which a liquid invades a porous material, dissolving components of the solid and thereby modifying its own rheology. This coupling between imbibition, dissolution, and evolving fluid rheology also occurs in food processing, filtration, and reactive porous media. While the resulting changes in fluid viscosity are known to affect imbibition, a quantitative description of how this evolving rheology determines the imbibition dynamics is still lacking. Here, we establish such a description for dissolution-driven fluid thickening. For a capillary tube in the well-mixed limit, we derive a generalized Washburn law showing that the evolving viscosity can be incorporated through a rescaled time given by the accumulated inverse viscosity. This predicts a collapse of the imbibition dynamics for different dissolution rates, which we confirm numerically using coupled free-surface and solute-transport simulations. When diffusion is slower, concentration and viscosity become spatially heterogeneous, resulting in a weaker retardation of the advancing liquid than predicted by the well-mixed theory. We then consider disordered porous media and quantify how dissolution-driven thickening and variations in pore geometry affect the dynamics. Our results extend the classical Washburn description to imbibition with evolving fluid properties and provide a quantitative basis for understanding fluid uptake when interactions with the solid progressively modify the rheology of the invading liquid.

title: Understanding Verification Vulnerabilities in Cross-chain Bridges: An Empirical Study
abstract: With the rapid development of blockchain technology, numerous heterogeneous blockchains have emerged, each featuring distinct architectures, consensus mechanisms, and application ecosystems. Cross-chain bridges have consequently become a critical infrastructure component, typically relying on smart contracts to facilitate message passing and asset transfers across heterogeneous blockchains. Unlike single-chain contracts, bridge contracts introduce additional verification logic to validate external-chain data, such as state proofs, message sender identities, and signatures. However, correctly implementing such logic is challenging. We refer to vulnerabilities that violate the security guarantees of cross-chain verification as Cross-chain Verification Vulnerabilities (CVVs). To characterize CVVs, we conduct the first systematic empirical study of this vulnerability class. By analyzing 588 security audit reports from 36 real-world cross-chain bridge projects, we derive 11 CVV patterns and organize them into 5 high-level categories according to the affected verification properties. Following this taxonomy, we construct a CVV dataset containing 830 vulnerability instances across 786 contract files. The dataset establishes mappings among audit reports, audited source-code versions, affected source files, and CVV-pattern labels. We then assess existing detection approaches. Current tools provide limited documented coverage of CVV patterns, while only two of four evaluated LLMs outperform an all-pattern constant baseline of 29.3% Macro-F1; the best reaches 51.2%. Together, the limited tool coverage and inconsistent LLM gains motivate detection methods tailored to cross-chain verification semantics.

title: PreSTO: Predictive Subtree Prefetching for Fast LLM Power Sampling
abstract: Power sampling improves large language model (LLM) reasoning at test time by sampling from a sharpened version of the base model's distribution. Its sampler, PowerMH, is slow because its Metropolis--Hastings (MH) updates are sequential: each accept/reject decision sets the state from which the next proposal is generated. Prior work reduces this cost by changing the sampler or the model (e.g., sequential Monte Carlo, approximate lookahead, distillation). We propose Predictive SubTree Prefetching (PreSTO), which accelerates PowerMH by prefetching future proposals and provably leaves its MH transition kernel unchanged. PreSTO views future MH outcomes as a tree of accept/reject decisions: in each model call, it generates the proposals of a \textit{prefetched subtree} of this tree in one batch, then follows the realized path with the original MH acceptance rule. We also observe that MH reaches only a sparse, nearly unary part of each prefetched subtree, we further design a \textit{predictive traversal rule} that chooses the subtree to maximize the predicted number of completed transitions. Across seven datasets and five base LLMs, PreSTO achieves median speedups of $1.71\times$, $1.91\times$, and $2.33\times$ on PowerMH and its follow-ups EntropyCut and MultiTryMH, respectively; on the first two, it makes a median of $3.9\times$ fewer model calls, each only $2.1\times$ longer. On LCB V6 with Qwen3.5-9B, the predictive traversal rule is a further $1.25\times$--$1.37\times$ faster than the default breadth-first traversal.

title: RoleWorld: Knowledge Transfer in World Modeling with Functional Role Abstractions
abstract: World models enable large language model (LLM) agents to anticipate action effects and make informed decisions. For generalization, it is desirable for such world models to transfer efficiently to new environments with similar interaction structure and underlying dynamics. Recent approaches encode world dynamics as symbolic rules or executable programs, whose compositional structure in principle affords transfer, but still organize such knowledge around environment-specific objects. To address this limitation, we introduce RoleWorld, a symbolic world modeling approach which uses reusable prototypes and environment-specific parameter values as functional role abstractions to represent how objects behave in interactions. From interaction trajectories, a teacher LLM extracts role prototypes and executable transition rules defined over role instances, together with a skill that guides the actor LLM to use role information in decision making. In a target world, without the teacher, the actor uses this skill together with its current role assignments and parameter estimates, and actively tests a role instance hypothesis through interaction when its uncertainty affects the current decision. Feedback from each action refines role assignments and estimates parameter values online, with no LLM parameter updates and the transition rules held fixed. Experiments on MARS benchmark show that RoleWorld enables robust generalization across environments with significantly altered object behavior, suggesting that functional role abstractions can serve as an effective component for knowledge transfer in world modeling. Project Page: https://future-item.github.io/RoleWorld.

title: Formation Dynamics of a Rotating Solar Spicule-like Event and Associated Energy-Mass Transport
abstract: We performed three-dimensional radiative magnetohydrodynamic(3D RMHD) simulations in an upward-directed (positive-polarity) open magnetic field with an initial background strength of 10 G. We identified vortex-associated spicule-like events and carried out a detailed analysis of one representative event. Prior to the formation of this spicule-like event, a photospheric vortex appears and twists the magnetic field lines, then develops upward into higher atmospheric layers, forming a magnetic tornado system. This event is generated during this process. At the periphery of this magnetic tornado, twisted magnetic field lines with negative vertical components reconnect with both external positive-polarity background fields and central positive-polarity fields. The magnetic reconnection sites rise and rotate together with the developed magnetic tornado, and many jet-like substructures in this event are closely associated with plasma upward ejections from these reconnection regions. A vertical force analysis shows that, for this event, plasma uplift in the photosphere and lower chromosphere is dominated by the pressure-gradient force, whereas in the upper chromosphere, the Lorentz force gradually becomes dominant. At a height of about 4 Mm above the solar surface, this event produces a mean upward mass flux density on the order of $10^{-7}~{\rm kg~m^{-2}~s^{-1}}$ and a mean upward Poynting flux density of approximately $525~{\rm W~m^{-2}}$. The wave-mode decomposition results show that the energy transport associated with the rotational spicule-like event is dominated by the Alfvén mode. Alfvén waves, fast-mode waves, and slow-mode waves carry energy into the lower corona in an approximate ratio of $10:7:3$.

title: PreCoG: Preview-Edit for Efficient Video Correction in Generation-Time
abstract: Iterative text-to-video generation relies on feedback to correct compositional and temporal failures. However, existing methods typically require another full generation run for each correction, repeating computation and potentially disrupting already correct content. We introduce PreCoG, an iterative framework for correcting semantic failures during video generation. PreQA diagnoses failures from low-cost previews and constructs corrective conditions, while PreEdit edits cached generation trajectories under these conditions, attenuating orthogonal changes to limit disruption of already correct content. PreCoG completes generation only for the selected candidate, reusing its cached trajectory to reduce redundant computation and help preserve semantic consistency between the preview and the final video. Experiments show that PreCoG achieves the highest VBench and T2V-CompBench scores and approaches VSR's leading VS2 score at $0.56\times$ its inference time. It also outperforms GENMAC on all three quality and alignment metrics at $0.86\times$ its inference time.

title: How Should We Evaluate Naturalness for Synthetic Speech with a Foreign Accent?
abstract: Recent advances in speech synthesis technology have enabled the generation of speech with diverse characteristics. One such characteristic is a foreign accent. In our preliminary experiments, we found that UTMOS, a widely used automatic speech quality assessment system, tended to assign lower scores to speech with stronger foreign accents, even though it is produced by a human speaker. This observation raised a question: How do humans evaluate the naturalness of foreign-accented speech? We conducted a large-scale subjective evaluation involving both native and non-native listeners under different evaluation instructions. The results showed that humans also considered accentedness when evaluating naturalness, but that defining naturalness in terms of human-likeness and selecting raters who have greater exposure to the target accent may enable more appropriate evaluation. This study aims to provide a starting point for future discussions on fairer and more appropriate evaluation of synthetic speech with a foreign accent.

title: Fix the Match, Not the Solver: STITCH -- a Self-Supervised Compatibility Measure for Eroded Visual Puzzles
abstract: Unlike the clean and pixel-aligned complete pieces of standard jigsaw benchmarks, real-world puzzle fragments lose their boundary regions to erosion, destroying the signal that classical compatibility measures (CMs) rely on.
