Using a duality formula for bimodules over division algebras, we prove that every twisted Calabi--Yau division algebra is index-symmetric. The examples include the Weyl skew fields and, more generally, the quotient division rings of rings of differential operators on smooth affine varieties in characteristic zero. Further examples are the quotient division rings of enveloping algebras of finite-dimensional Lie algebras, Ore extensions of twisted Calabi--Yau noetherian domains, quantum affine spaces, and group algebras of torsion-free polycyclic-by-finite groups.

title: Non-Hermitian Two-Kink Control of Corner States in Twisted Chern Bilayers
abstract: Corner states are bound by boundary-mass defects, but this geometric anchoring restricts their spatial and internal control. Focusing on twisted bilayers assembled from Chern insulators with opposite Chern numbers, we show that a mass-phase kink carried by a non-Hermitian interlayer mass and an independent imaginary-momentum kink separate the spectral, in-plane, and interlayer control of mass-defect corner states. The mass-phase kink creates the parent corner pole and fixes its energy and intrinsic decay, while directed interlayer tunneling encodes its layer polarization. The imaginary-momentum texture instead reshapes the closed-boundary envelope and redistributes stationary right-state weight between corners. A twisted Qi--Wu--Zhang bilayer verifies this division on arbitrary, including concave, boundaries. A $30^\circ$ twisted Haldane dodecagon realizes twelve finite-energy parent states whose in-gap spectral manifold persists while boundary patterns redistribute its normalized right-subspace weight toward six, three, two, or one target corners. The two kinks therefore cooperate or compete while keeping spectral ancestry, spatial weight, and layer character distinct, thereby establishing a unified framework for controlling mass-defect corner states across disparate boundary geometries and mass textures.

title: A Solvable Model in the Half-filled Landau Level
abstract: A solvable microscopic model of interacting electrons in a half-filled Landau level is presented. The Hamiltonian is a well-defined limit of the electron-electron interaction. The low energy sector consists of a set of independent, spatially interlaced, one-dimensional systems of non-interacting fermionic dipoles, each system with a Fermi sea ground state. The total number of dipoles in the set of Fermi seas forming the two-dimensional ground state equals the number of electrons in the system and the density of states at the Fermi level is that of a two-dimensional Fermi gas. The model is obtained by generalizing, or rather adopting, the existing exact solution on a thin, but not too thin, torus to the two-dimensional bulk case.

title: Schatten class membership of products of composition operators and their adjoints
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Schatten class membership of the product of a composition operator and the adjoint of another composition operator on the Hardy and Bergman spaces. We provide several sufficient conditions and necessary conditions for these operators to belong to the Schatten classes. Moreover, for some specific symbols including linear fractional maps, finite Blaschke products, and inner functions, we obtain necessary and sufficient conditions.

title: A noetherian Hopf algebra has bijective antipode
abstract: We prove that a Hopf algebra over an arbitrary field has a bijective antipode if either its left or right regular module has finite uniform dimension. In particular, this solves Skryabin's conjecture, posed in 2006, that every noetherian Hopf algebra has a bijective antipode. Starting from Skryabin's injectivity theorem for weakly finite Hopf algebras, we associate to each finite-dimensional subcoalgebra an essential left ideal of common denominators that is also a right coideal in the antipode image. An annihilator identity makes this image essential in the original algebra as a left module over the image, yielding finite left uniform dimension from finite right uniform dimension. A second denominator construction inside the antipode image, together with a restricted inverse-antipode identity, proves surjectivity.

title: Sori: Streamable and Controllable Model for Non-musical Audio to Symbolic Music Transformation
abstract: We introduce Non-musical Audio to Symbolic Music Transformation (NASMT), a novel task that converts non-musical audio into symbolic music representations. Unlike automatic music transcription, which assumes musical input and a unique correct score, NASMT is inherently one-to-many and requires evaluation along two axes: input correspondence and musicality. We present Sori, an encoder--decoder Transformer that addresses this task through domain adversarial training (DAT), which bridges the gap between musical and non-musical audio in the encoder's feature space, and classifier-free guidance (CFG) with a continuous parameter~$γ$ that controls the trade-off between correspondence and musicality at inference time. Across objective metrics and a listening study, Sori provides effective continuous control via $γ$ and compares favorably with instrument-agnostic transcription models. Sori supports real-time streaming on a consumer CPU. Audio examples are available at https://soridemo0320.github.io/sori-demo/.

title: Capturing Bisimulation-Invariant Exponential-Space Complexity Classes
abstract: Otto's Theorem characterises the bisimulation-invariant PTIME queries over graphs as exactly those that can be formulated in the polyadic mu-calculus. This extends to a characterisation of the full bisimulation-invariant exponential-time hierarchy, using a higher-order extension of the polyadic mu-calculus, called PHFL, which is naturally stratified by type order. The bisimulation-invariant fragment of k-EXPTIME is captured by the fragment of PHFL whose formulas have type order at most k. This is obtained using a generalisation of the Immerman-Vardi Theorem by Freire and Martins. Here we provide such a characterisation of the exponential-space hierarchy. We show that the bisimulation-invariant fragment of k-EXPSPACE is captured by the fragment of PHFL of type order k+1 whose formulas are tail-recursive. Tail recursion limits the interplay between fixpoints and higher-order functions so that model checking based on fixpoint iteration can be made more space efficient in a way comparable to tail recursion in programming languages. The capturing result makes use of a generalisation of Vardi's characterisation of PSPACE as first-order logic with partial fixpoints, namely that k-EXPSPACE is captured by higher-order logic of order k+1 with partial fixpoints.

title: Representation Theorems for Actual Powers over Two-Agent General Concurrent Game Frames
abstract: One of the most well-known connections between logic and games is Pauly's representation theorem: the induced powers of individuals and coalitions in concurrent game frames correspond, in a precise sense, to a certain class of neighborhood frames. The precise sense here is what is called alpha effectivity (or alpha power): the power of a coalition is characterized by the sets of states in which it can ensure that the outcome lies by taking some joint action. This definition is inherently monotonic, and, as pointed out by van Benthem, Bezhanishvili, and Enqvist (2019), that fact can obscure relevant information about the power structure in the game: we do not know whether two sets that a coalition has the power to enforce correspond to the same joint action or to different joint actions. An alternative is to characterize the power of a coalition by its actual power (called basic power by van Benthem, Bezhanishvili, and Enqvist (2019)): the collection of sets of states, each of which corresponds to one joint action by the coalition and all possible joint actions by the other agents. It has recently been argued by Li and Ju (2025, 2026) that standard concurrent game frames rely on three assumptions that may, in some cases, be too strong: seriality, independence of agents, and determinism. This yields a total of eight different classes of general concurrent game frames. In this paper, assuming two agents, we prove that, in terms of actual powers, the eight classes of general concurrent game frames are represented by eight corresponding classes of neighborhood frames. This generalizes a result by van Benthem, Bezhanishvili, and Enqvist (2019).

title: Whitney--Lagrange Decomposition for the First Family of Finite Element Differential Forms
abstract: We derive polynomial bubble duality in barycentric coordinates and construct explicit nodal bases for the first family of finite element differential forms. Logarithmic coordinates give an elementary proof of the Whitney--bubble decomposition. The Hessian of negative entropy defines a metric whose normalized Hodge star maps bubble generators to complementary-degree polynomial forms. This gives a direct geometric description of the known dualities and proves nondegeneracy of their integral pairings. Combining Whitney forms with shifted Lagrange polynomials then gives bases dual to tangential point evaluations in every dimension and order. The construction extends to scalar nodes that are unisolvent on every face. The interpolant is independent of the roots and commutes with face restriction.

title: Execution-Time Opacity in (Controllable) Timed Automata is Hard
abstract: Timing information leakage occurs whenever an attacker successfully deduces confidential internal information by observing some timed information such as the total duration of a run. Timed automata (TAs) are an extension of finite-state automata with a set of clocks evolving at the same rate and that can be tested or reset. Hence, this formalism is able to represent systems involving timing constraints reacting to the passage of time. Some of the transitions in a timed automaton may be controlled, i.e., enabled or disabled, to limit the runs that are allowed. Execution-time opacity (ET-opacity) aims at studying timing information leakage through the analysis of timed automata. More precisely, the ET-opacity problem consists in deciding whether an attacker can deduce whether some secret locations were visited by a run, solely from the run's duration. When control is allowed, the goal becomes to find a strategy that blocks the runs leaking information. This problem has been shown decidable for TAs, with and without control. However, these existing results only provide upper bounds on the complexity of the ET-opacity problem, sometimes largely above the tight bound. Our main contribution is to provide tight lower bounds for those two results. Moreover, for controllable TAs, two variants of ET-opacity (depending on whether detecting if a run did not visit a secret location represents an information leakage or not, and named full and weak ET-opacity respectively) had been separately studied; we prove here that these two notions are inter-reducible.

title: New Translations From LTL with Past to LDBA and DPA
abstract: We present asymptotically optimal translations from linear temporal logic with past to limit-deterministic Buchi automata and onwards to deterministic parity automata. In contrast to previously known translations involving past, the ones presented here are incremental: states and transitions can be constructed as needed on-the-fly, and they do not involve backtracking in order to correct for temporal inconsistencies. The past is naturally encoded in the formula by alternating between weak and strong versions of past operators. To handle the difficulties that arise from the alternation of least and greatest fix-point operators (such as between the "until" operator and its weak counterpart), we rewrite the given formula based on the infinitary behavior of a given word with respect to subformulae rooted with such operators.

title: Lasso Games
abstract: We study games on finite graphs with labelled or weighted edges in which plays end as soon as the first loop is formed. The resulting play has a lasso shape: a path (head) followed by a cycle (loop). We consider two semantics for determining the winner: the loop semantics, where only the loop matters, and the lasso semantics, where the entire play is taken into account. We show that adopting the lasso semantics may have a dramatic impact on both the complexity of the game and the memory required to play optimally. Mean-payoff games with lasso semantics are no longer positionally determined, and the threshold problem â€“ deciding whether the value of the game is at least 0 â€“ is PSPACE-complete. In contrast, lasso parity games are equivalent to weak parity games, remain positionally determined and are solvable in polynomial time. Furthermore, we show that if a positionally determined winning objective is closed under cyclic permutation and both the objective and its complement are closed under concatenation, then it is equivalent to the parity objective. Finally, we consider mod-k games, where the winner depends on the length of the path modulo k >= 2. We show that these games, in both semantics, are PSPACE-complete. Alongside computational complexity, we analyze the memory required to play optimally. We establish that for any game positionally determined in loop semantics, memory of size 2^n is sufficient in lasso semantics. We complement this by showing exponential memory lower bounds for lasso mean-payoff and mod-k games.

title: SkillFusion: Towards Reliable Multi-Skill Composition for LLM Agents
abstract: Independently authored skills can impose incompatible requirements, competing preferences, and redundant instructions when jointly loaded by an LLM agent. We propose SkillFusion, an offline compiler that reconciles these interactions into a reusable merged skill. Its central idea is to make composition decisions explicit through typed, scoped constraints linked to their source directives. A type-scope gate selects candidate interactions, while selective fallback revisits pairs potentially missed by structural pruning. A classifier identifies interaction types, and an adversarial verifier re-examines uncertain judgments. The resolver applies conditional routing or explicit priorities to hard conflicts, verified abstraction to soft conflicts, and deduplication to redundant instructions. Source-linked checks guide synthesis and compression, and metadata synthesis supports discovery of the merged skill. The resulting artifact retains associated scripts and resources and can be reused across tasks and executor models. SkillFusion achieves the highest mean Success among evaluated non-oracle methods on all three agent benchmarks and on both transfer benchmarks across three executor models. At the largest tested instruction configurations, it achieves over 2.5 times the Success of unresolved multi-skill loading, highlighting the growing value of reconciliation as composition becomes more demanding. The code will be open-sourced after the review process concludes.

title: Security in LLM-Assisted Coding: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Large Language Models accelerate software development but introduce severe security vulnerabilities. This systematic review investigates security risks in automated coding, benchmark limitations, and the role of human developers. Findings indicate that models frequently generate insecure code and faulty patches due to training data biases. Additionally, the models themselves are susceptible to direct attacks. Current evaluation methods suffer from data contamination and lack robust security metrics. Consequently, human oversight remains essential. Safer integration of automation will require more security-aware model architectures, stronger security-specific benchmarks, and more effective human-AI collaboration frameworks to mitigate these systemic risks.

title: On the OpenAI proof that Landau-Siegel zeros do not exist
abstract: A recent manuscript of OpenAI asserts that Landau-Siegel zeros do not exist. Here, we give a detailed account of its argument, arranged as a direct proof with explicit constants. There are absolute constants $q_0$ and $δ_0>0$ such that, for every primitive real Dirichlet character $χ$ of conductor $q\ge q_0$, every real zero $β\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,χ)$ satisfies $(1-β)\log q\geδ_0$, and one can take $q_0=10^{10}$ and $δ_0=3.0\times 10^{-3}$. Combined with a recent computation of Lu, Zaman, and Zhao, this result yields the bound $(1-β)\log q\ge 3.0\times 10^{-3}$ for every conductor $q\ge 3$. The proof is an interpolation determinant argument in the biquadratic field generated by $\sqrt{2}$ over the quadratic field attached to $χ$. A real zero close to one forces $χ(p)=-1$ for most primes $p$, and the Frobenius congruence at these primes makes a certain nonzero determinant divisible by higher powers of these primes than its Archimedean size allows. The underlying ideas are those of the OpenAI manuscript. The explicit constants, and the presentation, are new.

title: Toward Explainability in Multimodal Recommendation
abstract: Multimodal recommender systems effectively alleviate data sparsity and cold-start problems by integrating heterogeneous information, yet complex cross-modal representations and model decision-making processes also introduce new interpretability challenges. Despite the rapid growth of research on the interpretability of multimodal recommendation in recent years, relevant methods and evaluation criteria remain relatively fragmented, lacking a unified conceptual framework. To address this gap, this paper categorizes existing methods into modality explanation and post-hoc explanation based on the timing and manner of explanation generation, and further constructs a progressive system for each category. Building on this foundation, this paper synthesizes four categories of evaluation metrics from both objective quantitative and subjective perceptual perspectives, and reviews relevant datasets along the dimensions of application domain and data source. Through a comprehensive analysis of existing research, we further propose future research directions. This paper aims to establish a unified analytical perspective across multimodal representation, recommendation decision-making, and user preferences, providing a research foundation for building transparent and trustworthy multimodal recommender systems.

title: Dimension of affine iterated function systems on $\mathbb{R}^d$
abstract: Let $\{f_i(x)=M_ix+a_i\}_{i\in I}$ be an affine iterated function system on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with attractor $Λ$, and let $μ$ be an associated self-affine measure. Assume that the $M_i$ generate a Zariski dense subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb{R})$. Under the strong open set condition, we show that $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}Λ$ equals the affinity dimension and that $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}μ$ equals the Lyapunov dimension. The above results are consequences of the following projection theorem, which requires no separation condition. For every $1\leq n\leq d$ and for Furstenberg measure a.e. $(d-n)$-dimensional subspace $V$, \[ \dim_{\mathrm{H}} (P^V)_*μ=\min\{n,\,\dim_{\mathrm{H}}μ\}. \] This projection theorem in fact holds under hypotheses weaker than Zariski density: simplicity of the Lyapunov spectrum and a mild transversality condition (the Oseledets non-concentration property). The source of dimension increment in our proof is the positive dimension of the fiberwise conditional measures, exploited through Wu's one-dimensional entropy increase theorem. A key ingredient in reducing the higher-dimensional problem to this setting is a new structural result: a slab-filling property of the measure.

title: Learning Safety-Constrained Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation for Lunar Surface Operations
abstract: Robotic systems for lunar surface operations must act autonomously and preserve their own integrity in an environment where failures are unrecoverable and continuous supervision is impossible. This paper presents a Constrained Reinforcement Learning framework for quadrupedal mobile manipulators that learns a single whole-body policy for tracking a 6D end-effector pose specified in task space, with operational limits enforced during learning through a constrained learning mechanism. We introduce a reward formulation in which the transition between locomotion and manipulation emerges from the reward geometry rather than from an explicit gating mechanism, a stability term derived from the Gravito-Inertial Inclination Margin and motivated by the reduced-gravity dynamics of the lunar surface, and a design rule for reward regularization that follows from the multiplicative structure of the termination-based objective. The framework is evaluated in a lunar-analog simulation spanning three terrain morphologies at five difficulty levels under lunar gravity, with regolith contact properties calibrated to the JSC-1a simulant and varied from loose to dense. The learned policy attains mean position and orientation errors of 3.22 cm and 6.83 deg. under nominal conditions, retains this precision across regolith densities and over the operationally representative range of terrain difficulty, and reduces soft-constraint violation time by up to an order of magnitude relative to an unconstrained baseline while incurring no hard-constraint violations.

title: Rationality of Kontsevich moduli of stable maps, and their Galois descents
abstract: Let k be a field and X be a geometrically rational variety over k. We investigate the Kontsevich moduli spaces of genus zero, stable maps with curve classes of low degree on X over k, and define their twisted Galois descents. We study the k-rationality of these spaces in detail when X is a projective space/Severi Brauer variety and when X is moduli of genus zero n-marked points. When X is a homogeneous variety over the field of complex numbers, this is a well-known theorem of Kim-Pandharipande.

title: AlphaPilot: Multi-Turn Tool-Using LLM Agents for Adaptive Alpha Mining with Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Formulaic alpha mining seeks interpretable expressions that rank assets by future returns. The task is challenging because it demands simultaneous processing of unstructured market descriptions, historical data, and quantitative evaluation of candidate factors, yet most existing methods exploit only a subset of these signals. We introduce AlphaPilot, a reinforcement-learning framework that trains multi-turn tool-using LLM agents for adaptive alpha mining. The agent conditions on market descriptions, proposes factor expressions, queries real-data evaluator feedback, and updates a retained factor pool across turns. This design jointly leverages market text, LLM financial knowledge, real data, and evaluation feedback. At inference time, AlphaPilot performs day-by-day search and pool updates to adapt to shifting market regimes. Across three independent runs in out-of-sample rolling backtests on CSI300 and CSI500, AlphaPilot achieves mean total returns of 42.93% and 54.19%, with mean Sharpe ratios of 2.46 and 2.86, respectively. It attains the highest mean total return, Sharpe, and RankIC among the evaluated methods on both universes.

title: Hypersurfaces with constant sectional curvature of a product of two space forms
abstract: We complete the classification of hypersurfaces with constant sectional curvature of dimension greater than or equal to three in the product of two space forms.

title: SiteEvo: An LLM Agent for Autonomous Discovery of Site-Adaptive Massive MIMO Detectors
abstract: Designing a massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) detector that is tailored to each specific deployment site can improve detection performance, yet most existing detectors, including deep-unfolding methods, adapt mainly within human-prescribed algorithmic structures. This letter proposes SiteEvo, a site-adaptive agentic discovery framework that extends adaptation from parameter tuning to detector-algorithm discovery. Rather than selecting or recombining predefined architectures, the large language model (LLM) agent synthesizes complete executable detector programs under a common design contract by combining its pretrained communication knowledge, site-specific wireless evidence, and experience accumulated during the search. Each proposal defines its own processing structure and trainable parameterization, and the parameters are optimized by a communication-system backend. The resulting high-performance detector is further structurally refined to reduce block-level computational cost under a bit error rate (BER)-preservation constraint and is finally frozen for deployment without online LLM inference. Simulations across three sites demonstrate BER reductions by factors of 2.6 to 6.0 over the best-performing competing detector at each site at 6 dB, while structural refinement reduces block-level computational cost by 16.7-34.1% under a validation-BER constraint.

title: Phase-Gated Constrained Reinforcement Learning for End-to-End Capture and Detumbling of Non-Cooperative Targets
abstract: Active debris removal requires a servicer spacecraft to approach a non-cooperative tumbling object, capture it, and arrest its rotation. This sequence is conventionally divided among phase-specific controllers, each depending on knowledge of the target's inertia, a dedicated grappling fixture, or a hand-designed switch at the contact-rich seam where such pipelines are most fragile. We show that a single constrained reinforcement learning policy can execute the entire mission, driving a dual-arm free-flying servicer from free-space closing through friction-based fixture-free capture to full detumbling of a target whose mass and inertia are unknown and whose state is observed only through noisy estimates. The enabling mechanism is a smooth proximity gate applied at three loci of a constrained Markov decision process. In the reward it induces the phase structure rather than imposing it; in the action space it forecloses a degenerate grab-and-pull exploit as a hard guarantee; and in the constraint set it resolves a normalization failure of constraint-based learning, in which a constraint spanning phases that load it unequally is rendered nearly inert in the phase where precision matters most. Both the failure mode and the remedy apply to any multi-phase problem of this kind. Over 1000 randomized trials the policy succeeds in 99.5% while holding its contact-force, actuator, base-reaction and collision limits throughout, transfers zero-shot to unseen geometries and centre-of-mass offsets, and extrapolates across a tenfold range of target mass.

title: When Skills Remain But Access Fails: Factorized Skill Memory for Continual Skill Internalization
abstract: Skill internalization aims to convert externally specified procedural skills into persistent model capabilities, allowing language-model agents to execute them without retrieving or reinjecting skill descriptions at inference time. Yet when new skills are learned continually, whether previously internalized skills remain usable is still poorly understood. We study forgetting in continual skill internalization and uncover a clear hierarchical structure. Early in subsequent training, a model may lose the ability to invoke an old skill from the raw request, while supplying only the correct canonical skill name substantially restores the learned behavior; with further optimization, this conditional execution also degrades. We call these two stages skill-addressing forgetting and skill-execution forgetting. Guided by this finding, we introduce Factorized Skill Memory (FSM), which separates continual skill memory into a plastic Address Memory and a stable Execution Memory. At each stage, FSM trains a new LoRA executor using only current-stage data, freezes it after acquisition, and appends it to Execution Memory; in parallel, Address Memory incrementally learns to map current requests to executors without replaying historical requests or execution trajectories. At inference time, Address Memory selects one executor from the raw request, and only that frozen executor performs a single language-model generation. On a five-stage benchmark built from 100 TaskBench skills, FSM achieves 65.95% mean exact match and 93.38% addressing accuracy across two task orders, improving over the strongest replay-free parameter-isolation baseline by 14.3 percentage points while remaining within 1.9 points of Replay, which retains historical training examples.

title: Probing the chromo-electric dipole moment of top quark near the toponium production threshold at LHC
abstract: The recent observation of an excess near the kinematic $t\bar{t}$ production threshold by the CMS and ATLAS collaborations suggests the existence of a color-singlet and $S$-wave quasi-bound state of top quark. Due to the non-relativistic nature of top and anti-top quarks in this threshold region, toponium production provides an ideal system to probe the anomalous dipole moments of the top quark. In this work, we investigate the impact of chromo-electric dipole moment (CEDM) in $t\bar{t}$-gluon vertex on toponium production at the LHC. We implement the enhanced near-threshold production of the spin-0 color-singlet toponium state $η_t$ via gluon fusion. The resonant toponium contribution is then combined with the continuum $t\bar{t}$ production amplitude, including the interference effects induced by the top CEDM. Furthermore, we construct a set of asymmetries based on the angular distributions of charged leptons in the leptonic decay channel of $t\bar{t}$. Finally, we derive the expected exclusion limit on the top quark CEDM parameter $d_t^g$ using these lepton angular asymmetries.

title: RF Fingerprinting of DSP Implementations using Machine Learning: An Over-the-Air Case Study
abstract: Radio frequency fingerprinting aims to identify transmitters by exploiting small differences in the emitted signal waveform. Common approaches exploit hardware-dependent imperfections for that purpose. This work instead investigates whether differences between digital signal processing implementations of a transmitter can be identified from their radiated signals. As a practical case study, five different software-based DSP implementations for generating a 2-FSK RTTY communication waveform are considered. In a monitoring receiver, a classifier can identify these DSP implementations using convolutional neural networks that are trained on augmented software-generated signals represented as raw IQ, power spectrum or instantaneous frequency. The trained networks are evaluated on over-the-air recordings obtained using a shortwave transceiver and a software-defined radio receiver. The best neural network combines IQ and the power spectrum representation and achieves an accuracy of up to 90%. The study further examines the influence of the signal SNR and the observation bandwidth on the classification accuracy. The results demonstrate that DSP implementations leave distinguishable characteristics in the transmitted signals and suggest that DSP-dependent fingerprinting can provide complementary information for specific emitter identification systems.

title: Rabin Games Revisited
abstract: Rabin games have their roots in Michael Rabin's seminal work on automata over infinite trees and form a classical model for infinite-round games with Ï‰-regular winning conditions. They play a central role in automata theory and temporal synthesis: translating an LTL specification into an equivalent deterministic Rabin automaton reduces synthesis to solving a Rabin game. In practice, however, Rabin games are typically solved indirectly, via parity games. One possible reason is that many direct algorithms have a factorial dependence on the Rabin index k, the number of Rabin pairs. In this work, we revisit Rabin's 1972 recursive algorithm. The algorithm is implicit in Rabin's proof and intertwined with finite-state determinacy. First, we "excavate" it as an explicit arena-based solver using standard reachability- and BÃ¼chi-game solving as basic building blocks, thus avoiding the exponential dependence on the alphabet in Rabin's original presentation. Second, we show that memoization removes the factorial term from the recursion-tree analysis. Finally, we introduce a variation that recurses on the Rabin index. These results provide a modern analysis of Rabin's recursive method and a basis for studying direct Rabin-game solvers for temporal synthesis.

title: Concept Representations in Vector Space: Quantifying Sharedness and Idiosyncrasy of Meaning
abstract: Concepts are the basic units through which we navigate the world and communicate meaning. But do you and I really mean the same thing when we think or speak about a concept? The present study develops a measurement framework for modeling and analyzing interindividual variation in concept representations through sentence embeddings, dense vector representations mapping entire utterances into a shared geometric space. The framework is developed in a theoretical argument and validated, demonstrated, and subjected to robustness checks in a pre-registered study. Short personal definitions, elicited from $N = 125$ participants, are encoded as sentence embeddings and submitted pairwise to a crossed random effects model yielding two concept-level quantities: sharedness ($S_b$), the expected dissimilarity between two randomly drawn individuals, and idiosyncrasy ($I_b$), the person-specific share of total dyadic variance. Two validity tests support the approach: the embedding space fully recovers concept and domain organization from participant definitions even with the target word excluded, and a parameter-free classifier achieves 0.630 accuracy in a within-participant extensional prediction task against a chance baseline of 0.500 and a consistency ceiling of 0.893. The framework finds theoretically interpretable variation in $S_b$ and establishes $I_b$ as a reliable source of dyadic variance across concepts. Results replicate across three encoders varying in architecture and capacity, providing a reproducible and scalable instrument for the empirical study of meaning variation.

title: Toeplitz determinants for starlike mappings of order α in several complex variables
abstract: Let $F(z)=zf(z)$, where $f$ is a normalized scalar holomorphic function on the unit ball $\mathbb B$ of a complex Banach space $X$ or on the unit polydisk $\mathbb U^n$ of $\mathbb{C}^n$. We establish sharp bounds for two Toeplitz determinants involving the second, third and fourth Fréchet derivatives of $F$ when $F$ is starlike of order $α$, $0\leqα<1$. The first bound is sharp for the full range $0\leqα<1$, while the second is sharp for $0\leqα\leq 2/3$. The extremal mappings are explicitly identified, confirming the sharpness of the estimates.

title: Revisited Support Vector Machines: A Unified Joint Optimization Framework with Nyström Approximation for Scalable Adaptive Learning
abstract: The theoretical elegance of Support Vector Machines (SVMs), grounded in statistical learning theory, establishes them as a reference for robust classification. However, in the era of Big Data, classical SVMs face two major bottlenecks: the prohibitive cubic complexity $\mathcal{O}(N^3)$ of training and the rigidity of static kernels. Traditional methodologies treat kernel selection as a discrete, "brute-force" GridSearch problem, effectively decoupling the learning of data representation from the optimization of the decision boundary. This paper proposes a paradigm shift with a so-called "Revisited SVM", a unified framework that recasts the learning process as a continuous %bi-level joint optimization problem. We derive a novel objective function $J(α, θ)$ that allows for the simultaneous optimization of dual Lagrange multipliers and kernel hyper-parameters. To solve this challenging non-convex problem efficiently, we introduce a hybrid Block Coordinate Ascent (BCA) algorithm, tightly integrated with Nyström-based low-rank approximation, which drastically reduces computational complexity to $\mathcal{O}(Nm)$. Extensive experiments conducted across four heterogeneous domains (Bioinformatics, Finance, Cybersecurity, and Computer Vision) demonstrate that our approach not only matches but often exceeds exhaustive GridSearch accuracy, while delivering training speedups of up to 100x. Notably, on the complex NSL-KDD intrusion detection dataset, our adaptive kernel approach achieves 96.25\% accuracy compared to a mere 50\% for standard baselines, proving its unique ability to model complex non-linear manifolds in high-dimensional spaces. We validate our results using rigorous statistical tests and provide a theoretical convergence analysis of the proposed algorithm.

title: The Imperishable Record, Forgiveness, and the Future of Criminal Justice
abstract: Digital technologies can preserve records of wrongdoing indefinitely, and AI can give those records continuing influence over a person's future. We describe this condition as the eternal data present and argue that it threatens the possibility of forgiveness. In criminal justice, formal punishment has an end, whereas the harms caused by the continued use of criminal records may not. Drawing on Hegel's account of the "hard heart" and Arendt's account of the irreversibility of action, we distinguish two dangers that digital systems can combine. People may be permanently identified with what they have done, and acts that cannot be undone may continue to determine what happens to them. We propose a right to remain unfinished, supported by rights to limits on the weight given to older records, to re-evaluation in light of personal change, to reassessment of inferences that affect their lives, and to time limits on the use of records in specified decisions. These proposals extend the ethics of AI beyond accuracy, transparency, and non-discrimination to address how long past wrongdoing should be allowed to govern a person's life.

title: Witness Languages for Pumping Lemmata
abstract: In 2022 Dassow and Jecker started investigations on the operational complexity of the pumping constant w.r.t.~two pumping lemmata. Since then, the research on pumping lemmata emerged to several variants for regular as well as context-free languages. Within this work, we further investigate the \emph{witnesses} of regular languages (firstly introduced by Rauch) w.r.t.~different pumping lemmata: For a language $L$ and a minimal pumping constant $K$, a \emph{witness} of a language is a word that cannot be \emph{pumped} by $K$ w.r.t.~the given pumping lemma. Here, the pumping constant is minimal if for all smaller numbers, the pumping lemma condition is not satisfied. Alongside combinatorial investigations on (unary) witness languages, we introduce and study the measure of scattered factor distance, which is related to minimal pumping constants. We present bounds on minimal pumping constants by the scattered factor distance and show that deciding, given two regular languages, whether one of them is equal to the witness language of the second is \coNP-complete.

title: Large Decision Models: Repurposing Large Language Models as Single-Pass Decision Makers
abstract: Large language models make decisions through parallel prefill and sequential decoding. Although effective, this approach incurs decoding costs and does not explicitly expose decision probabilities. Existing task-specific classifiers require per-task training and offer limited generalization to unseen decision schemas. We propose Large Decision Models (LDMs), repurposing language models to return explicit probabilities over labels specified at run time using one prefill forward pass. We first adapt models to this interface through Diverse Decision Supervision (DDS), covering varied domains, rules and labels. To further narrow the performance gap to a reasoning model, Self-Posed Reasoning Distillation (SPRD) adds tasks generated by a frozen teacher, filters them for answer consistency, and trains on label distributions obtained from repeated teacher reasoning. We evaluate on DecisionVista, pairing new-schema tests with held-out human-labelled sources. Across three base models, the recipe improves accuracy over a step-matched baseline by 1.8 and 1.5 percentage points, respectively, achieving a 182-fold speedup in latency over reasoning rollout on Gemma-4-31B. Reasoning remains stronger on the new-schema test, motivating a confidence router for uncertain decisions. On development sets, routing recovers a median 92% of reasoning's accuracy advantage while generating 27-58% of its tokens. Code is available at https://github.com/JianhuiWei7/LDM.

title: From Observations to Authorized Actions: Measuring Source Information in Android Agents
abstract: Android agents read content from applications and web pages and act on it with the user's authority, yet they cannot reliably tell where that content came from -- its source, the application or document that supplied it. The WebView accessibility fields we inspected expose the host application but omit the document origins available inside the browser, so an agent reading through this interface cannot check which document supplied an object; a limited reproduction on an unmodified WebView yields the same finding. We build and separately evaluate two prototypes to examine how source information supports authorization. Our application-source monitor withholds side-effecting calls whose signed source record contains an untrusted application. With the source set derived from the OS accessibility log, it blocked every selected attack write in the tested runs, but it also withheld benign sends issued after reading untrusted content, flagged benign tasks that use external content, and carried source records into a later clean task. Our WebView source-reference gate uses records from a modified browser to check object origins and reference lifetime through direct calls; in a separate 24-trial evaluation, the live agent selected no disallowed object. Supporting benchmark and planner measurements characterize textual argument matches and attacker-target selection, without establishing causal dataflow or a controlled model ranking. The prototypes are not an integrated defense: the WebView gate still lacks authenticated browser delivery and atomic capture of selected bytes and origin. Together, the results show which source information the tested policies need and why it must stay linked to the object used in execution.

title: Data Portability Revisited: Toward the Human-Centric, AI-Driven Data Ecosystems of Tomorrow
abstract: This Article critically examines the contemporary regulatory framework and discourse surrounding data portability in the United States. Using recent regulatory developments in the European Union as an illustration, this Article suggests that although data access and portability are identified as vital issues in multiple policy instruments, in its current iteration, at least, legal conceptions of portability continue to reinforce the interests of service providers and data controller enterprises rather than individual end users. This Article argues that a paradigm shift toward a more human-centric data approach to data governance must occur, under which data would be recognized as fundamental to an individual's identity in a digital age. Therefore, it should be placed in the hands of individuals rather than service providers or data controller enterprises. This Article considers technical and market trends in the European Union that reveal and facilitate such a change. It suggests that regulatory frameworks should better align with these technological and market developments to encourage change-inducing trends among market actors. In short, this Article identifies a transformative approach to data portability that empowers individuals with the freedom and ability to aggregate their data in secure personal spaces under their control or dominion. Such a human-centric perspective on data portability is crucial in building Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered applications for individual consumers that can pave the way for the human-centric, AI-driven data ecosystems of the future.

title: Symmetric Bases and $\ell^p$ Embeddings in Musielak--Orlicz Sequence Spaces under $δ_2$
abstract: We study isomorphic embeddings into Musielak-Orlicz sequence spaces \(\ell_Φ\), where the normalized generating sequence \(Φ=\{ϕ_n\}\) satisfies the \(δ_2\) condition. Using admissible normalized blocks, we construct an associated limiting family \(\mathcal C_{Φ,τ}\) of Orlicz functions. If a Banach space \(X\) with a symmetric basis embeds into \(\ell_Φ\), then there is a function \(ψ\in\mathcal C_{Φ,τ}\) such that the basis of \(X\) is equivalent to the canonical basis of \(\ell_ψ\). An Orlicz sequence space \(\ell_ψ\) embeds if and only if \(ψ\) is equivalent near zero to a member of \(\mathcal C_{Φ,τ}\); in particular, \(\ell^p\) embeds exactly when such a member is equivalent to \(t^p\). Assuming differentiability of the generators on a common interval near zero, we also derive the necessary bound \(p\leq b_{Φ,(c_n),δ}\), where the upper growth index incorporates the summable errors in the \(δ_2\) condition. The same index yields cotype \(q\) for every \(q\geq2\) with \(q>b_{Φ,(c_n),δ}\). Examples with nonuniform growth and lacunary weights illustrate this bound. For alternating Nakano exponents, the explicit limiting family gives a sharper restriction than the index alone. For general Nakano exponents, we recover the known exact cotype criterion, including attainment of the optimal exponent. For weighted Orlicz spaces, we express the cotype criterion through summable scalar errors and recover the formula using the global upper growth index when \(w\in\mathcal A\).

title: Federated Semantic Residuals for Multimodal Recommendation
abstract: Federated Recommendation Systems (FedRSs) learn collaborative scores from interaction histories on device and rank items by them, so a higher score means a higher rank. Item text and images add semantic information that can reorder the list. Existing Federated Multimodal Recommenders (FedMRs) fuse this content into their models, which can obscure how content reorders the list. We therefore propose the SEmantic Residual Adapter (SERA), which keeps content out of an existing FedRS and adds semantic residual scores to its collaborative scores. Content can then lift an item above another only when its semantic residual score exceeds the other's by more than their collaborative score gap. This score grows with the item's content similarity to the user's interaction history and is capped at a residual bound. We prove that for any content, an item can enter the list only if its collaborative score is within twice this bound of the lowest one in the list. A larger bound lets content lift more items, including irrelevant ones, so the bound trades off how far content reaches against accuracy. With a validated bound, SERA improves all three FedRSs on all six datasets without adding personalized parameters. It outperforms FedMRs in most comparisons and lifts some FedRSs above centralized baselines.

title: Pathwise Alignment for Collaborative Filtering: Bilateral Conditional Flow Regularization
abstract: Collaborative filtering predicts user-item interactions from implicit feedback. We focus on matrix factorization (MF) trained with the Bayesian Personalized Ranking loss. This loss updates each user embedding only through that user's observed items and sampled negatives, so sparse feedback gives MF few constraints. To constrain each user through other users, we propose Pathwise Alignment for Collaborative Filtering (PACF), which trains MF with one network shared by all training pairs. At points between user and item embeddings, a flow matching term trains the network to predict the user-to-item step, reversed and scaled for sampled negatives. A trajectory consistency term pulls each user's predicted path to end at the observed item. Both terms update the embeddings, so the network is discarded after training, thereby maintaining the efficiency of MF at inference. We prove that a network with bounded sensitivity to its input point accurately fits users who share an item only if their embeddings are close, so these users constrain one another. Against eleven discriminative and generative baselines, PACF achieves the highest performance on all seven datasets. Its relative gains over MF are largest where feedback is sparsest. The shared network thus supplies the missing constraints through other users.

title: Orbital stability of solitary wave solutions of the derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation in the endpoint case
abstract: In this paper, we consider the orbital stability of solitary waves for the derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation $$iq_t+q_{xx}+i\partial_x\bigl(|q|^2q\bigr)=0, \quad (t,x)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}.$$ For the endpoint solitary waves satisfying $c>0$ and $c^2=4ω$, we prove the orbital stability in $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ without any additional assumptions. The proof uses conservation of mass and the second Hamiltonian $\mathcal{H}_2$ to keep the Bäcklund-transformed solution small in $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ uniformly in time. We establish an inverse Bäcklund compactness result to reconstruct the algebraic solitary wave as the spectral zero approaches the negative real axis.

title: Phase transitions and quasinormal modes of Euler-Heisenberg-dilaton AdS black holes
abstract: In this paper, we study phase transitions and scalar quasinormal modes(QNMs) of magnetically charged Euler--Heisenberg-dilaton AdS black holes in the extended phase space. We classify the horizon structures for all three signs of the EH coupling and derive the extended first law when the pressure and coupling are varied. For negative coupling, the physical branch exhibits a Van der Waals-like small/large black-hole transition. Using the improved asymptotic iteration method, we find two separated QNM trajectories below the critical pressure, whereas they merge into one continuous curve at the critical point. The GHS limit and the positive couplings considered here do not produce a finite-radius critical point.

title: CacheLink: Functional KV Transport for Zero-Prefill Cross-Model Context Handoff
abstract: KV caches make long-context serving efficient by reusing past computation, but model switching breaks this reuse and forces the receiver to prefill the context again. We study \emph{zero-prefill cross-model context handoff}: translating a sender cache into a receiver-compatible state so that the receiver can continue directly without prefilling same context. Existing affine transport methods show that receiver KV states can be substantially reconstructed from sender caches. However, through extensive analyses, we find that reconstruction fidelity is a poor proxy for receiver utility. Similar K/V reconstruction errors can lead to substantially different attention patterns, predictive distributions, and downstream accuracy, because conventional reconstruction objectives overlook the query-dependent functional importance of K and V in receiver attention. We thus introduce CACHELINK, which learns a coupled K/V correction through the receiver behavior directly. Across four independently trained sender--receiver pairs and seven evaluation panels, CACHELINK improves the equal-weight mean over all methods for every pair. In matched diagnostics, CACHELINK changes K/V squared error by less than 0.4% while substantially changing receiver attention and next-token behavior. At 32K context, it reduces handoff latency by up to $7.27\times$ relative to receiver re-prefill. Our findings verify that reconstruction fidelity alone is insufficient and that preserving the receiver computation induced by the transported cache is important for effective cross-model KV transport.

title: From Product Evidence to Access Rights: Auditing and Routing Non-Firm Grid Connections
abstract: Non-firm connection products can accelerate grid access while reinforcements are delayed, but their planning value depends on evidence supporting the contractual promise. We develop a one-way evidence-to-access framework for calendarized products. Stage A constructs and fixes directional restriction calendars from public residual-load and day-ahead price-timing signals. Stage B audits the submitted calendar and one bounded common repair, tests joint threshold attainability under the shared annual budget, and applies an aggregation-aware Power Transfer Distribution Factor (PTDF) certificate. Stage C treats the resulting ledger as fixed in queue-aware allocation and intervention planning. In the primary policy-package evaluation, the evidence-supported menu returns the same $2.119$~GW allocation as firm-only access, whereas authorizing the uniformly derated fallback raises awards to $6.442$~GW and reduces backlog from $136.076$ to $113.601$~GW-years; all $4.489$~GW of non-firm awards use the fallback. In a target-free matched control, evidence-routed and state-blind fallback menus attain primary objectives equivalent within EUR~1 and return the same accepted applicants, award years, routes, and intervention portfolio. Thus, in the reported testbed, fallback authorization rather than calendar-specific evidence support drives the access-volume effect.

title: The Brakke-BV structure of flat flows
abstract: We show that, in ambient dimension at most seven, varifold limits of the minimizing movements scheme introduced by Almgren--Taylor--Wang and Luckhaus--Sturzenhecker are integral Brakke flows. As a consequence, we show that $L^1$-limit points of the scheme, usually known as flat flows, are generalized BV flows. The result is unconditional and, in particular, remains valid even in the absence of energy convergence and in the presence of fattening.

title: Structured Stateful Relational Scripts with a High-Quality Dataset for Multi-Shot Audio-Visual Video Generation
abstract: Coherent multi-shot audio-visual video generation requires maintaining consistent identities while depicting evolving states and coordinating sounds across shot boundaries. Although dense captions describe individual shots in detail, they rarely specify which entities persist, how their states change, or which entities and actions produce sounds. To address this limitation, we propose Structured Stateful Relational Scripts (SSRS), a textual supervision representation that separates persistent entity and voice identities from shot-specific visual and auditory states. SSRS explicitly encodes sound-source bindings and temporal relations, while a global audio-visual event sequence connects local actions and sounds, including events that continue across shot boundaries. We further introduce MSAV-Script-100K, a large-scale dataset of curated multi-shot audio-visual videos paired with detailed SSRS annotations, enabling models to learn identity persistence, state transitions, and event continuity from structured supervision. Experiments demonstrate improvements in cross-shot consistency, adherence to specified state changes, and audio-visual alignment, highlighting the effectiveness of our SSRS and MSAV-Script-100K for coherent multi-shot audio-visual generation. Our proposed dataset is available at \href{https://huggingface.co/datasets/shenlehan/MSAV-Script-100K}{MSAV-Script-100K}.

title: REPRO: Reflective Evolutionary Prompt Optimizer for Automated LLM Red-Teaming
abstract: Safety-aligned large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to adversarial prompts that bypass their safety training. Existing automated red-teaming methods either require privileged access unavailable in production, rely on manually engineered per-model templates, or optimize a single objective without population-level diversity. We present REPRO (Reflective Evolutionary Prompt Optimization), a pure black-box framework that discovers adversarial prompts through evolutionary optimization driven entirely by a compressed open-weight 7B reflective model on a single consumer GPU. REPRO introduces two mechanisms absent from prior work, both isolated in a component ablation: semantic crossover, an LLM-guided multi-parent recombination operator, and Bayesian strategy selection via Thompson Sampling informed by structured failure analysis. We catalog REPRO's behavior on AdvBench, JailbreakBench, and HarmBench across 36 target models from 11 families, including GPT-5-nano, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Gemini-2.5-Pro, and Grok-4.1. Under our protocol REPRO reaches 100\% attack success rate (ASR) on every evaluated target in a single turn, at a median of 24 target queries per behavior. Two properties of the protocol qualify that figure. The judge scoring candidates during optimization also produces the reported ASR, and search halts when it accepts, so ASR reports whether search succeeded within the iteration budget rather than success at a fixed budget. All baseline figures are transcribed from their original papers, which use different judges, budgets, and model versions. We therefore present this as a catalog of model coverage under one protocol rather than a head-to-head ranking, and develop both qualifications in the paper.

title: SARATHI: Decoupled Data-Free Probing and Adaptive Reconstruction for Structured LLM Pruning
abstract: Structured pruning reduces the inference cost of large language models (LLMs) by permanently removing neurons and weight rows, yielding dense, hardware-agnostic speedup. Existing post-training methods couple neuron selection and weight reconstruction through a shared calibration dataset, introducing domain bias and out-of-memory failures at high sparsity. We propose SARATHI, a framework that decouples these two stages. A data-free \emph{NMF Residual Subspace Probe} scores neurons using intrinsic weight geometry, without accessing any calibration data, and carries a formal connection to Robust PCA. \emph{Adaptive OBS} then reconstructs the pruned weights with a localized calibration batch, operating in $\mathcal{O}(d^2)$ peak memory per layer and eliminating the global memory bottleneck of coupled methods. A \emph{Bias Shift Compensation} step corrects systematic activation drift in post-LayerNorm architectures that would otherwise cause perplexity collapse at high sparsity. Experiments across six models from two architecture families (gated and non-gated FFN) at 15--40\% sparsity show that SARATHI achieves competitive perplexity and matches or exceeds existing structured pruning baselines on zero-shot accuracy.

title: Semantically Steerable Image Tokenization
abstract: Adaptive image tokenizers compress an image into a variable number of tokens matched to its complexity, and recent work makes this allocation controllable: conditioned on a target reconstruction error, the tokenizer itself decides how many tokens an image needs. However, the fidelity measure guiding this allocation shapes which aspects of the image are preserved under compression. The pixel-wise error used in prior work is blind to the spatial structure that carries an image's meaning, and under heavy compression such tokenizers are prone to abruptly discarding tokens that encode essential content. We introduce GIST (Guided Image Semantic Tokenizer), an adaptive tokenizer that can be steered toward a requested semantic fidelity. Its token allocation is jointly controlled by pixel-level and semantic target errors, with semantic error measured in the feature space of a frozen DINOv3 encoder. This joint control enables semantic protection: with the semantic target fixed at zero, the reconstruction target can be relaxed to discard pixel detail while preserving what the image depicts. In a controlled comparison on ImageNet-100, GIST outperforms its pixel-controlled counterpart KARL at every token count, with up to $30\%$ lower LPIPS and $37\%$ lower DreamSim. On average, lowering its semantic target reduces LPIPS $2\times$ faster per token than lowering the reconstruction target, and up to $5\times$ in the low-token regime. Semantic fidelity is thus an effective control signal for adaptive tokenization: it lets a tokenizer see, and so preserve, what an image depicts.

title: Robust Proportionality Axioms for Additive Utilities
abstract: We study the model of participatory budgeting, in which a subset of candidates is selected subject to a budget constraint. Voters express their preferences by assigning a numerical utility to each candidate. Our focus is on formal analysis of proportionality, a central notion of fairness in multi-winner elections. Intuitively, proportionality means that each group of voters should influence the election outcome roughly in proportion to its size. Recent "plus" axioms of proportionality are particularly appealing notions: they are verifiable in polynomial time, and they provide strong representation guarantees without requiring groups of voters to have cohesive preferences. However, their existing formulations are restricted to approval-based preferences. We generalise extended justified representation plus (EJR+), and Core plus (Core+) to general additive utilities. Our approach builds on a payment-based interpretation of proportionality: candidates' costs are shared among their supporters, with the aim of balancing voters' total payments.

title: On a derived equivalence classification of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type
abstract: We consider a family $(Λ_λ)_{λ\in \Bbbk^\times}$ of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type over an algebraically closed field $\Bbbk$, where $\Bbbk^\times:= \Bbbk\setminus \{0\}$, and for each $λ\in \Bbbk^\times$, $Λ_λ$ is socle equivalent to $Λ_1$, which is the trivial extension of a hereditary algebra of type $\tilde{A}$. We compute their Hochschild cohomologies, which shows that $Λ_λ$ is not derived equivalent to $Λ_1$ if $λ\neq 1$. This means that a derived equivalence classification of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type given by Bocian--Holm--Skowro{\' n}ski is not complete.

title: OceanFlow: Coherent Flow Matching for Probabilistic Ocean Modeling
abstract: Probabilistic ocean modeling is essential for risk-aware marine operations, climate analysis, and scientific decision-making, where downstream decisions depend on the conditional distribution of future ocean states rather than a single deterministic trajectory. Recent data-driven ocean models have made deterministic global ocean modeling increasingly accurate and efficient, but probabilistic ocean modeling remains underdeveloped. Specifically, perturbation-driven ensembles can create spread without explicitly optimizing the joint distribution of their members, often yielding poor calibration and physical inconsistency. To address these issues, we propose OceanFlow, a coherent flow matching framework for probabilistic global ocean modeling. OceanFlow first establishes a sharp, stable mean anchor for the conditional ensemble. Flow matching then learns a coherent state-conditioned pathwise law that jointly reshapes the residual distribution around this anchor at each transition, preserving the predictive center while refining state-dependent uncertainty. We further introduce a Factorized Dynamics Operator (FDO), which combines factorized transitions with a learned state-conditioned response to parameterize the mean anchor and residual-flow velocity. Extensive experiments show that OceanFlow improves ensemble-mean accuracy, probabilistic reliability, and physical-consistency diagnostics over competitive baselines, supporting coherent flow matching as an effective route toward data-driven probabilistic ocean modeling. Code is available at https://github.com/YuanGao-YG/OceanFlow.

title: From Microresonator to Packaged Microcomb System: Fiber-Coupled Module and System Integration
abstract: We demonstrate a compact and robust soliton microcomb source designed for field-deployable operation. A directly fiber-coupled SiN microresonator was integrated with precise thermal control into a palm-sized module, reducing the footprint and volume by 16- and 81-fold, respectively. The module, together with the laser sources and optical amplifiers required for microcomb generation, was further integrated into a 19-inch rack-mounted enclosure, achieving system-level footprint and volume reductions of 2.3- and 3.7-fold, respectively. The packaged system achieved a 90% manual startup success rate and maintained continuous soliton operation for 18.8 days, while remaining operational under substantial temperature variations. A state-based automated startup scheme using discrete microcomb-state evaluation achieved single-soliton generation without manual intervention with success rates of 50% within 2 min and 60% within 3 min. Moreover, automated soliton initiation and sustained operation were demonstrated while the packaged microresonator module was directly subjected to random mechanical vibration. These results provide a practical platform for compact, robust, and field-deployable microcomb sources.

title: Improving the Bounds on Approximating Weighted Maximin Share for Chores
abstract: We investigate the problem of allocating indivisible chores among agents with arbitrary positive weights and additive nonnegative cost functions. An allocation is said to be $α$-weighted-maximin-share (WMMS) fair if the cost incurred by each agent is at most $α$ times her weighted maximin share. We establish that every instance admits a $4.124234528$-WMMS allocation. Moreover, for instances in which all weights and costs are rational numbers represented in binary, we give an algorithm that computes a $4.12424$-WMMS allocation in time polynomial in the number of agents, the number of chores, and the total binary encoding length of the input. Complementing these upper bounds, we construct a family of instances with strictly positive, identically ordered costs for which the optimal WMMS approximation factors converge to $e$. Together, our results substantially narrow the previously best-known gap of $[2,12]$ established by Li et al.~\cite{LWX26} to $[e,4.12424]$.

title: Crystals and the parabolicity conjecture
abstract: These notes introduce crystals and crystalline Dieudonné theory through the example of abelian varieties. After discussing $p$-divisible groups, $F$-isocrystals, slope filtrations, and overconvergence, we explain the parabolicity theorem for $F$-isocrystals and some of its applications to monodromy and Hecke orbits. Two appendices formulate research projects on isocrystals over formal schemes and on monodromy beyond the constant-slope setting. The exposition is intended for readers familiar with basic algebraic geometry and the étale and fppf topologies; prior knowledge of Witt vectors is helpful but not required.

title: GNFormer: Gaussian Neural Field Transformer for Efficient Camera-based Occupancy Prediction
abstract: Camera-based occupancy prediction provides geometric and semantic scene understanding for robot perception and has been adopted in autonomous vehicle and UAV perception systems. Gaussian primitives offer a promising alternative by potentially representing only occupied regions, thereby concentrating computation and representational capacity where needed and reducing wasted computation and memory in empty space. However, existing Gaussian-based methods suffer from poor primitive utilization, as ineffective training objectives leave some Gaussians in empty space, while the limited expressiveness of Gaussian functions restricts their ability to model complex shapes. To address these limitations, we propose a novel 3D representation, Gaussian Neural Field (GNF), which can accurately map voxel positions to semantic occupancies. In GNF, Gaussians and a neural network jointly parameterize the field, where the Gaussians define its spatial support and provide features for neural decoding, while the neural network enables more expressive occupancy modeling than Gaussian functions alone. We further develop the Gaussian Neural Field Transformer (GNFormer), a streamlined and flexible method that predicts GNFs for camera-based occupancy prediction. Across Occ-ScanNet, SSCBench-KITTI-360, and nuScenes-SurroundOcc benchmarks, GNFormer achieves the highest IoU and mIoU and the fastest inference among the compared single-frame methods. In the experiments, GNFormer can represent indoor and outdoor scenes with only 256 and 1024 Gaussians, respectively, substantially fewer primitives than prior Gaussian-based methods. The code will be released.

title: Rethinking Evidence Modeling: Context-Coupled Graph Learning for Multimodal Recommendation
abstract: Multimodal graph recommendation integrates observed interactions with item images and text to learn user preferences. These inputs constitute Semantic-Behavioral Evidence (SBE). Many existing graph methods incorporate collaborative and multimodal semantic relations, yet their aggregation and state updates remain context-separated, limiting the continuous composition of preference evidence across layers and the joint use of multiple sources. To address this limitation, we propose CC-MGRec, a context-coupled graph learning method that organizes SBE within a common graph learning context for cross-relation modeling and compositional propagation. Its context-coupled multimodal graph integrates user-item collaborative relations and item-item semantic relations, coordinating their message scales through joint normalization. Recommendation-grounded semantic calibration uses training behavior to adjust semantic neighbor weights while preserving normalized collaborative propagation coefficients. Collaborative-semantic compositional propagation updates shared node states layer by layer to continuously compose collaborative and multimodal semantic evidence, implicitly forming Preference Evidence Chains (PECs), including collaborative-semantic and visual-textual PECs. Joint execution of relation messages on the same shared node states within each layer preserves propagation outputs while reducing intermediate output processing and fusion overhead. We provide theoretical analysis of the proposed mechanisms. Experiments on three Amazon datasets demonstrate improved recommendation quality and faster inference during graph propagation.

title: BOLD PSF: Impact of k-space trajectories and timing on the depiction of T2* contrast
abstract: The timing of BOLD-fMRI is typically chosen such that TE matches T2*. This assumes contrast being exclusively elicited by signal differences at TE. While sensible for short or TE-symmetric readouts, such as EPIs, it oversimplifies contrast generation for longer or TE-asymmetric trajectories, such as spirals. We propose the concept of a BOLD PSF for a more comprehensive perspective on the imaging characteristics of a functional experiment. Our findings indicate that TE can be reduced for spiral-out without sacrificing BOLD-sensitivity when compared to EPI. Furthermore, we characterize the intrinsic trade-off between specificity and resolution of the BOLD response under varying TE.

title: A linear independence criterion for $p$-adic Hurwitz zeta values at odd integers
abstract: In this article, a new criterion is established to obtain the linear independence of some values of the $p$-adic Hurwitz zeta function at odd integers $s\geq 3$. We generalize a theorem of F.~Beukers, who gave, among others, an alternative proof---using Padé approximation theory---of a result originally due to F.~Calegari on the irrationality of the $p$-adic Riemann zeta value $ζ_p(3)$ for $p = 2, 3$. To prove our main theorem, we work in a general setting, where we construct and study new Padé approximants of Laurent series satisfying the functional equation $f(z) = f(1-z)$. This complements our previous work on the linear independence of $p$-adic polygamma values.

title: Quantum circuit representation and incomplete Bell measurements in Compton scattering
abstract: We formulate massless tree-level Compton scattering as an effective two-qubit operation on electron and photon helicities. In the Bell basis, the scattering map separates into two parity sectors and admits a simple quantum circuit representation with one nonunitary filter. After Kraus normalization, this filter defines an unsharp incomplete Bell measurement that distinguishes the two Bell-parity sectors but not the relative Bell label within each sector. We further show that the incomplete measurement alone does not surpass the classical teleportation threshold, whereas a subsequent complete Bell-basis readout enables unit conditional teleportation fidelity.

title: A Step in the Right Place: Understanding and Optimizing Timestep Placement in Continuous Diffusion Language Models
abstract: Continuous diffusion language models represent an emerging paradigm for language modeling. They generate text in parallel by iteratively refining continuous representations and mapping them back to tokens through a decoder. However, realizing the efficiency advantage of parallel generation requires maintaining generation quality with only a few denoising steps. Even when the number of steps is fixed, their placement along the denoising trajectory remains flexible. In this paper, we demonstrate that changing timestep placement alone can substantially alter the final latent representations and thereby affect the decoded token distributions. Building on these findings, we introduce StepTune, an algorithm that searches for timestep placements that improve generation quality. The search is conducted on a small calibration set and guided by a language-aware objective, with the model and sampling budget fixed. Once calibrated, the timestep placement is fixed and reused across inputs. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in unconditional generation perplexity and conditional task metrics across all evaluated sampling budgets. In particular, StepTune enables 16-step sampling with a frozen model to outperform its native 64-step baseline on both XSum summarization and WMT14 translation and reduces end-to-end latency by approximately $3.8\times$. These results establish timestep placement as a practical means of improving the quality-efficiency trade-off in continuous diffusion language models.

title: A Viscoelastic Wave Equation with Nonlinear Damping and Supercritical Variable-Exponent Logarithmic Sources
abstract: We investigate a viscoelastic wave equation with nonlinear variable-exponent damping and a variable-exponent logarithmic source, allowing supercritical growth. The main difficulties arise from the failure of the source to map the energy space into $L^2(Ω)$, the sign-changing logarithmic potential, and the lack of Sobolev control of the displacement for supercritical damping. Under an exponent condition linking the source and damping exponents, we prove local existence, an energy identity, and a continuation criterion. We prove finite-time blow-up for nontrivial solutions with nonpositive shifted initial energy. We also establish a blow-up criterion based on a sufficiently large initial displacement--velocity pairing, with a threshold depending on the positive part of the shifted initial energy, and derive an explicit upper bound for the lifespan. This criterion allows us to construct blow-up data at every prescribed level of the original energy. For initial data in a suitable stable region, solutions exist globally. For damping within the Sobolev range, a general relaxation condition yields energy decay estimates that include exponential and polynomial rates. Beyond this range, a time-weighted displacement estimate and a splitting of the memory integral give logarithmic decay.

title: Agent-Canary-Mas: End-to-End Evaluation of Protocol Risk in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Agent-to-agent protocols allow LLM agents to discover peers, exchange results, and coordinate tool use. A locally successful protocol attack, however, may be rejected by a later agent or propagated into a consequential task decision. Measuring local exploitability alone leaves this difference unresolved and provides limited evidence about which participant caused the final outcome. We present Agent-Canary-Mas, an end-to-end evaluation system that follows protocol risk through long-horizon multi-agent tasks. It covers five risk classes and 13 subclasses across A2A, ANP, and BCS, with 975 matched malicious--benign task pairs in five business domains. A shared OpenClaw framework runs autonomous, tool-using agents under different underlying models while preserving the task and execution setup. Matched runs separate local protocol success from downstream consequences; retained evidence connects participant selection, message consumption, tool activity, and task-state changes. We further evaluate a protocol-context Guard that checks an object's authority at consequential handoffs. Across three model conditions, local attack success is frequently at or above 90%, while consequence conversion ranges from 7.1% to 100.0%. Cross-agent evidence raises macro-averaged Audit-F1 from 29.7% to 95.5%. On Finance tasks, the Guard lowers average ASR from 86.1% to 53.8% and PTCR from 65.5% to 31.2%, with a measurable completion tradeoff. These results show that protocol risk depends on how agents use exchanged objects throughout the task, and that evaluating this path supports more informative risk assessment, attribution, and defense.

title: Breakdown of thermalization in quantum spin systems with long-range interactions
abstract: Quantum thermalization of closed systems -- i.e. the relaxation of local properties to their thermodynamic value along the Hamiltonian evolution -- is generically expected in non-integrable systems at finite energy density. In this work we show that quantum spin systems with at least one spin component coupled through long-range ferromagnetic interactions, and a second spin component coupled to a field, cannot in general thermalize to a paramagnetic state whenever they have a finite, negative energy per spin. The long-range interactions we consider decay as a power law of the distance, $\sim r^{-α}$ with $α< d$, where $d$ is the number of spatial dimensions of the system. The lack of thermalization is generic to an infinite family of Hamiltonians, and it is not associated to any form of integrability. It can instead be understood by the anomalous features of the thermodynamics of the system in the paramagnetic phase, which cannot be reflected in the properties of the eigenstates. This leads to a breakdown of eigenstate typicality and of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis. Interestingly, the non-thermal states emerging at long times in the dynamics display long-range multipartite entanglement, elevating the breakdown of thermalization to a resource.

title: Identifying and Measuring Treatment-Effect Heterogeneity across Sites through Within-Site Randomization
abstract: Parallel cluster-randomized trials can identify mean effects by site characteristics and risk differences between fixed predictors, while leaving residual heterogeneity and absolute prediction risk (mean squared error of site-effect predictions) unidentified. We acquire missing same-site cross-arm information by randomizing participants within selected sites. Under randomized site selection with compatible participant reference distributions and intervention versions, we characterize necessary and sufficient observation patterns for quadratic targets in a model with unrestricted joint distributions of site response means. From finite independent participant samples, we construct unbiased moments and exact covariances.
