However, language agents traditionally communicate via text exchange, which introduces a bottleneck in information transfer and adds prefill latency for downstream agents. Recent work proposes that directly sharing the key-value (KV) cache between language models can enable efficient latent collaboration, entirely bypassing standard text-based communication. To enable latent communication between heterogeneous models of different sizes, prior work introduces trained fusion adapters for each model pair, which limits practical deployment. We introduce CacheFuse, a training-free method which demonstrates that augmenting a downstream model with an upstream model's KV cache using linear interpolation consistently enables superior performance than the standalone downstream model can achieve. We systematically analyze CacheFuse across four reasoning and knowledge benchmarks and demonstrate up to 8.6 percentage points higher accuracy compared to single-model baselines and up to 12.2x TTFT speedup compared to text-based communication in multi-model inference.

title: Esports World Model Dataset
abstract: Interactive world models must capture how multiple participants jointly change a shared environment while observing different parts of it. Competitive games make this challenge concrete: players cooperate and compete, while fog of war, team vision and camera placement determine what each can see. Modeling these interactions requires data that connect individual observations and actions to shared state and events. We introduce the Esports World Model Dataset (EWM), a collection of human gameplay spanning StarCraft II, Dota 2 and Counter-Strike 2, with 3,053 games and maps and approximately 4,880 player-view hours, including estimated hours for the ongoing CS2 extension. It includes 4,628 completed StarCraft II views, all ten perspectives for 303 Dota 2 matches, and up to ten views per round in CS2. Across these views, replay-clock alignment connects rendered video with game-native actions, structured state and events from the same match. The three games expose complementary observation conditions: private fog of war, shared team vision and first-person viewpoints. In StarCraft II, player-specific entity records further distinguish live observations from remembered snapshots and link co-observed entities across opposing views. Together with temporal alignment, these records allow researchers to distinguish legitimate information differences from disagreement about shared state. By connecting human decisions, shared dynamics and player-specific information, EWM supports research toward jointly controlled multiplayer world models and interactive environments populated by teammates and opponents learned from human play.

title: Interactive 4D Volumetric Liquid Forecasting under Moving-Solid Interaction
abstract: We propose the task of Interactive 4D Volumetric Liquid Forecasting: predicting the spatiotemporal evolution of a future dense 3D liquid velocity field conditioned on how a solid object moves through it. This task provides an upstream physical forecasting primitive for systems that need to reason about motion-conditioned liquid response, including robotic liquid manipulation, digital twins, and rigid-fluid video generation. Existing works have made efforts in predicting flow around static or prescribed solid geometries and synthesizing visually plausible fluid motion. Yet these approaches provide limited coverage for interactive liquid dynamics, as they are not capable of forecasting how a moving solid induces a future full-domain liquid response. In this forecasting scenario, the hydrodynamic effect is condensed near an evolving liquid-solid interface, but the prediction target is a global spatiotemporal rollout. To address this challenge, we propose a two-level recurrent forecasting framework, TIDE/TIDES: TIDE isolates localized interface-driven forecasting, while TIDES adds transport-aware coupling and explicit stabilization to reduce accumulated rollout error. Across adapted neighboring baselines, controlled component ablations, motion/size OOD tests, and long-horizon evaluation, TIDES achieves the best forecasting performance and the ablations identify localized interaction, transport coupling, and stabilization as the key contributors. Together, our task formulation, benchmark, and TIDE/TIDES study establish a controlled foundation for moving-solid-conditioned dense liquid forecasting. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/jongwonryu/TIDE-TIDES.

title: Length-scale dependence of collective time reparameterization in swap dynamics
abstract: Swap Monte Carlo dramatically accelerates the equilibration of deeply supercooled liquids while preserving the equilibrium Boltzmann distribution. Recent work has argued that swap and other accelerated algorithms act by reparameterizing time: different dynamics follow the same slow relaxation process, but with different clocks. Here we test this idea in a continuously polydisperse glass former. We confirm that mean collective overlaps satisfy an approximate time reparameterization, in agreement with earlier results. However, the associated clock depends systematically on the collective probe length and on the relaxation stage. Thus the observed collective collapse does not define a unique, observable-independent material time. Over the numerically accessible $α$-relaxation regime, swap changes not only the rate of relaxation, but also its length-scale dependence. The resulting collective reparameterization is therefore only approximate and does not establish an exact dynamical equivalence between swap and reference relaxation.

title: Wasserstein rates of all orders for the Sato-Tate law of Kloosterman sums
abstract: Let $μ_q$ be the distribution of the normalized Kloosterman sums $\mathrm{Kl}(a;q)$, $a\in\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and let $μ_{\mathrm{ST}}$ be the Sato--Tate law. We prove $W_s(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/3}$ for $1\le s\le2$, $W_s(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/6-1/(3s)}$ for $2\le s<\infty$, and $W_\infty(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/6}$, answering a question of Kowalski and Untrau. More generally, we bound $W_s(μ,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})$ for all $s$ whenever the Chebyshev moments of $μ$ satisfy bounds of Katz type. For $s=2$ the bound also follows from a smoothing inequality of Borda and Cuenin; for $s>2$ and $s=\infty$ our bounds are stronger. The proof uses the quantile coupling, which arises from Stieltjes sums over two different intervals whose cells are paired so as to balance two measures, and which is optimal for all $s$ simultaneously; an explicit $W_2$ smoothing inequality relative to $μ_{\mathrm{ST}}$; and a sharp comparison between $W_s$ and the Kolmogorov distance for laws with square-root edges. The last result shows that $q^{-1/6}$ is the best rate for $W_\infty$ obtainable from Niederreiter's discrepancy bound. Numerically, for primes $10^3<p<10^6$, all these distances appear to decay like $p^{-1/2}$.

title: Geometric Parrots: Rule Absence vs. Rule Fragility in Spatial and Physical Reasoning for Vision-Language Models
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can answer many geometric and physical reasoning questions correctly, yet still behave inconsistently in interaction, for example, abandoning a correct answer when confronted with a confident but incorrect user assertion. Standard single-turn accuracy cannot distinguish such capitulations from beneficial corrections because it scores each response in isolation. We introduce GRIP, a controlled benchmark with 34 procedurally generated reasoning domains, 100,000 images, and 600,000 questions spanning geometric, spatial, visual, and physical reasoning. Each scene is generated by deterministic code, and every answer is derived directly from the underlying scene state, providing exact ground truth without human annotation. On GRIP, we propose Dual-Loop Evaluation. A closed loop probes each image with a five-step compositional question ladder to localize where reasoning fails. An open loop then re-elicits the model's answer under controlled challenges, including peer-model responses and unsupported user assertions. Because ground truth is known exactly, answer changes can be signed as corrections (wrong-to-right) or capitulations (right-to-wrong), separating two failure modes: rule absence and rule fragility. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/bilaljawaid980/GRIP-Benchmark, with further details at https://bilaljawaid980.github.io/grip-benchmark/.

title: DeepThink: A Conceptual Model for Knowledge-Addressable Recurrent Language Modeling
abstract: This manuscript presents DeepThink, a knowledge-addressable framework for recurrent language modeling. A Knowledge Bank stores typed Knowledge Units, a Knowledge Activator selects units from the current execution state, Knowledge Assembly produces an executable configuration, and a Shared Thinking Operator updates that state. An output stage then organizes generation. This organization exposes knowledge capacity, activation width, and recurrent depth as separate design variables, supporting both complete parameter packages and fine-grained expert or low-rank modules. We formalize the interfaces and their execution semantics, including state-dependent selection, parameter-space assembly, and thinking followed by generation. For compatible templates and complete runtime-state configurations, we establish an exact Fixed-Schedule Realization of an existing fixed-depth model. Exact shared-base reparameterization and pretrained output-tail reuse provide complementary initialization constructions. Together, these results define a route from pretrained models to dynamically selected and assembled recurrent computation. A synthesis of conditional computation, recurrent models, modular parameters, and knowledge interfaces positions DeepThink within the research landscape and identifies the design questions arising from their integration.

title: EventLens: Event-Structure Reinforcement Learning for Video Understanding
abstract: Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) achieve strong results on video question answering, yet often fail to recover the temporal structure that makes a video coherent. They may merge neighboring events, miss single-event progression, or infer implausible relations across events. We study structured temporal understanding as the ability to recover event structure from visual evidence, including event boundaries, single-event progression, and multi-event relations. We argue that this gap arises from a mismatch between current post-training objectives and temporal reasoning, where caption-style supervision allows models to rely on language shortcuts rather than visual temporal grounding. To address this, we propose EventLens, a vision-centric reinforcement learning framework that learns video understanding through event-structure recovery. Instead of reconstructing captions, EventLens trains models to recover temporal structure under controlled perturbations, such as altered temporal granularity, reversed progression, and shuffled event order. We instantiate this framework with a three-level temporal ontology and derive three verifiable task families: event segmentation, progression discrimination, and multi-event relation reasoning. These tasks admit deterministic rewards, enabling task-specialized GRPO training without human preference labels or learned reward models. We further introduce multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MT-OPD) to consolidate specialized policies into a unified model. Experiments on Qwen3-VL backbones show consistent improvements on temporal grounding and event-sensitive reasoning benchmarks, while preserving general video-QA performance. Learning curves further demonstrate that EventLens achieves comparable downstream transfer with significantly reduced training cost compared to direct mixed RL optimization.

title: Extending Wire-Driven Parallel Robots to Multi-Floating-Link Systems with an Inter-Body Wire
abstract: Parallel wire-driven systems are a framework in which multiple wires are connected to an end effector, and the end effector is driven by the tensions of those wires. Because they can transmit large forces, up to the breaking strength of the wires, over lengths on the order of several tens of meters, they can realize powerful actuation in large workspaces. In recent years, studies have also investigated connecting wires to external environments such as trees and columns and forming parallel wire actuation on site. However, conventional parallel wire-driven systems often assume a single end effector, and because of interference between wires and links in a shared workspace, it has been difficult to handle multiple floating links simultaneously. In this study, we realize multi-floating-link parallel wire actuation by introducing an inter-body wire. In real-robot experiments, the two bodies supported and lifted a mannequin and transferred it onto a stretcher as a rescue motion. This shows that parallel wire actuation can be extended from a single end effector to a multi-floating-link system, and indicates its potential for broader tasks such as the manipulation of large objects and rescue support.

title: A Dimension Estimate for Polynomial Growth Holomorphic Functions
abstract: On a complete noncompact Kähler manifold $M^n$ of complex dimension $n$ with nonnegative Ricci curvature, we prove that polynomial growth holomorphic functions of degree $d$ ($d\geq 0$) have an dimension upper bound $C(n)(1+d)^n$. In particular, $\dim_{\C}\OO_d(M)\leq C'(n)d^n,$ for $d\geq1$, and the estimate is sharp.

title: ProCARE: Real-World Study Automation via Profile-Grounded Evidence Contracts
abstract: Real-world studies (RWS) analyze routinely collected healthcare data, such as electronic health records and insurance claims, to estimate treatment effects, monitor safety, and identify risk factors outside randomized trials. Automating RWS with large language model agents is appealing but brittle: valid analyses depend on dataset-specific clinical semantics, including index dates, follow-up windows, patient/event-level units, and outcome boundaries that are often implicit in observational data. This leads to schema mismatches, temporal errors, inconsistent analytical granularity, and unsupported clinical claims. We present ProCARE, a profile-grounded framework that reformulates RWS automation as constrained compilation. ProCARE converts heterogeneous data profiles into Evidence Contracts specifying available variables, temporal attributes, distributions, and evidentiary limits, and compiles study objectives into RWS-IR, a strongly typed intermediate representation for variables, time relations, analysis units, and statistical tasks. Deterministic validation and localized repair then check and revise generated workflows across schema mapping, cohort construction, variable derivation, analysis, and interpretation. On 36 EHR-based benchmark tasks, ProCARE outperforms strong LLM-agent baselines in code executability, semantic consistency, and conclusion traceability, with automated violation diagnoses showing moderate-to-substantial agreement with blinded expert review.

title: EgoAlign: Situated 3D Understanding without Situation Descriptions
abstract: Situated 3D Question Answering requires models to interpret a 3D scene relative to an agent's pose. Existing methods commonly convey that pose through a natural-language situation description, which may be unavailable or costly to obtain in real-world deployments. While some methods additionally incorporate numerical pose, we find that randomly shuffling the agent pose causes little performance degradation, indicating limited functional dependence on the numerical pose. To address this gap, we introduce EgoAlign, a simple 3D language model that represents a scene in an agent-centric coordinate frame, together with a dedicated egocentric alignment stage comprising four complementary tasks: object category recognition, egocentric direction prediction, metric distance estimation, and spatial relation prediction. This stage teaches the model to consistently interpret scene geometry relative to the agent's pose before task-specific fine-tuning. EgoAlign achieves the strongest performance on SQA3D, Real-3DQA, and MSQA among compared methods while remaining highly efficient. More importantly, removing textual situation descriptions yields comparable or better downstream performance, whereas shuffling EgoAlign's numerical pose causes substantial degradation. These results show that EgoAlign establishes agent-centric spatial context directly from numerical pose without requiring textual situation descriptions.

title: DIGS: Distribution-Informed Gaussian Splatting for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary 3D Segmentation
abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D Gaussian segmentation typically binds semantic features to the per-Gaussian state via per-scene gradient training (1-4 h) or the more recent closed-form distillation. Both commit each primitive to a single feature; therefore, boundary Gaussians spanning multiple 2D instances are forced into a hard decision that degrades retrieval accuracy and yields unstable mask boundaries at render time. We present DIGS, a training-free framework with two stages, class-agnostic mapping and multi-modal encoding, that decouples instance discovery from linguistic naming. At the Gaussian level, our distribution-informed representation maintains an explicit top-$M$ label distribution per primitive, updated by a tempered Dirichlet rule; preservation of multi-peaked label distributions at boundary primitives allows a late-argmax renderer to recover clean instance boundaries. A bidirectional state machine aggregates these distributions into a persistent class-agnostic instance ontology. The instance-level encoding stage then fuses the CLIP visual embedding of each instance's isolated 3D footprint with the CLIP-text embedding of an LLM-generated attribute description, disambiguating visually similar instances. On a single A100, DIGS completes mapping and instance encoding on LERF-OVS in 1.0-3.2 min per scene, depending on whether LLM fusion is enabled, and serves native 3D queries in 5.4 ms. It reaches 71.95% mean mIoU on LERF-OVS, outperforming both the training-free SFS and training-based LaGa baselines. DIGS also achieves the highest mean mIoU on LERF-Mask and 3D-OVS and surpasses Gaga and ObjectGS on Replica under their respective evaluation protocols. Code is available at https://github.com/ZephyrZos/DIGS.

title: On Z-Noetherian Rings
abstract: In this paper, introduce a new finiteness condition for commutative rings, called $Z$-Noetherian, under which every ideal contained in the set of zero-divisors $Z(R)$ is finitely generated. This condition lies properly between Noetherian and $Nil_{*}$-Noetherian. We establish intrinsic characterizations of $Z$-Noetherian rings and investigate their stability under nilpotent quotients and localizations. Under the assumption that $Z(R)$ is an ideal, we obtain a primary decomposition theorem for ideals contained in $Z(R)$. For $ZD$-rings, we prove a Cohen-type criterion characterizing $Z$-Noetherian in terms of the finite generation of prime ideals contained in $Z(R)$. We further establish $Z$-Noetherian analogues of the Hilbert Basis Theorem and Krull's Intersection Theorem. Finally, we establish a principal ideal theorem for $Z$-Noetherian rings. Collectively, these results show that several fundamental finiteness and structural properties of Noetherian rings extend to the broader class of $Z$-Noetherian rings.

title: One-Shot Learning for Double-Shot Latte Art: Adapting Cobot Pouring Skills with Dynamic Movement Primitives
abstract: Latte art is a complex task requiring dexterity and precision, making it a challenging and commercially relevant task. A one-shot learning system is employed in which a single barista demonstration is segmented into five functionally distinct phases, each encoded as an independent Cartesian Dynamic Movement Primitive (CDMP) with its own parameters. Against a single-CDMP baseline, per-phase encoding reduces transition endpoint error by 3.2-4.5 times and art-stroke shape error by 2.7 times, reproducing jug tilt to below 1 degree RMS in the pouring phases. The learnt pour scales from a 280mL to a 400mL cup through a single spatial offset and a scaled recipe, with no re-demonstration. The phase-based CDMP approach generalises beyond latte art to any demonstration task whose phases have distinct spatial or temporal requirements whilst demonstrating the ability to adapt reproductions to suit different task requirements.

title: Regularity lemma for Gaussian polynomials
abstract: We prove a regularity lemma for polynomials with fixed degree $d$ and any number of standard Gaussian input variables. Following modern approaches to the Szemer{é}di regularity lemma, we deduce our results from a general formulation of the regularity lemma using ultraproducts. Along the way, we give a direct combinatorial proof of the celebrated ``fourth moment theorem'' of Nualart and Peccati, which characterizes the asymptotically Gaussian polynomials inside degree-$d$ Gaussian chaos as those such that $\mathbb{E} p^2 \to 1$ and $\mathbb{E} p^4 \to 3$.

title: Probe Signatures of Quantum Chaos with Quantum Sensing
abstract: The spectral form factor (SFF), which is the Fourier transform of the two-point spectral correlation, is a fundamental diagnostics of quantum chaos. Nevertheless, its experimental detection in quantum many-body systems was less unexplored until recently. Here, we establish a relationship between the SFF with the quantum Fisher information (QFI) by means of quantum sensing protocols. Furthermore, when the eigenvalues and eigenstates of the disordered Hamiltonian are statistically independent, we prove that QFI is typical both in short and long timescales while numerics suggest that it is also typical at intermediate timescales, which ensures self-averaging of QFI. The self-averaging property renders the experimental measurement of QFI with our protocol less noisy in contrast with the direct measurement of SFF which is known to be non-self-averaging. Our results reveal an intriguing connection between quantum noise and the signatures of quantum chaos.

title: Label-Centric Knowledge Retrieval for Zero-Shot Text Classification
abstract: Flagship large language models (LLMs) offer rich general knowledge and strong reasoning capabilities, but their high inference cost and latency limit their use for large-scale data labeling. We study zero-shot text classification with semantically meaningful labels and task descriptions, without task-specific labeled examples or classifier feedback. We propose \textbf{SLKR} (Semantic Label Knowledge Retrieval), a label-centric retrieval-augmented generation framework that separates offline knowledge construction from lightweight online inference. Offline, a flagship LLM independently generates label definitions, retrieval keywords, and boundary rules for potentially confusable label pairs, forming a reusable label-knowledge store. Because this construction operates over the label space rather than the input corpus, its one-time flagship cost can be amortized across large-scale inference. Online, hybrid semantic and lexical retrieval first identifies the top-$K$ candidate labels and then selects up to $M$ input-relevant boundary rules connecting candidate-label pairs. A lightweight LLM performs the final classification in a single call using the retrieved definitions and rules. Across three public benchmarks and a real-world multilingual book-classification dataset, SLKR achieves the best results on all four datasets with Qwen3.5-4B and on three of four with Ministral-3-3B, while using compact input contexts and no task-specific labeled examples. Boundary ablations further show that retrieving a small set of input-relevant rules preserves performance close to using all boundaries with substantially less context, supporting efficient reuse of flagship-generated label knowledge for lightweight classification.

title: Chirally pinned flat bands, helical minibands, and bias-controlled topology of Jackiw-Rebbi states in a periodically modulated Dirac mass texture
abstract: Flat bands amplify interactions into correlated phases, and topological bound states are robust by principle; combining the two in a model that is both exactly analyzable and experimentally accessible is therefore especially desirable. Here we show that a square-lattice model with a slowly modulated Dirac mass texture, $m(x)=m+m_0\cos(2πx/L)$ with $L$ up to hundreds of sites, provides such a setting, without engineered geometries, lattice-scale textures, or long-range hoppings. Exact nesting reduces the problem, independently at each transverse momentum $k_y$, to a $1+1$ dimensional Dirac Hamiltonian with a position-dependent mass: every simple zero of $m(x)$ binds Jackiw-Rebbi zero modes, and the two walls of a period form an effective Su-Schrieffer-Heeger ring. The model interpolates between a chirally pinned flat band at large $L$, a helical miniband whose nodes are enforced by a boundary phase of the ring, and a bias-dimerized regime in which the sign of the bias sets a winding number. A central result is that the miniband bandwidth is not a single scale: a max-min measurement conflates three widths of different origin, the helical height $W_{\rm JR}$ exponential in the period, the zone-edge upturn $W_{\rm edge}\propto L^{-2/3}$ dominating at large $L$, and a bias bump exponential in $L$, so the flat band is robust against bias in the thermodynamic limit. We analyze two lattice realizations, a two-orbital model with modulated inter-orbital hybridization and a single-orbital bond-order texture sharing the nodal physics while leaving the van Hove points gapless, and propose experiments on cold-atom superlattices, Kekule-ordered graphene, STM designer lattices, and microwave arrays.

title: A Novel Coexistence Scheme for OFDM and OTFS Waveforms for Uplink in 6G Networks
abstract: The upcoming sixth generation (6G) wireless networks are designed to support advanced applications that the current air interface based on orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) cannot accommodate, necessitating innovations in waveform design. Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) has emerged as a promising alternative, offering enhanced performance particularly in high-mobility channel environments. However, deploying fundamentally different waveforms over the same frequencies fails to exploit the mutual relationships between them. In this paper, a forward-compatible yet backward-compatible coexistence framework is proposed, where various OFDM waveform options are incorporated while seamlessly integrating OTFS within the same network. The proposed coexistence paradigm involves utilizing a specially designed spreading matrix in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain to process OTFS data. The matrix is tailored to establish orthogonality between OTFS and OFDM waveforms, effectively reducing cross-interference when both coexist within the same time-frequency (TF) resources. Our results demonstrate up to a 6 dB improvement in bit error rate (BER) performance for the OTFS waveform compared to other coexistence schemes. The proposed approach also shows greater interference resilience and approaches the upper bounds of achievable rates. By utilizing the full bandwidth and time duration, it enhances range and velocity resolutions, leading to improved sensing performance. These findings are supported by mathematical analysis and extensive simulations for uplink scenarios.

title: Regularity of the Price of Anarchy in Routing Games over the Multivariate Demand Space
abstract: We study the price of anarchy (PoA) in nonatomic routing games as a function of the full vector of origin--destination demands. We show that the Beckmann value function is continuously differentiable on the positive demand cone, with gradient equal to the equilibrium origin--destination cost vector; hence the PoA is continuously differentiable on the regular demand region. We prove that the nondifferentiability set has Lebesgue measure zero and, when every edge cost is strictly increasing or constant, is covered by countably many codimension-one submanifolds. Under the same cost structure, all equilibrium objects are cellwise as smooth as the edge costs. For affine costs, the exceptional sets become finite unions of lower-dimensional polyhedral cells linked by an exact scaling law, and the maximum of the PoA over a cell closure is attained on the cell boundary, generalizing the one-dimensional endpoint result. The theory is illustrated on the Sioux Falls benchmark network.

title: Exploring Mixed Reality for Engagement in Robotics: A Comparison of Robot Control Methods
abstract: This paper presents a Mixed Reality (MR) robotics experience that provides an accessible introduction to interacting with a physical robot. The application combines a TurtleBot with a virtual animal-tending activity and three control methods: Joystick, Waypoint, and Path-Drawing. A mixed-methods user study with 10 participants investigated changes in robotics interest and confidence following the experience and how the control methods influenced engagement, workload, and preference. Confidence increased following the experience, with the exploratory analysis indicating a significant pre--post difference, while the increase in interest was not statistically significant. The control methods produced clear differences in perceived workload and ease of use, with Path-Drawing generally more demanding and difficult to use. Joystick was preferred by eight of ten participants and was associated with better perceived performance and lower frustration. However, no statistically significant differences were detected in the other engagement dimensions, suggesting that the most preferred method was not necessarily more engaging across all aspects of the experience. These findings highlight the importance of considering both usability and engagement when designing how users interact with robots in introductory MR experiences.

title: Exploration strategies for Gaussian process bandit optimization with inference regret guarantees
abstract: Existing cumulative regret guarantees for Bayesian optimization (BO) do not necessarily characterize the quality of the algorithm's final output. This gap is critical under noisy evaluations, where the goal is to return a single high-quality recommendation. To address it, we introduce efficient exploration strategies that can be incorporated into any BO procedure by occasionally replacing the acquisition query with an exploration query. To validate this approach, we bound the Gaussian process posterior standard deviation over the search space via the fill distance of the queries, which measures the largest region left unexplored. We then use this result to derive upper bounds on the inference regret, i.e., the gap between the global optimum and the function value at the algorithm's returned point. Empirically, these exploration strategies improve the final recommendations of existing BO algorithms on synthetic benchmarks, hyperparameter optimization, and a control task.

title: Self-Avoidance Governs Re-entrant Coil-Globule Transition of Inertial Active Brownian Ring Polymers
abstract: Active matter systems composed of self-propelled entities exhibit a wide range of out-of-equilibrium phase behaviors and collective dynamics. Assemblies of active particles, e.g., in a linear structure, are particularly interesting, as they exhibit an intriguing interplay between activity and geometrical restrictions due to self-avoidance and entanglements. Using Langevin dynamics simulations of an active Brownian ring polymer with translational and rotational inertia, we uncover an inertia-driven re-entrant coil-globule transition in the absence of any attractive interactions. We show that rotational inertia plays a paramount role, leading, in the globular state, to spontaneous, nonzero, radially outward polarization of the active forces. Self-avoidance and entanglements break the rotational symmetry of active beads and effectively stabilize the globular states. The transition becomes increasingly sharp with increasing rotational inertia, yielding highly compact globular conformations at intermediate activities, whereas at high activity the polymer re-expands into a coil state. Scaling of the radius of gyration reveals crossovers from self-avoiding, phantom-like to compact-globular structures. Further, rotational inertia enhances transport properties, with an intermediate activity-induced Rouse-type bead diffusion and a long-time diffusion coefficient displaying a power-law dependence on the moment of inertia. Our study establishes a purely inertia-induced mechanism for controlling the collapse of active polymers, arising from spontaneous active-force polarization and self-avoidance.

title: Field-driven phase transition crossover in kagome antiferromagnet Mn$_{3-x}$Co$_x$Sn
abstract: Mn$_3$Sn exhibits a complex magnetic phase diagram with multiple symmetry-breaking phenomena. Minute electron doping at the Mn site breaks the kagome lattice symmetry in Mn$_3$Sn. In this work, we exploited this to tune the order of the magnetic phase transition using magnetocaloric effect in Mn$_{3-x}$Co$_x$Sn single crystals. Pristine Mn$_3$Sn shows metallic behaviour with a spin-reorientation transition at 278 K, which shifts to 175 K upon Co doping. Additionally, Co doping also induces a weak-ferromagnetic transition near $\approx 210$ K. The effect of Co doping results inverse to conventional magnetocaloric effect, with enhanced magnetic entropy change. Further, the scaled entropy change reveals a field-driven magnetic phase transition crossover from first order to second order in Mn$_{2.75}$Co$_{0.25}$Sn crystal. Based on experimental data, a new phase diagram is constructed, depicting the field evolution of various magnetic orders.

title: A New Lens on Multi-GPU Communication: API-Level Memory Models for Portable Optimization
abstract: As network communication increasingly becomes a performance bottleneck for ML and HPC workloads, it is more important than ever to optimize multi-GPU data transfers. Recently, low-level device APIs have emerged that allow programmers to perform fine-grain optimizations via one-sided put/get operations triggered directly from the device. However, the communication libraries providing these device APIs (e.g., rocSHMEM, MSCCL++, and NCCL/RCCL GIN) currently lack a rigorous memory model defining how their primitives interact with the underlying memory systems. Without this, emerging HPC and ML workloads aggressively optimizing network communication via device APIs can be brittle, error-prone, and face compatibility and inter-operability challenges. This paper proposes the use of API-level memory models for these emerging device communication APIs. An API-level memory model defines the memory semantics of communication API calls in a way that abstracts lower-level details from the API user and simplifies development. This work defines one such model for device-side communication (implemented in AMD's recently open sourced rocSHMEM library) and demonstrates how formal relaxations to such a model can enable low-level LLM performance optimizations while retaining a well-defined standardized interface. Specifically, we describe how updating the SHMEM API implemented by rocSHMEM can properly support cache bypassing for network data, improving performance of a collective communication workload by up to 2.48x, a fused compute+communication workload by up to 1.77x, and a state-of-the-art expert-parallel communication workload by up to 1.18x.

title: Correct Choices, Failed Sequences: Choice2Seq Benchmarks Correctness Retention Across Output Interfaces
abstract: A model may select the correct answer yet fail to construct it through a sequence of local decisions. We introduce Choice2Seq, a diagnostic benchmark that measures correctness retention across complete-answer selection and sequential construction in independent runs on the same problems and candidate sets. Sequence Composition Rate (SCR) measures the fraction of correctly selected items that are also answered correctly through local construction. Jev achieves 97.1% and 99.5% selection accuracy on arithmetic and lexical retrieval, yet retains only 33.0% and 2.1% of those correct choices under serial construction, respectively. Substantial gaps also emerge for StartLux and Qwen, including when Qwen emits characters directly. Restricting local options to candidate-supported characters improves construction, while explicit position indexing improves copying fidelity, even for incorrect selections. These interventions distinguish task correctness, plan fidelity, and output compliance. Matched dialogue-state evaluations reveal that local field construction largely preserves Jev's correct states but reduces Qwen's mean-turn accuracy, highlighting task- and interface-dependent differences. Sequence-level confidence and request-cost analyses further characterize completed outputs.

title: When Sample-Splitting Choices Matter in TMLE and AIPW: Cross-Fitting, Targeting, and Repetition
abstract: Variants of targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE) and augmented inverse-probability weighting (AIPW) with machine-learning nuisance models differ in which observations train them, how bias is corrected, and whether splits are repeated. In known-truth simulations of a binary-outcome average treatment effect, eight headline estimators shared each setting's library, inner folds and truncation bound; coverage differences were judged against a prespecified two-percentage-point margin. With a low-complexity library and good overlap (n = 3000), all but a half-sample baseline covered equivalently (0.928-0.939). With one random forest on the primary data-generating mechanism, estimators fitting the propensity in-sample undercovered severely (0.12-0.48), whereas cross-fitting both nuisances raised coverage to 0.91-1.00, two overcovering. Under near-positivity, every AIPW estimator covered better than every TMLE estimator with the unweighted fluctuation (0.907-0.917 versus 0.656-0.806 at the primary setting, all undercovering); looser truncation widened the gap. At the primary settings, pooled-versus-fold-specific and single-versus-double cross-fit constructions (involving four additional estimators) were usually equivalent; under extreme weights, pooled-targeting estimates were 1.7-1.8 times as dispersed as fold-specific ones. Repetition reduced partition dependence but made several intervals more conservative. Two real-data analyses illustrate these sensitivities. Results support cross-fitting both nuisances when empirical-process conditions cannot be justified, and assessing truncation and AIPW-versus-TMLE sensitivity under poor overlap.

title: Repairing covariance functions on metric trees through a Hausdorff-type distance
abstract: A compact metric tree is the natural domain of spatial data recorded along a river network, a root system, or the branched processes of a cell, and a suitable distance between two points is the length of the path joining them. That distance admits almost none of the covariance models of spatial statistics, since only the roughest members of each family stay nonnegative definite, and the resulting fields are nowhere mean square differentiable. The repair proposed here is a change of metric. Comparing two points through their distances to the leaves gives a Hausdorff-type metric built from the shortest-path one. The new metric has a closed form, agrees with the shortest-path one inside every edge, and is strictly smaller across branching points. Any correlation function valid in a Euclidean space of dimension equal to the number of leaves may then be composed with it, returning the Matérn, powered exponential, and generalized Cauchy families at every degree of smoothness, and, on trees with few leaves, also correlations that change sign or have compact support. The same construction yields the multivariate Matérn and space-time models of the Gneiting class. In simulations covering a range of smoothness and of spatial scale, maximum likelihood provides estimates without appreciable bias, and on a reconstructed microglial cell the smooth models reduce the cross-validated prediction error by half.

title: Detectability of 21-cm Power Spectra from the Epoch of Reionization using Modern Radio Telescopes
abstract: One of the unsolved questions in astrophysics and cosmology is the development of a robust physical model to explain the thermal history of the intergalactic medium during the epoch of reionization. Various astrophysical models have been proposed, but current models remain only partially constrained by available observations. To clarify this ambiguity, hydrodynamical, semi-numerical, and N-body simulations can help solve this issue. One notable simulation from the epoch of reionization is the 21SSD simulations, which provide high-resolution results for the global 21-cm brightness temperature and the 21-cm power spectrum during the epoch of reionization. The simulation includes 45 models spanning three key astrophysical parameters of X-ray emissivity, Lyman-band emissivity, and the X-ray hard-to-soft emissivity ratio. Distinct values of these parameters result in different models of this simulation. In this work, four active radio observatories, including HERA, MWA, GMRT, and LOFAR have been considered to investigate the sensitivity and thermal noise of the 21-cm power spectrum. Each observatory has a particular sensitivity based on its instrumental characteristics, which helps assess which models lie above the forecast sensitivity thresholds of current instruments.

title: Grouped Sparse Bayesian Estimation for Near-Field Massive MIMO Channels
abstract: This paper studies near-field massive MIMO channel estimation based on an electromagnetic channel model with limited pilots. Starting from Maxwell's equations, we derive the homogeneous background response and the scattering response in the spatial and wavenumber domains. It is found that a compact scattering cluster produces a localized receive--transmit transverse-wavenumber block across finite apertures, thereby yields a block-sparse NLOS channel coefficient matrix in the wavenumber domain. Considering the spatial non-stationarity of large-scale antenna arrays, we introduce visibility factors at the transmit and receive sides of the channel model. To solve the non-stationary sparse channel estimation problem in the wavenumber domain, we propose a visibility-aware block-sparse Bayesian channel estimation algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves lower channel-estimation NMSE than benchmark schemes.

title: Towards Privacy-Preserving ASR: Speaker-Level Machine Unlearning
abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems are commonly designed to transcribe linguistic content independently of speaker identity. However, speaker-specific information can persist within the latent representations of ASR models, raising privacy concerns when training data includes sensitive individuals. While machine unlearning has been studied in several speech tasks, applying speaker unlearning to ASR remains challenging due to the strong entanglement of linguistic and speaker-related information in speech representations. In this work, we conduct a layer-wise analysis of Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) based ASR representations, revealing that speaker identity is primarily encoded in intermediate encoder layers. Based on this observation, we explore a feature-level unlearning strategy that targets these identity structures. Experiments on the VCTK corpus show that the proposed approach removes the influence of specific speakers while maintaining robust transcription performance.

title: Orbital cancellation and reentrant localization in a quasiperiodic trimer ladder
abstract: Uniform orbital detuning can restore spatial extent even as quasiperiodic modulation strengthens. In a trimer ladder with fixed hoppings and orbital modulation signs, increasing detuning and modulation amplitude together drives successive avoided crossings that redistribute orbital weights, suppressing the projected onsite potential in both lower molecular bands while leaving the third strongly modulated. Complete-band participation scaling supports two reentrant high-participation windows, with wave-packet propagation corroborating spatial recovery at representative controls over the studied sizes and times. These diagonal cancellations leave residual interband modulation, which generates a self-energy whose magnitude depends on the molecular level separation. Gaussian quadrature improves convergence of closed-walk determinant estimates used to cross-check energy-resolved attenuation. Comparing the coupled and decoupled ladders under the same finite-size participation criterion shows that restoring the full off-diagonal modulation narrows both sampled windows, with a larger absolute contraction of the second.

title: Time-Frequency Continuous-Variable Quantum Teleportation with Single Photons
abstract: Quantum teleportation, a key building block for quantum technologies, enables distant parties, Alice and Bob, to transfer an unknown quantum state using entanglement, local operations, and classical communication. In this work, we propose a quantum teleportation protocol for single-photon time-frequency continuous variables, where time is the time of arrival at a detector. We detail the operational requirements of the protocol, notably the nonlinear interactions needed for the photon-photon time-frequency entangling gate. By explicitly treating the detector position as the reference frame for time of arrival, we show that, even with ideal classical and quantum channels, the input-output fidelity is not unity unless the receiving party can correct the detector-position mismatch. This results in a trade-off between teleportation fidelity and the temporal bandwidth of the input photon wavepacket. The protocol itself can be used for remote detector synchronization. In particular, we show that time-frequency cat and Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states provide an internal temporal ruler through fidelity revivals. We further derive the classical and best-copy fidelity thresholds for single-photon Gaussian wavepackets, finding that the relevant vacuum-equivalent shot noise is input-dependent, in contrast with quadrature-based continuous-variable quantum teleportation. Our proposal derives from a quantum theory of space-time events, whereafter we establish space as a reference for the time degree of freedom, thereby grounding our work in ongoing research on reference frames and superselection rules in quantum optics and quantum information. Beyond protocols harnessing time-frequency continuous variables of single photons, this work points toward remote synchronization in quantum communication architectures.

title: MSC: Multi-Stage Caster-aware Control Framework with Uncertainty-Aware NMPC and RL-based Execution Layer
abstract: Freely swiveling casters are widely adopted in industrial AMRs/SDVs for their mechanical simplicity and load capacity. However, caster misalignment during low-speed or high-curvature maneuvers induces strong contact nonlinearities, widening the planning-execution gap between commanded $(v, ω)$ and realized motion. Existing caster-aware strategies are highly sensitive to state-estimation reliability, causing unstable execution in uncertain transition regimes. To address this, we present Multi-Stage Caster-aware Control (MSC), a planning-execution integrated hierarchical framework featuring two core mechanisms. First, an uncertainty-aware NMPC (CU-MPC) dynamically schedules caster-aware costs and input regularization using predictive uncertainty to suppress overly aggressive maneuvers. Second, a reinforcement learning-based execution layer estimates and predicts caster states under partial observability, transforming high-level velocity commands into physically executable wheel speeds adapted to current contact conditions. Validations in Isaac Sim and real robots demonstrate that MSC offers a clear comparative advantage over existing decoupled compensation approaches by significantly improving caster-state estimation accuracy, minimizing misalignment, and enhancing tracking robustness in caster-sensitive maneuvers.

title: Intrinsic Soft X-ray Emission from the Hot Circumgalactic Medium in IllustrisTNG
abstract: We study the intrinsic 0.5--2~keV emission of the hot circumgalactic medium (CGM) in the IllustrisTNG simulation TNG100-2 at redshifts 0, 0.1, and 0.2. We calculate the emission of gas cells with $T \geq 10^6$~K in the spherical shell between $0.15R_{500}$ and $R_{500}$ and compare samples selected by their star-formation activity. X-ray luminosity increases with halo mass, although the class-dependent fits cover different mass intervals. Among galaxies with positive luminosity and star formation rate (SFR), the high-activity sample retains a positive association after a linear adjustment for halo mass. The residual association is weaker in the quiescent subset with positive luminosity and SFR. Within $10^{11.75}<M_{500}/M_\odot<10^{12.25}$, the high-activity sample has more centrally concentrated emission and a median luminosity about five times that of the quiescent sample. The two populations have similar median hot-gas masses despite their different X-ray luminosities and radial profiles. These differences are consistent with variations in the spatial distribution and thermodynamic state of the emitting gas, although the samples are not matched in halo mass. Our results suggest that soft X-ray emission probes the structure of the hot CGM as well as its gas content, offering a way to investigate how star formation and feedback shape gaseous halos.

title: Lüshi-1840: Building and Probing a Knowledge Cutoff for a Classical Chinese Language Model
abstract: Language models trained only on text from before a given year are useful for studying hindsight and historical language, but the open collections of pre-modern Chinese carry no publication dates and unreliable dynasty labels. We present Lüshi-1840, a 983M-parameter model trained from scratch on 12,262 books (1.28B characters) selected as composed before 1840. A first corpus, dated by a common heuristic, in effect ended at 1644 while containing twentieth-century material. We describe the re-dating and cleaning pipeline that replaced it and an audit with markers the pipeline did not use, which still finds later material. On the model side we measure surprisal, relative to a modern reference, on annals compiled after the cutoff. For events after 1840 against events up to 1820 the ratio is 1.38 (95% interval 1.33-1.44), against about 1.00 for modern general-purpose models. In a series of 294M models, adding the later court records lowers the ratio from 1.33 to 1.16, and the two models diverge from the 1820s, where the added records begin. The probe tracks the coverage of sources and does not establish a single cutoff year; none of our probes exposes the audited contamination. Model, book list and scripts will be released.

title: FOAdapter: A Plug-and-Play Spatial Tokenizer for Low-Bitrate FOA Speech Coding
abstract: Spatially encoded speech conveys not only linguistic information but also spatial cues. This enables listeners to distinguish and localize speakers, contributing to more natural and realistic auditory experiences in applications such as remote conferencing and immersive media. Neural speech codecs (NSCs) enable high-quality reconstruction of monaural speech at increasingly low bitrates while preserving linguistic information, but their ability to effectively preserve spatial cues remains limited. We propose FOAdapter, a plug-and-play spatial tokenizer that leverages a pretrained monaural speech codec to efficiently represent both linguistic and spatial information in first-order ambisonic (FOA) speech at low bitrates. Comprehensive evaluation demonstrates that FOAdapter consistently preserves spatial information across all evaluated codecs. Source code and audio examples are available on our demo website.

title: A Proof of the Erdős Matching Conjecture for Large Matchings via Sharp Tail Probability for Sums of i.i.d. Nonnegative Random Variables
abstract: We resolve a conjecture of Łuczak, Mieczkowska and Šileikis on the maximal tail probability of sums of independent and identically distributed nonnegative random variables. Specifically, for every integer $k\ge1$ and every $0\le x\le1/k$, we prove \[ \sup_{\mathbb E X_1\le x}\mathbb{P}(X_1+\cdots+X_k\ge1) =\max\{1-(1-x)^k,(kx)^k\}, \] where the supremum is over nonnegative i.i.d.\ random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_k$. We also characterize all maximizing distributions. Using this result, we prove the Erdős Matching Conjecture for every fixed $k\ge3$, all sufficiently large $s$, and every $n\ge k(s+1)$. More specifically, we show that in this range, the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph containing no $s+1$ pairwise disjoint edges is \[ \max\left\{ \binom{k(s+1)-1}{k}, \binom nk-\binom{n-s}{k} \right\}. \] Moreover, every extremal family consists either of all $k$-sets meeting a fixed $s$-set or of all $k$-sets contained in a fixed $(k(s+1)-1)$-set.

title: VGGA: Geometry-Grounded Autoencoder for Video Generation
abstract: Autoencoders are the core component of latent video generative models, compressing high-dimensional videos into compact latent spaces for downstream generation. However, existing video autoencoders are primarily optimized for pixel-level reconstruction, providing limited supervision for learning structured latent representations. We argue that videos should not be treated merely as signals to be reconstructed, but rather as 2D projections of dynamic 3D worlds that exhibit explicit and well-structured geometric properties. Building on this insight, we propose \textbf{V}ideo \textbf{G}eometry \textbf{G}rounded \textbf{A}utoencoder (\textbf{VGGA}), a geometry-aware video autoencoder that explicitly incorporates geometric constraints into the reconstruction process. Specifically, VGGA grounds the learned representations along three complementary geometric dimensions: \emph{Structural Depth}, \emph{Motion Correspondence}, and \emph{Projective Warping}. These objectives are unified within a Video Geometry Decoder, which employs a shared spatio-temporal upsampling trunk to jointly optimize geometric learning and RGB reconstruction. Through these geometry-grounded objectives, VGGA encourages the latent representations to capture the underlying 3D structure and motion of dynamic scenes. VGGA consistently improves video generation across both geometry-centric and human-motion domains, reducing gFVD by 28.1\% on RealEstate10K and 37.7\% on Taichi-HD. Notably, these substantial generation improvements are achieved while maintaining comparable reconstruction quality, demonstrating that geometry-grounded representation learning yields a more effective latent space for video generation.

title: Stein degree over fields of characteristic zero
abstract: We show that the Stein degree of horizontal divisors on generalised log Calabi-Yau fibrations or certain vertical divisors of Fano type fibrations over arbitrary fields of characteristic zero is bounded by constants that are independent on the ground field.

title: {Access|Use|Sustain|_}-ability: Exploration and Quantification of a Linguistic Structure and Its Use in HCI
abstract: Language plays a crucial role in research and technology design, throughout problem formulation, method descriptions, analysis of findings, and interpretation. In this paper, we focus on a particular, trending linguistic pattern in the Human-Computer Interaction literature, which we call -abilities. Examples include usability, accessibility, and explainability. These -abilities have become increasingly popular, with potential impacts on the discipline. They take a verb, turn it into an adjective, and finally nominalize it. We approach the -abilities phenomenon with a survey of the HCI literature between 1988 and 2025. All in all, we identified 349 different -abilities. Moreover, the use of -abilities notably increased since the late 2000s, both in the absolute number of different -abilities and the frequency of use of the most popular ones. The majority of -abilities we found had a positive notion, and most -abilities with a negative notion are prefixed counterparts of their positive opposite (e.g., un+sustainability). We critically discuss implications of their increased use. First, -abilities change the literal meaning of design intentions. For example, acceptability reduces the concrete verb accepting into only its potential (acceptable), and finally nominalizes it, claiming the existence of acceptability as a somewhat stable and real, abstract characteristic of a technology. Second, the prefix-based opposite construction can weaken the design goal. Un+sustainability avoids clarification of the -ability's meaning (here e.g., ecological or financial), and does not spell out the expected impact of designs that are not sustainable (e.g., the destruction of nature). Future work should compare the use of -abilities in English with other languages to better understand the ways in which they transform meaning.

title: Deterministic preparation of squeezed and non-Gaussian states in coupled qubit-boson systems
abstract: Deterministic preparation of bosonic resource states is a central task in continuous-variable quantum information processing and quantum metrology. Here we develop a measurement-based imaginary time evolution (MITE) protocol for preparing squeezed and non-Gaussian states. The protocol combines ancilla-mediated weak measurements of the Hamiltonian with a conditional phase rotation that suppresses excited state trapping and stabilizes convergence toward the ground state. The method is potentially applicable in hybrid discrete variable-continuous variable (DV-CV) platforms, where the qubit acts as the measurement readout. We demonstrate deterministic convergence over a broad range of parameters and show that the performance degradation near the stability boundary is governed by the shrinking Bogoliubov quasiparticle gap. The same framework also extends to non-Gaussian bosonic resource states, including Schrödinger cat states and excited states of the single-mode squeezing Hamiltonian, which display Wigner negativity. The squeezed states remain robust under bosonic loss over experimentally relevant regimes.

title: Geometric bulk conductances in even dimensions
abstract: Let $P$ be a short-range projector on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^{2n},\mathbb{C}^m)$ and $U=(U_1,\dots,U_{2n})$ be a transverse family of open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$. We give an elementary proof of a recent result of Martinian-Stoiber, which extends a two-dimensional result of Drouot-Zhu to all even dimensions. Specifically, using only Stokes' theorem and the Poincaré lemma, we show that the geometric Kubo formula $\operatorname{Tr}\big(P[P,\mathbf{1}_{U_1}]\wedge\cdots\wedge[P,\mathbf{1}_{U_{2n}}]\big)$ is the product of a topological integer $\mathcal{X}_U$, which depends only on the relative positions of $U_1, \dots, U_{2n}$, and of the bulk conductance of $P$. Our proof writes the geometric bulk conductance as the pairing of $P$ with a cochain on $\mathbb{Z}^{2n}$ - an idea originally due to Kitaev - and deforms the cochain rather than the sets $(U_1, \dots, U_{2n})$. The proof presented in this paper is due to Claude Opus 5.5.

title: Bootstrapping Classical and Quantum Query Lower Bounds for Finding Tarski Fixed Points
abstract: The Tarski fixed-point problem asks for a fixed point of a monotone map on a $k$-dimensional grid lattice of width $n$ and has applications in game theory, economics, and verification. Substantial gaps remain between the known upper and lower bounds on its quantum query complexity. We prove two hardness bootstrapping theorems for quantum query lower bounds. Starting from a hard instance family whose instances have pair-wise incomparable unique fixed points, and a lower bound established by the nonnegative adversary method, we bootstrap this lower bound by (i) a factor of $Ω(t)$ when the dimension is multiplied by $t$ and the width remains unchanged, and (ii) a factor of $Ω(\log m)$ when the width is multiplied by $m$ and the dimension is doubled. Applying these theorems, we obtain three consequences: (i) an $Ω(k\log^2 n)$ lower bound for $k\geq 4$, improving previously best-known classical and quantum lower bounds; (ii) for every fixed constant $α>0$, there exists a constant $δ(α)>0$ such that $Q_ε(\text{Tarski}(n,k))=Ω(kn^{δ(α)})$ whenever $k>n^α$, and in particular, an $Ω(kn^{0.0072})$ lower bound for $k>n^{2/203}$, the first lower bound with simultaneous linear dependence on the dimension and polynomial dependence on the width; and (iii) a superpolynomial lower bound of $(k/\log k)^{Ω(\log k)}$ for exponentially wide grids, where $n=2^{Θ(k)}$. The last result rules out a route to polynomial-time algorithms for simple stochastic games and ARRIVAL through generic polynomial-query black-box Tarski solvers.

title: Collective Floquet engineering between two distant superconducting artificial atoms
abstract: A one-dimensional waveguide is a crucial medium for transferring propagating quantum information between remote qubits, yet the photon-mediated interaction is typically fixed by the static device geometry, qubit parameters, and their couplings to the transmission line. Such an interaction can be engineered to be coherent or dissipative via virtual- or real-photon exchange, respectively, yet its effective strength remains fixed in either case. Here we demonstrate dynamical control over this interaction by applying Floquet engineering to two superconducting qubits coupled to a waveguide terminated by a capacitive mirror. By positioning one qubit at an antinode and the other qubit at a node or an antinode of the resonant standing wave, we realize a Hermitian or non-Hermitian coupling between the two qubits. A periodic flux drive of the qubit frequencies then enables on-demand control of the coherent energy splitting and the collective decay. Our results establish Floquet engineering as a route to dynamically reshape both coherent and dissipative photon-mediated interactions between remote quantum emitters.

title: C^(sigma+alpha) regularity for fractional Hamilton-Jacobi equations, and rates of convergence in periodic homogenization
abstract: We study two related questions for nonlocal equations of Bellman type: the regularity of solutions when the set of controls depends on the state variable, and the periodic homogenization of stationary nonlocal Hamilton-Jacobi equations driven by uniformly elliptic integro-differential operators of order $σ\in(0,2)$, whose kernels depend simultaneously on the slow variable, the fast periodic variable and the control. The effective equation is again a nonlocal Bellman equation, but its supremum runs over a set of viscosity Mather measures that varies with the space variable, in a merely Hölder continuous way. We first develop a $C^{σ+α}$ regularity theory for nonlocal Bellman equations with Hölder continuous, state-dependent index sets, extending the Schauder estimates of Caffarelli-Silvestre and Serra, in a general framework independent of homogenization. We then use these estimates as a source of compactness to construct a classical solution of the effective problem, unique among bounded classical solutions. Finally, combining this regularity with discounted approximate correctors, we make the perturbed test function method quantitative, and prove that the whole family of solutions converges to the effective solution, with the explicit rate $ε^{σα/(2+α)}$, where $α$ is the Hölder exponent of the data.

title: MP-MNCA: Morphology-Prior Masked Neighbor Cross-Attention for Efficient Spatial Domain Identification
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics jointly captures molecular state, tissue morphology, and spatial organization, yet spatial-domain methods are typically compared only at late training checkpoints, obscuring differences in convergence efficiency. We introduce MP-MNCA, a morphology-prior masked neighbor cross-attention framework that preserves the full 3,000 dimensional highly-variable-gene representation while selectively routing molecular information across spatial neighbors, with histological similarity incorporated as a continuous attention prior under a self-supervised masked neighbor-contrastive objective. Across 12 heterogeneous human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) sections, MP-MNCA is evaluated against established spatial-domain baselines using both convergence trajectories and epoch-wise spatial-domain visualizations. Our results show that MP-MNCA (i) reaches coherent spatial-domain structure in substantially fewer training epochs, as reflected quantitatively by convergence curves and qualitatively by progressive spatial grids, and (ii) maintains strong clustering quality, achieving a mean peak refined ARI of 0.546 versus 0.549 for the strongest baseline (STAIG), while attaining the highest mean refined NMI of 0.657 versus 0.640. Moreover, MP-MNCA outperforms STAIG on 7 of 12 sections in ARI and 11 of 12 in NMI, demonstrating faster convergence without sacrificing spatial-domain quality.

title: SafeDSE: Joint Exploration of Safety Architecture Patterns, Mapping, and Scheduling for Dataflow Applications With Safety Arguments (Extended Version)
abstract: Embedded platforms increasingly host safety-related streaming functions next to less critical ones. Whether a safety architecture pattern, such as a doer/checker pair, protects a function depends on the cores that run its components. Their schedule must meet the throughput requirement, and mixing safety integrity levels (SILs) on one core raises development cost. This report presents SafeDSE, a design space exploration framework for synchronous dataflow applications. One declarative constraint model decides the pattern of each actor, the placement that the fault model requires, the static-order schedule, and the platform, and prices SIL promotion. Guards activate the chosen patterns in a fixed graph that holds all of them, and node potentials encode throughput. An independent verifier re-checks every solution, and a generator turns its checks into evidence of a safety argument in Goal Structuring Notation. On 9 benchmark instances under period bounds, no rule that fixes patterns before mapping was both always feasible and never more expensive under conservative pricing, while joint exploration was. In the generated arguments, 49 to 62% of the leaves cite verifier checks; the rest are claims a mapping cannot discharge. Optimality within the model was proven for all synthetic graphs with up to 16 actors. This extended version adds the full model, the verifier and generator in detail, the complete catalog and parameters, and a proof of the potential characterization. It also reports every experiment per instance, a mutation analysis of the verifier, and the negative results of the development.

title: Representation Type and Schurian Finiteness of Tits Algebras
abstract: We determine the representation type and Schurian finiteness of the Tits algebra of a finite central real hyperplane arrangement over an algebraically closed field. The algebra is representation-finite when the arrangement has at most two hyperplanes, tame when it has three, and wild when it has at least four. Moreover, it is Schurian-finite if and only if the arrangement has at most two hyperplanes. Both classifications hold over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. The proof combines Saliola's bound-quiver presentation with explicit module constructions, convex subquivers, essentialization, and deletion. In the $\mathbb{R}^2$ case, we describe all eleven indecomposable modules for two lines and construct a full exact embedding of modules over a free algebra for at least four lines.

title: Minimal Subsystems for Characterizing Genuine Multipartite Entanglement
abstract: Genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) is a valuable resource for quantum technologies, but quantifying it in many-body systems can be demanding since measures defined through optimizations over bipartitions are often assumed to require large joint measurements and many measurement settings. We introduce the concepts of GME evaluation length and GME evaluation number, which capture, respectively, the largest subsystem that must be jointly measured and the number of distinct subsystems that need to be measured to evaluate multipartite entanglement measures defined via bipartition optimizations. Taking the genuine multipartite concurrence (GMC) as a canonical example, we show that, for $N$-qubit Haar-random pure states, the GMC can be evaluated using only $N$ single-qubit purity measurements. Thus, for typical many-body states, evaluating the GMC requires considering only the $N$ single-site bipartitions, rather than the exponentially many distinct bipartitions. We further corroborate this behavior numerically for physically accessible states generated by local random quantum circuits. Our results show that the practical cost of quantifying GME can be dramatically lower than suggested by its formal definition, establishing measurement complexity as a complementary operational lens for multipartite entanglement.

title: Limiting distributions of the rightmost eigenvalue of the truncated circular Unitary ensemble across all truncation regimes
abstract: We study the limiting distribution of the largest real part of the eigenvalues of truncated unitary matrices. Let \(U_m\) be an \(m\times m\) Haar-distributed unitary matrix, and let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) be the eigenvalues of its upper-left \(n\times n\) principal submatrix. We determine the limiting distribution of \(\max_{1\le i\le n}\Re Z_i\) under a unified normalization: the limiting law is Gumbel when $q:=m-n\to\infty$ and is of Weibull type when $q$ is fixed. The fixed-\(q\) limiting laws converge to the Gumbel law as \(q\to\infty\). We also give a unified formulation of the normalizing constants for the spectral radius that recovers the previously known limiting laws.

title: RefTAG: Reflection-aware Temporal Audio Grounding in Large Audio Language Models
abstract: Temporal audio grounding requires locating every occurrence of a queried target, making both occurrence counts and interval boundaries essential. We propose RefTAG, a post-training framework for verifiable temporal self-correction. Its Reflection Chain-of-Thought (Re-CoT) protocol combines draft intervals, discrete count and boundary actions, and revised intervals in one response. Supervised fine-tuning on these trajectories (Re-CoT-SFT) teaches the protocol; reinforcement learning (RL) jointly rewards final localization and revision outcomes. Across 8,228 queries, Re-CoT-SFT improves query-weighted mIoU over final-answer SFT by 1.74 percentage points. RL further improves TAG-Bench multi-target mIoU by 0.40 points and R@0.5 by 0.86 points. The final model achieves 38.50% TAG-Bench mIoU and 51.01% mean mIoU across three datasets, outperforming the evaluated open-source MOSS-Audio and FireRedAudio models and the commercial Gemini-3.1-Pro on both measures. These results demonstrate that explicitly coupling count- and boundary-aware revision with joint reward optimization provides an effective and verifiable path to temporal audio grounding.

title: Letter of Intent for Alpha Knockout from Nuclei in Hard Exclusive Processes with ALERT
abstract: We propose to measure hard exclusive $α$-knockout reactions from the light $α$-conjugate nuclei $^{12}$C, $^{16}$O, and $^{20}$Ne using electron scattering. Three reaction channels will be measured for the first time on the same target set: (i) the quasi-elastic knockout $(e, e' α)$ knockout, which establishes a baseline against $α$-clustering model calculations and tests final-state-interaction (FSI) models; (ii) coherent deeply virtual Compton scattering (DVCS) on a bound $α$, which provides a quark-level probe of the bound system through the beam-spin asymmetry; and (iii) coherent vector-meson production ($ϕ$ and J/{$ψ$}) on a bound $α$, which probes the gluon distribution of the bound cluster through two-gluon exchange. The central observables are ratios of cross sections and beam-spin asymmetries between the bound $α$ in $^{12}$C, $^{16}$O, and $^{20}$ Ne and the free $^4$He ground state. Together these measurements directly address the question of the role of QCD in the structure of light nuclei : do the quark and gluon distributions of an $α$ embedded in a heavier nucleus differ from those of a free 4He, and do those modifications track the increasing $α$-clustering strength along the $α$-conjugate chain? The measurement will use the 12 GeV CEBAF accelerator in Hall B with the CLAS12 spectrometer instrumented with the ALERT low-energy recoil detector and high-pressure gas straw targets. ALERT, which replaced the CLAS12 silicon vertex tracker, was successfully commissioned and operated during Run Group L (RG-L) from April through August 2025. It uniquely provides identification of low-momentum recoiling light ions (p, d, t, $^3$He, and $^4$He) close to the beamline at the high luminosities required by these exclusive channels.

title: OneShot: Label-Efficient Detector Weighting for Time Series Anomaly Detection
abstract: Time series (TS) anomaly detection (AD) lacks a universal detector, with the best choice determined by the series rather than by the algorithm. Existing methods therefore either select one detector for each series or average a pool of them. However, both assume that no label ever arrives, while a deployed monitor does receive them, since an operator confirms the alarms it raises. In this paper, we propose ONESHOT, which uses a single confirmed anomaly to weight the pool rather than to choose one detector from it. Specifically, we score each detector on the confirmed anomaly, and those scores become the weights of a soft mixture over the whole pool. We show that a single confirmed anomaly is enough to come close to the best detector for the series. Across 152 univariate and 73 multivariate series, ONESHOT outperforms the strongest single detector, averaging the whole pool, and even picking the best detector on the confirmed event. Code is available at: https://github.com/seunghan96/one_shot.

title: When Participant Disjoint Validation Is Not Enough to Establish Generalization in Parkinson's Gait Classification
abstract: Participant-disjoint cross-validation prevents direct participant overlap, but it may still produce optimistic estimates when acquisition site and diagnosis are structurally dependent. We examined Parkinson's disease classification using 159 pressure-walkway summary features from 133 WearGait-PD participants, including 65 participants with Parkinson's disease and 68 controls. The cohort was non-factorial: two sites contained only one diagnostic group, whereas VA-Seattle was the only site containing both groups. In repeated participant-level nested cross-validation, site alone achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.955 plus or minus 0.003, exceeding the gait-feature model (0.882 plus or minus 0.014). Under the evaluated logistic-regression pipelines, adding gait features to site, age, and sex produced no measurable improvement in pooled discrimination. More site-controlled evaluations produced lower and imprecise estimates: VA-Seattle same-site AUC was 0.668 (95% bootstrap confidence interval 0.477 to 0.836), and the JHOC + Bayview-to-VA-Seattle transport stress test achieved 0.576 (0.375 to 0.770). Supporting within-diagnosis site-prediction and site-conditioned permutation analyses showed that the gait representation retained substantial acquisition-site structure. These findings indicate that participant-disjoint pooled validation did not isolate disease-related discrimination from site-associated variation. They encourage careful examination of site-label dependence and, where possible, support for pooled results through within-site or independent validation before broader claims are made about generalization across institutions.

title: Higher order isoperimetric inequalities and rigidity for surfaces in $\R^n$
abstract: We establish a family of sharp higher order isoperimetric type inequalities for smooth compact surfaces in Euclidean spaces of arbitrary codimension. These inequalities involve arbitrarily high derivatives of the boundary curve, together with the mean curvature vector of the surface. For example, the first and second order inequalities yield the sharp two-sided estimate for the isoperimetric deficit: \begin{align*} & \fracπ{R}\int_{\partial M}|x-Rν|^2\, ds +2π\int_M x\cdot H\, dA \le L^2-4πA\\ \le& \fracπ{R}\int_{\partial M}|x-Rν|^2\, ds +2π\int_M x\cdot H\, dA +\fracπ{3R}\int_{\partial M}|x+R^2κ|^2\, ds, \end{align*} where $R=\frac{L}{2π}$ and the origin is chosen to be the centroid of the boundary. For minimal surfaces, equality in the lower bound holds precisely for flat disks, whereas the second inequality admits non-round equality cases. Our results extend that of Carleman, Sachs, Chakerian, and Li-Schoen-Yau. A distinctive feature of our work is the unexpected rigidity structure arising at higher orders. At the first and second orders, equality curves admit decompositions into circular Fourier modes supported in mutually orthogonal planes. Remarkably, this phenomenon fails at higher orders. We establish a multiplicative factorization of the unit tangent map into elementary planar rotations acting on a fixed unit vector, providing a characterization of equality cases at arbitrary order. As a result, we construct a third order equality curve in $\mathbb R^3$ whose Fourier modes cannot be decomposed into mutually orthogonal circular modes.

title: Optimal Synthesis on the Special Linear Group
abstract: We study the exponential map on the group of real two-by-two matrices with determinant one, endowed with a left-invariant Riemannian metric. Using the Euler-Poincaré equation and its linearization, we determine the conjugate and Maxwell times and identify a domain on which the exponential map is a global diffeomorphism onto the complement of the Maxwell stratum. This provides an alternative proof that the first Maxwell time coincides with the cut time. We obtain an explicit matrix description of the cut locus and characterize the globally minimizing geodesics. Furthermore, we analyze the first Maxwell-time function, determine its unique global minimum, and show that the injectivity radius is $\frac{π\sqrt{14}}{4}$. Finally, we characterize the intersection of the cut and conjugate loci and prove that every geodesic is equi-optimal.

title: Event-Driven Safe Control of a Black-Box Balancing Wheel with Friction-Gated Actuation
abstract: Commercial balancing wheels are closed systems: an internal controller keeps the board upright, and a rider steers by shifting weight and twisting the hips. We augment a one-wheel with a lead-screw weight shift for longitudinal motion and a reaction wheel for yaw.
