abstract: Let $R$ be an integral domain and let $w$ denote the $w$-operation on $R$. A nonzero GV-torsion-free $R$-module $M$ is called $w$-secondary if, for every $r\in R$, either $M/rM$ is GV-torsion or $r^nM=0$ for some $n\in\N$. A $w$-module $M$ is said to admit a $w$-secondary representation if $M=(N_1+\cdots+N_n)_w$, where each $N_i$ is a $w$-secondary submodule of $M$. Such a representation is called minimal if the ideals $P_i=\sqrt{\Ann_R(N_i)}$ are pairwise distinct, and $M$ is called $w$-representable if it admits such a representation. If the sum can be chosen direct, then $M$ is called strongly $w$-representable. We characterize $w$-secondary modules and investigate their localization and $w$-closure properties. For a nonfield domain $R$, we prove that $R$ is $t$-almost Dedekind if and only if $\wdim R=1$ and every $w$-representable $w$-module is locally strongly $w$-representable: each of its nonzero localizations at maximal $w$-ideals is strongly representable. Global strong $w$-representability is retained when all the radical annihilators in the representation are nonzero.

title: Rigidity results for overdetermined problems of p-Laplace equation with spatially dependent data
abstract: Let $p>1$ and $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded smooth domain. We study the following overdetermined problem for the p-Laplacian: \begin{equation*} \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} -Δ_p u=f(x)&x\inΩ,\\ u=0&x\in\partialΩ,\\ \frac{\partial u}{\partialν}=g(x)&x\in\partialΩ, \end{array} \right. \end{equation*} where $ν$ is the inward unit normal to $\partialΩ$ and both data may depend on position. A boundary-local version of the moving-plane argument is developed for the possibly degenerate p-Laplace operator. The advantage of this argument is that it avoids the analysis of the degenerate set of the p-Laplacian. Under some reasonable structural conditions, we prove that the solvability of the above mentioned problem forces the domain to be a ball, the source to be radial, and the Neumann datum to be a suitable constant. We also give an explicit formula for the solution. Further consequences include one directional domain symmetry, the conclusion that full rigidity follows from reflection information in any set of directions whose linear reflections generate a dense subgroup of the orthogonal group $O(n)$, and a constant mean curvature characterization.

title: On Measures of Dissimilarity on the Majorization Simplex
abstract: The majorization simplex $\mathcal{P}_n$ is the set of probability vectors of length $n$ whose entries are arranged in non-increasing order. Under the majorization order, $\mathcal{P}_n$ is a lattice, and it is the natural space for comparing distributions when the labels of the outcomes are not relevant. In this work, we study measures of dissimilarity (and, similarity) on $\mathcal{P}_n$. Our first set of results concerns the Rényi-entropy based distance $d_α(p,q)=H_α(p)+H_α(q)-2H_α(p\vee q)$ proposed by Yadav and Shkel (2026), which generalizes a metric of Cicalese, Gargano and Vaccaro (2013). We show that $d_α$ is a metric on $\mathcal{P}_n$ for $α\in[1,\infty)$, while for $α\in[0,1)\cup\{\infty\}$, $d_α$ is not a metric in general. Our main result in this part identifies the necessary and sufficient conditions for equality in the triangle inequality of $d_α$ when $α>1$, for which we identify the equality conditions for the supermodularity of the Rényi entropy $H_α$. Our second set of results concerns the total variation distance and the Hellinger affinity (also called the Bhattacharyya coefficient) on $\mathcal{P}_n$. We obtain a number of bounds on these measures, along with some of their equality conditions. The resulting Hellinger affinity based upper bound on the total variation distance can be smaller than the bounds obtained from Pinsker's and the Bretagnolle--Huber inequalities.

title: A No-Go Theorem for Nonspherical Bounces with a Single Negative Mode
abstract: False vacuum decay is conventionally described by a spherically symmetric bounce with a single negative fluctuation mode. This raises a fundamental question: can the single negative mode requirement itself enforce spherical symmetry, independently of action minimization? For a single real scalar field with a smooth potential in flat spacetime, we rigorously prove that every localized nonspherical saddle with zero initial velocity has at least three negative modes. Additional reflection symmetries further tighten these bounds, as illustrated in a sextic scalar model. Our findings exclude nonspherical bounce candidates with a single negative mode, providing a complementary spectral foundation for the spherical bounce description of false vacuum decay.

title: EHR-Bench: A Chinese Multi-Task Benchmark for Recruitment AI
abstract: Recruitment applications span diverse operations, from drafting job descriptions and interpreting queries to organizing profiles, assessing fit, and recommending candidates and jobs. Systematic LLM evaluation therefore requires task coverage that reflects this range of business needs. We introduce EHR-Bench, an open Chinese benchmark comprising twelve tasks across six capability families and five recruitment scenarios. The tasks cover generation, extraction, classification, retrieval, semantic similarity, and reciprocal ranking within one evaluation framework. An internal recruitment dataset guides task definitions, the occupation taxonomy and sampling targets, output requirements, and scoring protocols. Following these specifications, we construct 8,336 task instances from public materials and controlled augmentation, with source-aware expert review and documented provenance. We evaluate twelve LLMs through task-level, capability-level, and aggregate comparisons. Closely ranked models exhibit distinct task strengths, and performance varies across input sources, reference evidence, and candidate pools. Five shared models retain the same observed Overall ordering on a private operational reference, with variation in capability and task correspondence. EHR-Bench provides a reproducible foundation for systematic model assessment, task-specific model selection, and further research on LLMs for recruitment. The project repository is available at https://github.com/EhrBench/EHR-Bench.

title: 2D Block OMP for Near-Field Channel Estimation with Extremely Large-Scale UPA
abstract: Channel estimation for extremely large-scale uniform planar arrays (UPAs) requires exploiting near-field channel structure to reduce pilot overhead. With a specifically devised channel representation matrix, the near-field channel exhibits a 2D sparse structure, which a conventional 1D block partition might divide into multiple groups. This work develops a 2D block orthogonal matching pursuit (2D-BOMP) estimator that exploits this structure through rectangular coefficient grouping. We establish sufficient recovery conditions for noiseless and noisy measurements and compare the sufficient pilot-length requirements of 1D and 2D partitions. Numerical simulations demonstrate the estimation benefits of 2D-BOMP in estimating the near-field channels of large-scale UPAs, compared with the conventional 1D-BOMP as well as the polar-domain based OMP method.

title: StageBreaker: Shifting Video RL Post-Training Scheduling from Stages down to Data Dependencies
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training has emerged as the key paradigm for improving autoregressive video models. Emerging vision-language reward models further strengthen post-training with accurate rewards, but their long chain-of-thought inference substantially raises the associated costs, while the pursuit of long videos prolongs policy training. Despite these rising costs, existing video RL systems still adopt coarse-grained stage-centric execution, which stalls policy training until all reward evaluation finishes, replays every trajectory twice due to a further barrier within policy training, and induces load imbalance across GPUs. To address the challenges, we propose StageBreaker, a fine-grained data-dependency-driven scheduling framework, which schedules the true dataflow of an RL step rather than its stages. Specifically, StageBreaker overlaps policy training with reward evaluation by exploiting reward-separable policy training, and merges the two trajectory replays into one by leveraging loss-independent back-propagation. It further balances GPU load by scheduling computation at the finer granularity. Our evaluation results show that StageBreaker achieves a speedup of up to 1.41$\times$ over stage-centric execution.

title: 3D-VITAL: Visibility-aware Identity Training from Artificial Liftings of 3D Reconstruction model for Cross-View Object Re-Identification
abstract: We address the Cross-View Object Re-Identification (ReID) task, aiming to match identities across drastically different viewpoints. We focus on Single-View Aerial-Ground ReID (SV AG-ReID), where models train on one viewpoint and must generalize to another at inference. To bridge this viewpoint gap, related work employs generative models to synthesize novel views from source images as additional training data. We leverage recent advances in large-scale single-view 3D mesh reconstruction to lift source images into textured meshes and to render them from new viewpoints. However, this pipeline produces unreliable data in two distinct ways. First, the reconstruction may fail and produce geometrically incorrect meshes, resulting in severe corruption in rendered novel views. Second, even when the geometry is correct, the rendered novel views contain hallucinated textures in regions not visible in the source image. The reconstructed mesh carries a per-pixel partition between regions visible from the source view and regions that the reconstruction model had to hallucinate, available as a deterministic byproduct of rendering. We introduce this per-pixel visibility map and exploit it in a two-stage design. Cross-View Consistency Filtering (CVCF) discards geometrically incorrect meshes by ensuring multi-view consistency between source and novel views over visible patches. Visibility-Aware Attention Supervision (VAAS) leverages the visibility map to guide the model's attention toward reliable regions of the rendered view during training. Combined, these two components enable our method, 3D-VITAL, to better leverage the synthetic signal from single-view 3D mesh reconstruction. 3D-VITAL sets a new state-of-the-art on three SV AG-ReID benchmarks. Code and data will be released at https://github.com/TurtleSmoke/3D-VITAL.

title: Surface-to-Volume Homogenization of NonLinear Steklov Eigencouples with NonHomogeneous Orlicz Growth in Perforated Domains
abstract: We study normalized principal Steklov eigencouples on periodically perforated domains when both the bulk energy and the boundary normalization have general, possibly nonhomogeneous, Orlicz growth. The surface term on the hole boundaries carries the critical surface-to-volume scaling. For each fixed mass level, the constrained minima converge along the whole family, while selected minimizers, fluxes and Lagrange multipliers converge along subsequences to the corresponding objects of a homogenized problem. In the limit, the bulk operator is given by a convex cell problem, and the boundary term becomes a volume term weighted by the total surface density of the reference hole. The key tool is a strong approximation of the microscopic traces by cell averages, measured in the scaled surface modular.

title: Feature-Context Consistency: Unsupervised Adversarial Detection with Drift Stability on Attributed Graphs
abstract: Adversarial detection on evolving attributed graphs faces two challenges: fraud labels arrive late or not at all, and natural distributional drift erodes any trained decision boundary. Modern detectors can reach strong detection rates when labels are available and the distribution is stationary; sustaining that quality without labels and under drift is the open problem. We identify feature-context consistency -- the alignment between a node's attributes and its aggregated neighborhood attributes -- as a single structural signal that addresses both. We formalize it as the Context Boost (CB) score within a Restricted Boltzmann Machine framework (CB-RBM) and prove two complementary worst-case guarantees: a strict separation between the expected CB of legitimate and adversarial nodes, with gap growing linearly in model capacity, whenever the adversary's context stays far enough from legitimate neighborhood context; and a Wasserstein-Lipschitz bound on how far the CB distribution moves under natural drift. We validate on XBlock Ethereum phishing (~153K nodes) and Reddit banned-user detection (~11K nodes), with two further datasets in the appendix spanning diverse domains. With zero labels, CB-RBM achieves AUROC >= 0.96 on four adversarial attacks and keeps FPR close to its calibrated 5% target under drift -- outperforming supervised GNNs (hundreds of labels), unsupervised graph-anomaly baselines, and a standard RBM whose FPR collapses to 89-100%. What typically requires separate mechanisms -- label-free operation and drift stability -- here follows from a single structural regularity of the data. Code: https://github.com/serval-uni-lu/CB-RBM.

title: Colloid-Colloid Interactions Impact Network Morphology of Confined Colloidal Drying Patterns
abstract: Colloidal suspensions that are confined between two closely spaced plates and left to evaporate slowly form maze-like labyrinth patterns in the final stage of evaporation. The fingers in these patterns form bifurcations and occasionally loops, which we may quantify with a skeletonization method. We compare drying patterns formed with two different salt concentrations in the droplet which changes the screening length and therefore the effective colloid interactions. We find that the junctions generally follow Murray's law for optimal transport networks, and that the typical bifurcation angles peak around 53. Screened droplets additionally show more loopy networks, and is characterized by bands of transversal fingers before merging into a central non-fingering colloidal aggregate. Our observations suggest that colloid-colloid interactions can strongly influence the large-scale topology of the pattern while leaving the local geometry of the individual fingers unchanged.

title: Belief Space Planning for Risk Signal Temporal Logic via Mixed-Integer Convex Programming
abstract: Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specifies robot tasks with spatio-temporal requirements, and its robustness semantics allow planning by trajectory optimization. In practice, robots estimate their state from noisy measurements, and when the information gained from a measurement depends on the state, the robot can actively reduce its uncertainty by planning in the belief space. The resulting problem is, however, generally non-convex, for which gradient-based methods are neither complete nor globally optimal. In this paper, we consider Risk STL (RiSTL) planning in Gaussian belief space and show that an information-form parameterization of the belief, together with a convex relaxation of the belief dynamics, yields a mixed-integer convex program (MICP). We prove that the MICP is sound and complete, and that the relaxation preserves the globally optimal input trajectories. We validate the effectiveness of our method in numerical simulations.

title: Sharp parameter gaps for quantized Mabuchi energies and cscK metrics
abstract: For polarized manifolds, we show that semistability for the quantized Mabuchi energy at one fixed finite parameter is equivalent to uniform K-stability and to unique existence of constant scalar curvature Kähler (cscK) metrics. We obtain sharp comparisons between quantized Mabuchi slopes at different parameters and with the ordinary Mabuchi slope. In the presence of automorphisms, we give an equivariant criterion using torus twists under the vanishing of the Futaki character. The estimates also hold for finite-energy geodesic rays in compact Kähler classes. On a fixed ruled surface with discrete automorphism group, we construct cscK polarizations with unbounded critical parameters. Their ratios to the $α$-invariant are also unbounded.

title: GQL Datatypes as an RDF Vocabulary
abstract: The ISO GQL standard introduces a rich value-type system for property graphs, including scalar, temporal, byte-string, list, record, and dynamic union datatypes. The vocabulary presented here additionally covers a vector extension. At the same time, RDF-based knowledge graph systems identify literal datatypes by IRIs and interpret typed literals through value spaces, lexical spaces, and lexical-to-value mappings. This paper presents the GQL Datatypes RDF Vocabulary, a lightweight RDF vocabulary that represents selected GQL datatypes and the vector extension as RDF datatype IRIs and describes their hierarchy, aliases, and selected constraints using RDF, RDFS, OWL, and XML Schema Datatypes vocabulary terms. The vocabulary is intended to support interoperability between GQL-oriented property graph systems and RDF-based knowledge graph systems. We describe its namespace and datatype model, summarize its datatype coverage, and show how the accompanying generator and validator use the vocabulary. In the reference implementation, RDF literals retain GQL datatype IRIs; XSD mappings declared in the vocabulary support scalar validation, while lists, records, and vectors are encoded directly as JSON lexical forms of vocabulary-typed literals.

title: Investigation of RIS Integration in Satellite Systems Guided by ITU-R VSAT Radiation Diagram
abstract: The introduction of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) technology marks a transformative era in modern communication systems, enhancing coverage and facilitating higher data transmission rates. While recent research has delved into the integration of RIS into satellite networks, a critical and practical gap persists concerning its implementation in the satellite-Very Small Aperture Terminal (VSAT) downlink, specifically amplifying contributions from the VSAT side. This paper addresses this gap by proposing a simple and engineering methodology to optimize RIS position and orientation, incorporating considerations for the antennas' radiation patterns and the system's topology to streamline optimization variables. The primary objective of this paper is to alleviate the double fading constraint in the reflect link without the need for active elements, achieved by leveraging the Fresnel zone of the RIS. The improvement power ratio depends on the frequency and the VSAT 's diameter. The results show that for a VSAT with diameter 1m the gain is up to 9dB at 2 GHz (S band) and up to 14dB at 4 GHz (C band). Additionally, the RIS channel equation is refined, encompassing the tropospheric attenuation and accounting for electromagnetic wave polarization.

title: Well-posedness for the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi-Dirac-Fokker-Planck equation
abstract: This paper is concerned with space inhomogeneous Fermi-Dirac-Fokker-Planck equation posed on a classical kinetic phase space. The nonlinear factor $f(1-f)$ appears both in the transport term and in the collison part of the Fokker-Planck operator, accounting for the exclusion principle of fermions. Solutions are subject to the physical constraint $0\leq f\leq 1$. Previous existing results have mainly been obtained under suitable smallness or close-to-equilibrium assumptions. A main difficulty stems from the nonlinear and degenerate parabolic structure of the equation. We prove the existence and uniqueness of global solutions without any smallness or close-to-equilibrium assumptions. To construct solutions, we use a vanishing viscosity approximation by adding a Laplacian in the spatial variable. We derive uniform estimates for the regularized problem and obtain compactness in the space of functions of bounded variation $(BV),$ allowing us to pass to the limit as the spatial viscosity vanishes. Since the limiting equation is degenerate with a nonlinear transport, we formulate an appropriate notion of entropy solutions incorporating the kinetic structure of the equation. We prove uniqueness within this class and show that every vanishing-viscosity limit satisfies the entropy formulation. Our result provides a global well-posedness theory beyond the perturbative regime.

title: Estimation of Rational Inattention--Additive Random Utility Models
abstract: This paper develops likelihood-based estimation for parametric rational inattention--additive random utility models. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality of the exact maximum likelihood estimator and provide conditions under which the simulated estimator shares its asymptotic distribution. To implement estimation, we develop Newton--BA, a KKT-guided hybrid of Newton--Raphson and Blahut--Arimoto (BA). The algorithm accommodates both interior and boundary solutions and substantially improves computational efficiency relative to direct BA while preserving numerical accuracy. Monte Carlo simulations show that parameter recovery improves with sample size and that confidence-interval coverage is generally close to the nominal $95$ percent level. Finally, we compare our model with no- and perfect-information logit benchmarks in an empirically calibrated ModeCanada experiment. Our model achieves similar in-sample likelihood fit to perfect-information logit but more accurately recovers key preference parameters, choice probabilities, and responses to travel-time changes.

title: Fisher-Information Certification from Bell Statistics: CHSH Bounds, Information Loss, and Finite-Data Guarantees
abstract: Bell-test data are typically used to certify nonlocal correlations, while quantum metrology is concerned with the sensitivity of measurement statistics to unknown parameters. Here we connect these tasks at the level of experimentally accessible Bell statistics. Using standard moment-based Fisher-information inequalities, we derive lower bounds on the classical Fisher information directly from Bell scores and their parameter dependence, without requiring full state tomography. For CHSH measurements we establish a hierarchy between the information contained in the full outcome record, the set of individual correlators, and the compressed Bell parameter, thereby quantifying the metrological cost of data compression. In polarization-phase sensing, this hierarchy reveals a Bell-metrology tradeoff: the point of maximal CHSH violation need not maximize, and can even suppress, the Fisher information carried by the Bell score itself. We further derive finite-sample lower-confidence bounds from coincidence counts and analyze the effects of biased marginals, accidental coincidences, visibility loss, and multipair emission. The framework provides a practical route for extracting metrological guarantees from Bell-type experiments using only standard correlation measurements.

title: Piercing boxes and products of trees
abstract: We give a new upper bound on the piercing number $τ(\mathcal{F})$ of a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of axis-parallel rectangles in the plane when every $p$ members contain an intersecting pair. Namely, we prove $τ(\mathcal{F}) = O(p(\log\log p)(\log\log\log p))$, improving the factor $(\log\log p)^2$ in the best previously known bound to $(\log\log p)(\log\log\log p)$. For each $d>2$, when $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite family of axis-parallel boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$, this yields $τ(\mathcal{F}) = O(p(\log p)^{d-2}(\log\log p)(\log\log\log p))$. We also study an analogous problem replacing $\mathbb{R}^d=\mathbb{R}\times\cdots\times\mathbb{R}$ with the Cartesian product $T_1\square\cdots\square T_d$ of trees $T_1,\ldots,T_d$, and boxes with objects of the form $S_1\square\cdots\square S_d$ where $S_i$ is a subtree of $T_i$. For a finite family of such objects under the same intersection assumption as above, we establish an upper bound $τ(\mathcal{F})=O(p(\log p)^{d-1})$ for each $d$. We also construct examples showing that this upper bound cannot be improved in order of magnitude.

title: The manufacture of examples II: the "para-classical" orthogonal polynomials
abstract: Under the stated regularity assumptions, the full orthogonality functionals of the five finite para-families considered here are classical for the respective affine, quadratic, $q$-quadratic, $q$-linear and alternating calculi. For each of the para-Krawtchouk, para-Racah, $q$-para-Racah and $q$-para-Krawtchouk families, two finite solutions of one global structural equation have $N+1$ nodes altogether and common moments through degree $N-1$. Their relative mass changes only the central recurrence coefficients. We prove regularity for every normalised combination with both component masses non-zero and recover the full published functionals and recurrences. The alternating construction identifies para-Bannai-Ito within the same structural framework. For the four non-alternating families, equal positive combinations give persymmetric Jacobi matrices; the known spectral gap criterion then decides perfect state transfer. Explicit parameter correspondences locate the classical components and resonant limits of the full systems. A positive seven-point example shows how further named families can be manufactured without a new governing principle. Counterexamples to mathematical assertions in three of four recent preprints expose the consequences of insufficient hypotheses for finite representations and physical models. In an era of AI-assisted symbolic production, we call for a standard that rewards structural explanation and verification rather than the proliferation of examples.

title: Averaged Annealed Markov Chains Achieve the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA, Part I: Glauber Dynamics
abstract: In the tensor principal components analysis (tensor PCA) problem, we are asked to recover an unknown vector in $\{\pm1\}^N$ from a noisy observation of its $k$-th tensor power, for a fixed $k\ge3$. Tensor PCA exhibits a well-studied information-computation gap: global algorithms such as spectral methods and sum-of-squares work above an algorithmic threshold, below which we know matching lower bounds (against these and some other restricted models of computation). In contrast, local algorithms such as Markov chains were only known to succeed from a random initialization at a polynomially larger signal-to-noise ratio, and were believed to be inferior to global algorithms for tensor PCA. We show that Glauber dynamics, when supplemented with annealing and ergodic averaging, achieves polynomial-time strong recovery above the algorithmic threshold from a uniformly random initialization, demonstrating that local Markov chains can succeed all the way down to the algorithmic threshold from an uninformative cold start.

title: Finiteness of open substacks with proper moduli spaces
abstract: For an algebraic stack of finite type, we construct a finite stratification of an atlas such that every universally closed open substack pulls back to a union of strata. As a result, there are only finitely many open substacks admitting a proper adequate moduli space.

title: Universal Distributed Feature Extraction Complementary to Side Information via H-Score
abstract: This paper considers a distributed estimation system where edge nodes transmit averaged features to a center node for parameter estimation. A key challenge arises when the center node possesses auxiliary side information: how to design local extractors that are universally optimal for any downstream task, while avoiding redundancy with the side information. To tackle this problem, we orthogonally decompose the joint function space and demonstrate in the weak-dependence regime that the modal decomposition of the canonical dependence kernel's conditional-additive component yields optimal, task-independent features. We construct a distributed nested H-score to learn this decomposition and show that, under a limited feature budget, the mean-squared error (MSE) gap to the best task-specific features is determined solely by the task's alignment with the discarded, least informative modes, and vanishes to leading order for every square-integrable task once the budget is sufficient.

title: About P-adic Numbers and Professor Igor Volovich on the Occasion of his 80th Anniversary
abstract: We recall a 1987 paper written by Volovich and our subsequent work with Okada which established the Feyman rules for the p-adic string and the related non-local field theory which found diverse physical applications. We add some memories of visits to Moscow during 1989-91.

title: Attention-Graph Curvature for the Verification of Mathematical Reasoning
abstract: Language models have recently solved open Erdős problems and achieved gold-medal level performance on International Mathematical Olympiad problems. But their solutions, written in natural language, cannot yet be verified by proof assistants. An erroneous reasoning step can invalidate every step that comes after, so it is advantageous to detect errors early. Several methods have been proposed to detect erroneous reasoning quickly based on the features of the forward pass of the language model that performs reasoning. In this work, we study whether the directed Forman curvature of that model's attention graph, a local quantity computed at an edge from the attention weights around it, carries information about a step's correctness. To do so, we evaluate four per-step verifiers on ProcessBench with and without the curvature appended to their input. Appending curvature values improves the overall mean performance of all four verifiers. ReProbe, the verifier that takes every token of a step as input, shows the largest improvement. Adding the curvature increases the time of the language model's forward pass by 18% on average.

title: Environmental Dependence of Satellite Planarity and Orbital-Pole Coherence around Milky Way Analogues in a Hydrodynamical Cosmological Simulation
abstract: We examine whether the unusual spatial flattening and orbital-plane coherence of the Milky Way's classical satellites are connected to the Galaxy's location in the cosmic web. We compare the 11 classical satellites with the 11 most massive satellites of 11,922 Milky Way-mass hosts in the TNG300-1 hydrodynamical simulation. We measure flattening with both the simple inertia tensor (SIT), which retains radial information, and the reduced inertia tensor (RIT), which isolates angular anisotropy. Orbital-plane coherence is characterized by the minimum opening angle containing the axes of the eight most coplanar satellite orbits. For the Milky Way, we find $(c/a,b/a)=(0.183,0.558)$ for SIT and $(0.364,0.736)$ for RIT, together with an eight-orbit opening angle of $21.9^\circ$. The corresponding fractions of simulated systems at least as extreme are $4.94\%$, $12.28\%$, and $5.04\%$, respectively. We describe the environment using the velocity-shear tensor smoothed on $2\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$ and compare the full sample with Local Group-like pairs, systems whose shear eigenvalues match those reconstructed for the Local Group, and hosts in knots, filaments, sheets, and voids. Among the well-sampled environmental subsets, the shape and opening-angle distributions differ only weakly. Although the cosmic web imprints preferred orientations on host spins and satellite orbital-plane axes, the Milky Way combines orientations that are uncommon in the simulation. We conclude that the present-day cosmic-web environment alone does not substantially increase the occurrence of Milky Way-like satellite configurations. This result does not rule out an origin in anisotropic accretion, since neither the present-day web class nor its shear eigenvalues fully encodes the assembly history of an individual satellite system.

title: 1/f frequency-noise reduction in nanomechanical resonators by dissipation dilution
abstract: The frequency noise of a resonant nanomechanical sensor is well understood down to its thermomechanical limit, but the longest useful averaging time is set by a flicker, or $1/f$, frequency-noise floor whose origin has remained unknown. We show that this floor is the thermal noise of the tension. By the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, the tension of a resonator with fixed ends fluctuates by an amount set by the loss angle of its material; for structural damping, these fluctuations produce $1/f$ frequency noise with a flicker coefficient $h_{-1}=E k_{\mathrm{B}} T/(2πVσ_0^2 Q_{\mathrm{el}})$, with $Q_{\mathrm{el}}$ the intrinsic loss under elongation, that contains no free parameter and is diluted by the tensile stress $σ_0$ in the same way as damping is in dissipation dilution. Silicon nitride strings and membranes from 30 to 340~nm thickness follow the predicted volume scaling, the predicted $σ_0^{-2}$ dilution across resonators and within stress-engineered strings, and the predicted thickness dependence, which places noise-active two-level systems in the volume and at the surfaces of the resonators, all at the absolute level set by the independently measured intrinsic loss. The same relation accounts for published data between 78 and 296~K; below 78~K, the loss measured at the resonance no longer represents the loss probed by the noise, marking the limit of the structural-damping assumption. Dissipation dilution therefore lowers the $1/f$ floor, and the longest useful integration time of a resonant sensor is set by its prestress, volume, temperature, and intrinsic loss angle.

title: Spectral extremal problems on $[a,b]$-factors in binding graphs, and beyond
abstract: The binding number $b(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum value of $|N_{G}(X)|/|X|$ taken over all nonempty sets $X\subseteq V(G)$ such that $N_{G}(X)\neq V(G)$. A graph $G$ is 1-binding if $b(G)\geq 1$. Fan and Lin [Electron. J. Combin. 31 (2024) P1.30] characterized the unique spectral extremal graphs among 1-binding graphs with $δ(G)\geq k$ that contain no $k$-factor for $k=1$, $2$. Subsequently, Tang and Zhang solved the problem for $k\geq 3$. Note that $δ(G)\geq a$ is a necessary condition for the existence of an $[a,b]$-factor in a graph $G$. For $1\leq a<b$, Fan et al. [Discrete Math. 349 (2026) 115103] determined the unique spectral extremal graph $H_n^{a,b}$ among connected graphs with $δ(G)\geq a$ that contain no $[a,b]$-factor. Note that $b(H_n^{a,b})<1$. This motivates the corresponding spectral extremal problem for 1-binding graphs. Note that every 1-binding graph with $δ(G)\geq 1$ contains a $[1,b]$-factor for $b>1$. For $2\leq a<b$, we in this paper determine the unique extremal graph $\mathcal{B}_n^{a,b}$ with the maximum spectral radius among 1-binding graphs of order $n$ with $δ(G)\geq a$ that contain no $[a,b]$-factor. The toughness of a non-complete graph $G$ is $t(G)=\min\{\frac{|X|}{c(G-X)}\mid X\subseteq V(G)\, \text{and}\, c(G-X)\geq 2\}$. A graph $G$ is 1-tough if $c(G-X)\leq |X|$ for every $X\subseteq V(G)$ with $c(G-X)\geq 2$. Every 1-tough graph of order $n\geq2$ is 1-binding. Note that $t(\mathcal{B}_n^{a,b})<1$. This leads us to investigate the corresponding spectral extremal problem for 1-tough graphs. Note that every 1-tough graph with $δ(G)\geq 1$ contains a $[1,b]$-factor for $b>1$. For $2\leq a<b$, we in this paper characterize the unique extremal graph with the maximum spectral radius among 1-tough graphs of order $n$ with $δ(G)\geq a$ containing no $[a,b]$-factor.

title: Audit Before You Distill: A Controlled Workflow for Reasoning Transfer into Compact Medical Language Models
abstract: Teacher rationales can help a smaller model answer health professions questions, but they can also reinforce errors. We examined when they help and how this evidence can guide training using Brazilian Portuguese questions from medical and multiprofessional residency examinations. First, we measured how a teacher rationale changed the student's probability of selecting the correct answer and compared this effect with rationales drawn from other questions. The complete rationale increased this probability by 21~p.p. when the teacher was correct and decreased it by 14~p.p. when the teacher was wrong. By intervening on the reasoning content, we showed that shuffled rationales did not produce the same pattern. Guided by this result, we trained only with rationales attached to correct teacher answers and compared answer-only training, step-by-step distillation, and our proposed Distill-SFT method. Distill-SFT showed a modest advantage over step-by-step distillation on previously missed questions under reasoning, while using fewer training instances by combining the answer and rationale into a single target. We also investigated catastrophic forgetting using the out-of-domain ENEM dataset. Answer-only training reduced reasoning accuracy by 12~p.p. relative to baseline, compared with approximately 4~p.p. for either rationale-based training method. Together, these findings support a workflow that audits rationale content before distillation, verifies teacher answers before supervision, and trains compact models efficiently for health professions question answering.

title: Forecasting carbon-risk hotspots ahead of the extreme 2026 El Niño
abstract: A potentially super El Niño is forecasted in 2026, raising the need to anticipate land carbon-cycle risks before its impacts unfold. We develop a prospective early-warning framework that uses dynamic global vegetation models driven by an ensemble of ECMWF seasonal climate forecasts and machine-learning burned area predictions. Forecasts indicate a $0.23 \pm 0.21$ PgC reduction in global net biome productivity in the second half of 2026, with hotspots of sink weakening in eastern South America and elevated fire risk in Southeast Asia.

title: The Online Steinitz Problem
abstract: Inspired by Steinitz's celebrated result (1913) and recent online vector-balancing results of Kulkarni et al. (2024) and Aden-Ali (2026), we introduce the online Steinitz problem: $T$ vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, each of $\ell_2$-norm at most $1$ and with total sum zero, arrive one at a time and must be assigned immediately and irrevocably to unused positions of an array. The goal is to keep every prefix sum of the resulting order small. We first obtain deterministic prefix-discrepancy bounds of $O(\log T)$ for $d=1$ and $O(\sqrt T)$ for $d\ge2$. Our main contribution is a general reduction that converts deterministic and randomized online vector-balancing algorithms, which assign signs to arriving vectors, into online ordering algorithms. Combined with recent vector-balancing results, this yields a randomized algorithm with prefix discrepancy $O(\log T+\sqrt{d\log T})$ and running time $O(dT\log T)$. The guarantee holds with high probability against an oblivious adversary. The reduction also gives bounds for sparse vectors and extends to inputs in arbitrary compact convex bodies. Finally, we prove matching lower bounds in both the deterministic and randomized cases.

title: Versatile two-layer model for thermohydraulic prediction of microchannel heat sinks
abstract: Three-dimensional conjugate heat-transfer simulations provide detailed predictions for microchannel heat sinks but can be computationally demanding when many geometries and operating conditions are evaluated. This study develops a versatile two-layer model (VTLM) that reduces the three-dimensional problem to two coupled two-dimensional fields while retaining the in-plane geometry of the flow passages and fins. Effects associated with the unresolved channel-height direction are incorporated through hydraulic and thermal closures that account for wall friction and the fluid- and fin-side contributions to interlayer heat transfer. The closures are evaluated from the representative channel geometry, flow-development condition, and fin configuration. The VTLM was assessed against three-dimensional reference models across broad ranges of channel aspect ratios and operating conditions, including uniform and nonuniform fin arrangements. Compared with the existing two-layer models, the VTLM showed improved overall agreement with the three-dimensional reference results. The results showed that prediction accuracy was governed mainly by the flow-development condition and channel aspect ratio, from which a conservative screening guideline was proposed for the examined straight-channel configurations. The assessment of finned expansion--contraction channels further supported the applicability of the VTLM to the investigated passages with abrupt width changes. Overall, the VTLM provides a reduced-dimensional framework for thermohydraulic analysis across the range of microchannel heat-sink configurations examined in this study without explicitly resolving the channel-height direction.

title: Where Is the "Self" of a Large Language Model? -- From Self-Index to Self-Reference
abstract: We separate two functional levels of self familiar from biology: a self-index, which separates one's own from external material and shapes processing, as corollary discharge does in nearly all animals, and self-reference, the higher ability to recognize what is one's own, as in mirror self-recognition. We probe both by placing the same text in an Assistant, User, or System message rendered by the model's own chat template. In Qwen3.8-27B we report three levels of evidence. Persistence: as predicted in advance, the representation of the text separates the model's own message from both external sources at all 64 layers and for every text. Coupling: asked who wrote the preceding message, the model claims its own messages (0.77) and assigns User and System messages alike to the user, and how strongly it claims each message is predicted by the size of its self-index (Spearman up to 0.68). Intervention: exchanging the internal states that follow a message reverses the self-attribution between layers 15 and 31; removing the self-index direction from them at layer 39 lowers the claim more than a random direction; and in arithmetic the model adopts a wrong step more often when it wrote the step itself (0.92 versus 0.75). Across eight open-weight models from four families, the levels are nested and do not follow model size: three models show neither, three a self-index without self-reference, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next recognizes its own messages only after reasoning (0.66, none of the external ones), and only Qwen3.8-27B shows both without thinking; no model shows self-reference without a self-index, and reasoning brings it out only where one exists. We propose that self-reference is a higher-level ability built on a self-index, a content-independent displacement superimposed on the whole representation of the model's own messages, and that neither level is a by-product of problem-solving ability.

title: Safeguarding Intelligent Power Dispatch:A Performance-Equivalent-Model-Based Safety-Critical Control Method for DC Microgrids
abstract: Intelligent power dispatch is enabling fast and self-adaptive decision-making in microgrids, yet its deployment in real-world industry remains limited due to unresolved safety concerns. Existing safety-preserving approaches typically rely on an accurate characterization of the feasible operating region, which is impossible to obtain under uncertain and heterogeneous system dynamics. Moreover, even a dispatch command verified as feasible at a discrete setpoint may become unsafe during its continuous physical execution. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a safety-aware dispatch adjustment framework that uses performance-equivalent modeling of closed-loop systems (PEM-CLS) and embeds high-order control barrier functions and control Lyapunov functions within a quadratic programming formulation (HOCBF-CLF-QP). PEM-CLS captures EMS-required power-regulation dynamics solely from port-level responses, without requiring internal subsystem models, parameters, or controller information. Its modeling error is analytically characterized and explicitly bounded, enabling requirement-oriented dynamic abstraction for safety-critical control. Based on these PEMs, the HOCBF-CLF-QP safety controller coordinates heterogeneous transient power responses and corrects unsafe EMS commands to maintain dynamic safety during command execution. Four deliberately constructed extreme stress-test scenarios are used to expose conflicts between nominal EMS commands and physical safety. Without intervention, the DC-bus voltage violates its safety limit in all four cases, whereas the proposed framework maintains QP feasibility and limits the voltage deviation. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an algorithm-agnostic safety execution layer for intelligent power dispatch without requiring an exact feasible-region model or detailed internal information of lower-level devices.

title: Realistic simulation of universal multiport interferometers with losses within a Gaussian formalism
abstract: Photonic technologies are among the leading platform contenders for demonstrating quantum advantage. Nevertheless, photon losses represent the major hurdle for the realization of a fault-tolerant optical quantum computer, and the need for an accurate characterization of this phenomenon is crucial for classical simulations of quantum algorithms on noisy backends. The noisy regime would require the simulation of the algorithm on a Fock backend or rather assuming the a priori hypothesis on the uniformity of the optical losses, which may lead to wrong predictions about the outcome from the algorithm on a cerain hardware. We propose a Gaussian model that can reproduce a lossy dynamics through the experimental characterization of imperfect interferometers, yielding the corresponding mean vector and the covariance matrix. Such model can be adapted to any continuous-variable architecture (spatial or time-bin encoded) and for both the Gaussian boson sampling or general-dyne based algorithms. Eventually, we quantify the drift of optical losses from being uniform throughout the multiport interferometer by a numerical simulation. This work proposes a blueprint for future characterizations, tailor-suited for specific devices and architectures, as well as for potential error correction and mitigation techniques, and it paves the way for realistic simulations of quantum algorithms on NISQ optical platforms.

title: Learn from Move: the Next Step for GUI Agents
abstract: Existing benchmarks for GUI agents primarily focus on increasing task difficulty by extending task horizons. Besides, enabling agents to explore unfamiliar environments and successfully complete tasks within them is also a critical yet challenging problem. We introduce LatentGUIWorld, a benchmark of six tasks in three matched pairs organized by the evidence needed for control: $I_0$ uses prior knowledge and available observations, $I_1$ requires interaction that directly reveals hidden semantics, and $I_2$ identifies dynamics from action-response relationships. Frontier models struggle especially on $I_2$ tasks. We introduce MOVE, which separates movement from button events and exposes intermediate visual feedback, together with demonstrations of iterative exploration and control. Ablations show that both action granularity and multi-step demonstrations improve performance. After SFT, LatentLearner-9B achieves 50.0% overall success on LatentGUIWorld, comparable to several frontier models. Joint RL further raises egocentric Drag and Ten-Choice success to 92.0% and 75.3%. Behavioral analysis reveals multi-step exploration. In egocentric Drag, RL increases Pearson correlation between error-normalized commands and ideal gain compensation from 0.610 to 0.803. Together, these behaviors show that models learn to explore through interaction and adapt their control to environment dynamics. The same format improves GUI grounding after RL, reaching 67.37% mean accuracy across five benchmarks versus 66.72% for conventional RL.

title: Optical Signatures of a Black Hole in Effective Quantum Gravity
abstract: In this article, we present an investigation of observational signatures of a black hole (BH) in effective quantum gravity (EQG), particularly gravitational weak lensing and shadow analyses with the assumption that the BH is surrounded by uniform and non-uniform plasma. First, we review the spacetime by comparing it with well-known BH spacetimes such as Schwarzschild and Reissner--Nordström BHs. Subsequently, we explore the effect of the uniform and non-uniform plasma on the BH shadow. The results indicate that shadow radii decrease under the influence of the BH charge and both uniform and non-uniform plasma parameters. In addition, we obtain theoretical constraints on the spacetime parameters using observational data from the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) collaboration. Finally, we study gravitational weak lensing around the BH in EQG surrounded by uniform and non-uniform plasma. It was found that increasing the uniform plasma frequency leads to a rise in the deflection angle and vice versa for the non-uniform plasma.

title: Lost in Contrast: Instruction-Preserving Decoding for Reliable Visual Question Answering
abstract: Visual contrastive decoding corrects answers using the prediction difference between the original image and a reference condition, yet the same contrast also turns supported abstentions into incorrect answers. We find that abstentions are lost at two stages: contrastive decoding with candidate filtering can exclude the abstention token before any comparison takes place, and the reference branch's response to the abstention instruction is removed when the reference prediction is subtracted. We therefore propose instruction-preserving decoding, which keeps the effect of the abstention instruction on the original-image prediction intact while leaving the contrast strength freely adjustable. Using a perturbed image and an image-free prediction as references, we obtain IP-VCD and IP-M3ID. On decision utility (DU), which credits both correct answers and supported abstentions, both methods outperform all compared non-IP baselines on every one of nine models on VizWiz, and IP-VCD also leads on eight of nine models on Food-101. Candidate measurements and paired per-question comparisons show that computing the instruction effect and the visual contrast term separately lets contrastive decoding support both correct answers and supported abstentions.

title: Matrix algebras with orthogonal Cauchy-like transforms and Toeplitz approximation: a negative result
abstract: We consider newly designed matrix algebras associated with Cauchy orthogonal transforms. In this work, we are interested in checking the approximation of Toeplitz matrices using algebras of matrices, where each matrix is diagonalized by a fixed Cauchy orthogonal transform, in the spirit of fast algorithm based on preconditioning. We use the Korovkin theory for checking the Toeplitz approximability. Unfortunately and somehow surprisingly, the Korovkin test is negative, in contrast with the successful test for all the Fourier-like and trigonometric algebras, widely used in the relevant literature. More in detail, for the Cauchy algebras, the Frobenius optimal approximation fails to lead to the desired clustering, as also confirmed by ad hoc numerical experiments. It remains open to understand which kind of structured matrices can be approximated by these new algebras.

title: Universal Varieties for Signatures of Membranes
abstract: Membranes are sufficiently smooth vector-valued functions defined on the unit square, widely used in applications such as interpolation of image data. The signature of a membrane is a collection of nonlinear features that capture its essential geometry. We index these features in the graded Hopf algebra of two-parameter shuffle products and study the algebraic varieties for each graded component. At each truncation level, we obtain the dimension of this variety via a novel Witt-type formula. We propose a Chen-Chow theorem for membranes, provably at the second truncation level, and conjecturally for higher levels with extensive computational evidence in the computer algebra system OSCAR.

title: Trace-to-Architecture: Capability Bottleneck Diagnosis for Harness Revision
abstract: Improving an LLM agent requires knowing what to change when it fails. Similar failures can require different fixes, and resolving one problem can expose another. We introduce Trace-to-Architecture (T2A), a framework that uses execution trajectories to determine what to change in an agent's harness and when those changes apply. A development agent diagnoses failures using execution evidence from successful and failed tasks, revises the corresponding harness components, and then checks whether target tasks improve, selected successful tasks remain successful, and the edits are actually triggered. New execution evidence guides subsequent diagnosis and revision. Across ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and AppWorld, T2A achieves the highest aggregate score for all three evaluated task agents, exceeding their respective strongest baselines by 6.2--30.3 points. We also integrate T2A's diagnosis and validation procedures into Meta-Harness, improving the resulting harnesses' mean ScienceWorld score by 21.6 points from the same starting harness.

title: Bounding MrP: Subnational public opinion estimation without detailed census data
abstract: Multilevel regression with post-stratification (MrP) is the dominant method for estimating public opinion in subnational units. The method requires the full joint distribution of demographic variables in a subnational unit, which is often unavailable from public census tabulations. Existing approaches fill this gap by imposing assumptions to combine marginal distributions of census variables into a synthetic joint distribution. We propose sharp MrP bounds instead: the smallest interval containing all estimates of subnational public opinion consistent with the marginal distributions alone. The bounds solve a pair of linear programs and are computationally feasible for typical applications in political science. Applied to two prominent examples in the literature, the bounds are tight enough to be informative and often more accurate than MrP restricted to a coarser, observed joint distribution of census variables. The bounds serve as margin-consistent interval estimates and a diagnostic when researchers use a synthetic joint distribution to construct MrP estimates.

title: MMP for smooth co-rank one foliations
abstract: We prove the existence of minimal models for smooth co-rank one foliations of general type.

title: Finite-event modulation transfer through forward-scattering media
abstract: How spatial structure is transferred through a forward-scattering medium depends jointly on pattern scale and propagation distance. Starting from photon exit displacements, we derive modulation transfer while retaining the number, depths, and projected angles of individual deflections, with event occurrences described by a homogeneous Poisson process along the propagation path. The second angular moment yields a leading low-frequency loss proportional to $k^2z^3$, where $k$ is angular spatial frequency and $z$ is thickness. At finite frequency, the model predicts two coupled departures: loss bends below its low-frequency quadratic extrapolation at fixed thickness, and transfer curves separate by thickness at fixed $k^2z^3$. The leading corrections to both effects arise from the same fourth angular moment. For symmetric, nondegenerate projected-angle distributions, the full response further establishes increasing loss with thickness in the same medium at fixed joint variable. Binary-pattern measurements through TiO$_2$ suspensions span five nominal loadings, seven thicknesses, and 20 spatial frequencies, supporting the approximate low-frequency scaling and showing both departures. A Gaussian effective-angle response calibrated only on lower-frequency data predicts the held-out higher-frequency band without refitting, with a logarithmic root-mean-square error of 0.0181 compared with 0.1021 for quadratic extrapolation. The results show that finite-event statistics provide a common physical origin for spectral bending and thickness-dependent departure from low-frequency scaling, linking coarse-pattern transport to finer spatial structure.

title: Quantifying Precision in Measurement of Individualized, Evidence-Based Learning Across Sessions in Applied Behavior Analysis Therapy
abstract: Current performance criteria used in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) are often based on whether a learner meets a predetermined benchmark e.g., 8 out of 10 correct responses across several sessions. Although these criteria help practitioners make instructional decisions, they provide limited information about how likely it is that the learner has truly acquired the skill. In this paper, we introduce a Bayesian approach that combines practitioners' prior expectations with the learner's ongoing performance data to estimate the learner's future performance level. Rather than providing only a pass or fail decision based on the criteria, we add an element of precision around that criteria to make decisions more nuanced to the testing conditions used. We also developed an R Shiny application for Measurement of Individualized, Evidence-Based Learning (MIEBL) that allows practitioners to apply this method in practice, supporting more informed instructional decisions and providing insight into the strengths and limitations of commonly used mastery criteria.

title: Queue-Aware Token Communications: Bridging AI Representation and Wireless Service
abstract: The rapid advancement of foundation models and edge intelligence is transforming wireless networks from data-oriented communication systems into artificial intelligence (AI)-native service platforms. Token communications (TokenCom) has emerged as a promising paradigm that directly transmits task-oriented AI representations. However, existing studies typically assume that generated tokens can be transmitted immediately, overlooking the queueing dynamics arising from the mismatch between token workload generation and time-varying wireless service capability. To address this limitation, we introduce Queue-Aware TokenCom, which explicitly incorporates token queues into the AI service pipeline. We present an end-to-end architecture integrating AI representation generation, token workload management, wireless transmission, and downstream task inference. We then discuss two key design directions: budget-aware token representation optimization and queue-aware token service optimization, with the token budget serving as a critical interface between AI performance and communication efficiency. Moreover, we investigate fixed and adaptive token budget strategies to characterize the fundamental tradeoff between AI performance and communication efficiency in dynamic wireless environments. Finally, we outline research directions toward closed-loop, task-aware, and scalable TokenCom systems.

title: On Intersection of Character Varieties Associated to Dehn Fillings of the Whitehead Link and Its Generalization
abstract: The canonical component of the character variety of a hyperbolic 2-bridge link complement M is an algebraic surface, from the work of Thurston. If we fix a boundary component T of M and perform a Dehn-filling on T, we get a 1-cusped manifold whose character variety is commonly a generalized curve that is naturally embedded in the character variety of M. If we perform distinct Dehn-fillings on M, we get various generalized curves on the canonical surface. In this paper, we analyze how these curves intersect with each other in the surface and study the topological implications for these intersection points. We also classify the intersection points that correspond to reducible characters, using the twisted Alexander polynomials associated to the Dehn-fillings. Throughout the paper, we use the Whitehead link as a motivating example to illustrate our core methodology, while some generalizations to other 2-bridge links will also be discussed.

title: GROMM: Generative Risk-neutral Option Market Models
abstract: We present a statically and dynamically arbitrage-free European option market model with smooth interpolation between option prices, based on the SANOS framework, and prove that its dynamics admit a unique strong solution. In spirit, it is a stochastic model for local volatility when the latter is used as a representation of a European option price surface, not as a pricing model. We illustrate the strength of our approach on S&P Index Option data from January 2022 to August 2025. We show that the model's initial state fits within bid/ask for more than 95% of relevant market option prices. We then train the model dynamics under $\mathbb{P}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$ and show that the model is indeed free of arbitrage while fitting the dynamics of the market well. We also propose a range of BHW-tests to test for absence of arbitrage.

title: TheoPhysEval: Assessing AI agents at autonomous theoretical physics problem solving
abstract: We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. Without AI assistance, a typical problem in our collection could be solved by a world expert in about a day or less but would take considerably longer for experts in adjacent specialties. We test the ability of off-the-shelf AI agents to tackle these problems autonomously, without human hints. When given access to tools available in a realistic setting, including the ability to search the literature and write scripts for numerical and symbolic work, the best-performing agent, GPT-6-Astra harnessed in Codex, obtains the final answers with a near-perfect accuracy of 98% at an average cost under USD 3 per problem. On average, agents show only small changes in accuracy when denied web search and access to background research papers, suggesting significant memorization of the literature. These results suggest that state-of-the-art agents can accurately perform concrete calculations required across theoretical physics research. We comment on the broader implications of these findings and discuss possible explanations for the current lack of agent-led breakthroughs in theoretical physics despite their outstanding problem-solving abilities.

title: PathPilot: An Adaptive Question-Conditioned Multi-Magnification Navigation Agent for Whole-Slide Image Analysis
abstract: The diagnostic capability of WSI agents relies on effective slide navigation to identify diagnostically relevant regions and efficiently integrate evidence across the slide. While in clinical practice, pathologists dynamically examine slides across multiple scales, integrating global and cellular evidence in a sequential manner, existing AI navigation approaches mostly operate at a single fixed magnification or rely on predefined magnification traversal. This mismatch prevents existing methods from modeling cross-magnification interactions and adaptive magnification selection inherent to real diagnostic workflows. We propose PathPilot, a clinically consistent multi-magnification WSI navigation agent that explicitly models cross-magnification localization and evidence-adaptive exploration. Specifically, we introduce a CrossMagLoc that learns magnification-specific diagnostic localization from pathologist viewing behavior and integrates information from adjacent magnifications to identify the diagnostically most relevant region within the current ROI, thereby providing a diagnostically informed starting point for subsequent question-conditioned exploration. We further introduce an EviRegionSearch that starts question-conditioned exploration from this region, progressively accumulating question-relevant evidence and adaptively determining the next navigation action according to the remaining evidence requirement. Their iterative interaction enables PathPilot to sequentially explore across ROIs and magnifications until sufficient evidence is acquired. Extensive QA evaluations across five cohorts demonstrate consistent superiority over competing SOTA methods on inter/external cohorts, respectively, validating question-conditioned evidence acquisition across regions and magnifications that mirrors the sequential, knowledge-driven navigation of pathologists.

title: VAttnPO: Visual Attention-Guided Policy Optimization
abstract: Multimodal reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards commonly assigns one sequence advantage to an entire response. This outcome-level signal distinguishes overall response quality but leaves changes in visual-evidence use across generated tokens implicit. We introduce VAttnPO (Visual Attention-Guided Policy Optimization), which uses answer-conditioned visual attention to refine token-level credit while preserving the verifier-derived trajectory-mean advantage. A frozen old policy constructs a visual reference by teacher forcing the known correct answer and produces a visual distribution for each rollout token. VAttnPO measures their agreement in visual-attention space using Jensen--Shannon divergence, rather than reading guidance from teacher output-token distributions or introducing an attention-matching objective. Trajectory centering, relative-position weighting, and credit balancing turn this agreement into a zero-mean, position-aware correction to the GRPO sequence advantage. Token intervention, visual-index permutation, and trajectory analysis provide diagnostic evidence linking this signal to model behavior, visual correspondence, and generation position. On Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, VAttnPO raises six-task image AVE from 70.97 with GRPO to 73.50 and scores higher on every reported structured, video, and MME metric. Gains over GRPO also hold on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and InternVL3-8B-Instruct.

title: Amortised adaptive importance sampling
abstract: Monte Carlo sampling algorithms aim to produce samples from a target distribution with a given unnormalised probability density function. The high cost of running Monte Carlo algorithms, with many simulation steps or particles needed to obtain a good empirical approximation to the target, can be reduced by introducing learnable components into the sampler -- a form of amortisation. Once these components are trained, amortised samplers can produce high-quality samples with less computation at sampling time than training-free algorithms would require. We propose an amortised sampler built upon the framework of adaptive importance sampling -- a hierarchical importance sampling procedure where the proposal is iteratively adapted. Our amortised adaptive importance sampling algorithm fits a lightweight neural network that adapts the proposal using information obtained over the course of sampling. By training our sampler over many different targets taken from the same family of distributions, we obtain a sampler that can adapt to a specific target at sampling time without a priori access to the target's parameters. We show that our procedure can efficiently sample from targets within the family the sampler was trained on, giving improvements over target-specific amortised samplers and training-free adaptive importance sampling algorithms. We also explore the potential for generalisation, where the trained sampler is used to sample from targets outwith its training family.

title: CopyQuad: Quadrupedal Skill Transfer from a Single Side-View Video Without a Depth Model
abstract: Video-to-robot pipelines for quadrupedal imitation insert a learned lifting stage, either a monocular depth model or a per-clip 3D reconstruction, to recover the one axis a side-view camera cannot see. We present CopyQuad, which omits that stage and pins the missing axis to the robot's own stance width instead. The setting is side-view footage of sagittally dominated motion, where limb motion is almost entirely in the image plane. A frozen 2D keypoint detector and a fixed analytic retargeting then turn a single uncalibrated clip into a robot reference whose foot targets are reachable by construction, so no per-clip trajectory optimization is needed. One phase-indexed reward structure, whose only per-behavior freedom is three scalars from a shared sweep, learns a dog walk, a horse walk, a horse trot and two non-periodic gestures, all deployed zero-shot on hardware. We then measure what omitting the axis costs. In a training-free rigidity test, a video depth model varies the distance between the animal's hips by $40$ to $107\%$ of its own mean and a single-image metric model by $22$ to $58\%$, though that distance cannot move. Motion capture puts the true lateral paw travel of a dog walk at $4.5$ cm peak to peak, a mean deviation near $1.4$ cm against the $3.5$ cm of lateral foot error our policies already leave, so the discarded axis sits below the pipeline's resolution. Depth repaired to feasibility never beats the constant, and the unrepaired estimates put the robot on the ground.

title: Emergent Spinorial Structure in Mesoscopic Irreversible Thermodynamics
abstract: We reconstruct a geometry of thermodynamic coordinates from transport coefficients within a mesoscopic canonical model. Self-adjoint flux observables determine a compatible evolution generator containing symmetric and antisymmetric transport coefficients. When the Hermitian transport tensor is positive, an exact graded first-order factorization reproduces this generator on its scalar sector. Its commutators define a spectral distance whose metric depends only on the symmetric tensor. Gradients of the antisymmetric tensor can change the evolution while leaving the metric unchanged. The construction allows coordinate-dependent coefficients. In the constant Onsager regime, a Clifford representation gives the same distance and an algebra fixed by the transport matrix. Published transport data for a $\mathrm{Bi_2Te_3}$ film give a principal-distance ratio of approximately $2.12$ in normalized coordinates at $ZT\simeq0.68$. We also examine a separate quadratic entropy-production observable and distinguish its discrete spectrum from the spectrum of the evolution generator. The spinorial representation adds no physical spin degrees of freedom.

title: Impact of shear and dilational membrane viscosities on capsule shape and dynamics under shear flow: a theoretical study
abstract: In artificial (micro)capsules or cells such as red blood cells for example, the two-dimensional (2D) rheology of the membrane (or the shell) is viscoelastic and not only elastic. The deformation and inclination of such a capsule are theoretically studied under shear and extensional flows. The membrane mechanics is described by the Kelvin-Voigt model: the 2D dissipation with the Boussinesq-Scriven law associated to specific dilational and shear Boussinesq numbers $Bq_d$ and $Bq_d$ respectively while the elastic constitutive law is either Hookean, strain-softening (neoHookean) or strain-hardening (Skalak). The dynamics depends on the elastic capillary number $Ca$, the Poisson ratio (or $C$ in Skalak law), the viscosity ratio $λ$, the nonlinearities included in the constitutive law and both boussinesq numbers. Three dynamics are identified in the limit of weak deformations: a tank-treading motion in the limit of small elastic capillary number with a characteristic time depending on $λ$, $Bq_s$ and $Bq_d$, an oscillation without any elasticity and a damped oscillation leading to a tank-treading motion in the limit of large Boussinesq numbers. In all cases, both shear and dilational 2D dissipations contribute differently leading to non-trivial results. In the case of a Skalak law with $C=1$, $Bq=Bq_s=Bq_d$ and $Bq>>λ$, the deformations in the limits $Ca<<1$, $Bq=O(1)$ and $Ca=O(1)$, $Bq>>1$ determined in the seminal work of \cite{barthes1985role} are recovered.

title: Revisiting the Bobkov-Chistyakov-Götze theorem on approximately Gaussian marginals
abstract: We study one-dimensional marginals of an isotropic, log-concave probability measure in $\mathbb{R}^n$. We show that the Kolmogorov distance between a typical marginal and the standard Gaussian distribution is at most $C/n$, for a universal constant $C > 0$. This bound is optimal in general, up to the value of the universal constant. It improves the Gaussian approximation bound of Bobkov, Chistyakov and Götze by a logarithmic factor in the log-concave setting.

title: The XMM Cluster Survey: Cross-Calibration of eROSITA and XMM using Dark Energy Survey Y3 Galaxy Clusters
abstract: We present the cross-calibration of the eROSITA and XMM telescopes, using galaxy clusters detected by redMaPPer from the first three years of Dark Energy Survey observations (DESY3RM). We use the X-ray: Generate and Analyse (XGA) Python module to measure eROSITA properties, and validate our methodology using a deep pointed eROSITA CAL-PV observation of A3158, and a sample of 119 clusters from the expanded HIgh FLux Galaxy Cluster Sample (eeHiFLUGCS). Next, we construct a sample of DESY3RM clusters matched to XMM observations analysed by the XMM Cluster Survey (XCS), and to clusters in the first release of the eROSITA All-Sky Survey (eRASS1). This produced a sample of 114 DESY3RM clusters with both XMM and eROSITA detections. Our resulting X-ray temperatures determined from eROSITA were compared to eRASS1 catalogue values, showing consistency between the two analyses. Comparisons between XMM and eROSITA temperatures reveal a systematic offset, with XMM temperatures 28$\pm$7% higher on average. Finally, we fit $L_{\rm X,soft}$-$λ_{\rm RM}$ and $T_{\rm X}$-$λ_{\rm RM}$ scaling relations for both eROSITA and XMM using the same cluster sample, finding minimal differences in the $L_{\rm X,soft}$-$λ_{\rm RM}$ relation but a clear normalisation offset in the $T_{\rm X}$-$λ_{\rm RM}$ relation, particularly for the highest richness systems. This study will enable future work combining eROSITA and XMM observatories for DESY3RM clusters.

title: A census of Dark Energy Survey Year 3 redMaPPer galaxy clusters in a high exposure eROSITA All Sky Survey region
abstract: We present the cross-match of galaxy clusters detected by redMaPPer using the first three years of Dark Energy Survey (DESY3RM) operations, and the first release of the eROSITA-All Sky Survey (eRASS1) taken by eROSITA on board the Spectrum Roentgen Gamma telescope. We define a sky region ($60^{\circ}<{\rm R.A.}<90^{\circ}$ and $-58^{\circ}<{\rm Dec}<-48^{\circ}$) whereby the mean eRASS1 exposure time of clusters falling within this footprint is $\sim$2.5 times longer than the mean exposure time of the full eRASS1--DESY3RM overlap. Limiting to a redshift range $0.2 < z < 0.65$ and redMaPPer estimated richnesses to $>$50, we obtain a sample of 57 clusters. We match these clusters to the cluster catalogue constructed for the eRASS1, finding 45 clusters with a match and 12 with no match in the catalogue. X-ray properties of the 12 unmatched clusters are estimated via a forced photometry analysis. We investigate the form of the luminosity-richness relation, finding the relation using the full 57 cluster sample is statistically consistent with using only the 45 matched clusters, and will require the deeper data of future eRASS releases (or dedicated X-ray follow-up) to explore further potential differences. Using external data from XMM, ACT and SPT, we find detections of 5 of the 12 unmatched clusters, indicating the presence of virialised gas. Finally, we found the 12 unmatched clusters occupy a higher redshift range and lower richness range (compared to the matched clusters), and find no evidence for an underlying physical reason for the lack of X-ray emission.

title: Essential factors for surface homeomorphisms
abstract: Let $f$ be a homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus at least one that is isotopic to a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism, possibly relative to a finite invariant set. We construct an intrinsic monotone factor by collapsing the maximal continua whose iterates have uniformly bounded diameter in the universal cover. The quotient is homeomorphic to the original surface and the factor is isotopic to $f$ and has several strongly chaotic dynamical features. It is infinitely continuum-wise expansive, tight, and topologically mixing, and it has a dense family of rotational horseshoes, dense periodic points, and a single topological homoclinic class. The factor can be taken as an area-preserving homeomorphism. The quotient preserves stable translation length on the fine curve graph and the applicable homological rotation sets. When $f$ is $C^\infty$, a companion paper gives a unique measure of maximal entropy for the factor; it has full support and is Bernoulli.

title: FoveaTree: Information-Density Trees for Query-Guided Visual Token Pruning in Video Large Language Models
abstract: Video large language models (Video LLMs) encode each frame into hundreds of visual tokens, making video inference expensive. Existing methods reduce this cost through similarity-based merging or attention-based selection but face two challenges: Hierarchy-blind Pruning, which overlooks regional compressibility and can discard critical evidence, and Attention Drift, where positional effects and attention sinks shift text-to-vision attention away from task relevance. We propose FoveaTree, a two-stage, training-free visual-token pruning framework. First, Merge-Gain Density Estimation measures the feature distortion caused by regional merging and constructs a quadtree-derived density map to guide token dropping, merging, and retention. Second, Attention Tree Pruning uses the surviving units and inherited tree topology to refine text-to-vision attention in intermediate LLM layers, preserving relevant regional evidence while removing low-relevance content. We evaluate FoveaTree on InternVL3.5-8B and Qwen3-VL-8B across five video question-answering benchmarks and one captioning benchmark at 50%, 30%, and 10% visual-token retention. FoveaTree consistently achieves overall state-of-the-art performance across the evaluated settings, offering a strong accuracy-efficiency trade-off.

title: Before Attention Sinks Form: Hidden-State Geometry Reveals and Modulates Their Formation
abstract: Attention sinks are usually studied after they have formed. We ask whether a measurable hidden-state change appears beforehand and whether changing that geometry alters what happens later. To remove network depth as a shortcut, we compare prompts in the same model and at the same layer. When sink timing varies across prompts, simple spectral summaries of the hidden states add information beyond current attention, with the clearest prompt-specific signal in a short window about two to three layers before sink formation. The predictive strength varies across cohorts, so we treat the spectrum as a readout of a pre-sink state change rather than a universal warning statistic. The signal is broader than one measured extreme activation. We then modify only the singular values of the post-layer hidden states after current attention has already been computed. These interventions change later sink behavior in Qwen2.5, GLM-Z1, and GPT-OSS relative to norm-matched random spectral perturbations. In Qwen2.5, the immediate suppressive effect is accompanied by a reduction in next-layer query--key preference for position~0, and the learned spectral directions remain stable when estimated from substantially less training data.
